  **b.** to renounce, forsake
s: Middle voice from [G575](G575) and [G5021](G5021); literally to *say* *adieu* (by departing or dismissing); figuratively to *renounce:* - bid farewell, forsake, take leave, send away.

d:
**1.** to perfect, to bring quite to an end
**2.** accomplish
s: From [G575](G575) and [G5055](G5055); to *complete* *entirely*, that is, *consummate:* - finish.

d: **1.** to put off or aside or away
s: From [G575](G575) and [G5087](G5087); to *put* *away* (literally or figuratively): - cast off, lay apart (aside, down), put away (off).

d: **1.** to shake off
s: From [G575](G575) and τινάσσω tinassō (to *jostle*); to *brush* *off:* - shake off.

d: **1.** to pay off, repay
s: From [G575](G575) and [G5099](G5099); to *pay* in full: - repay.

d: **1.** to assume boldness, make bold
s: From [G575](G575) and [G5111](G5111); to *venture* plainly: - be very bold.

d: **1.** severity, roughness, rigour
s: From the base of [G664](G664); (figuratively) *decisiveness*, that is, *rigor:* - severity.

d:
**1.** abruptly, precipitously
**2.** sharply, severely, curtly
s: Adverb from a derivative of a compound of [G575](G575) and τέμνω temnō (to *cut*); *abruptly*, that is, *peremptorily:* - sharply (-ness).
o: from a derivative of a comparative of [G575](G575) and temno (to cut)

d:
**1.** to turn one’s self away from
**2.** to shun, avoid
s: From [G575](G575) and the base of [G5157](G5157); to *deflect*, that is, (reflexively) *avoid:* - turn away.

d: **1.** absence
s: From the participle of [G548](G548); a *being* *away:* - absence.

d: **1.** to carry off or bring away
s: From [G575](G575) and [G5342](G5342); to *bear* *off* (literally or relatively): - bring, carry (away).

d: **1.** to flee from, escape
s: From [G575](G575) and [G5343](G5343); (figuratively) to *escape:* - escape.

d:
**1.** to speak out, speak forth, pronounce
  **a.** not a word of everyday speech but one belonging to dignified and elevated discourse
s: From [G575](G575) and [G5350](G5350); to *enunciate* *plainly*, that is, *declare:* - say, speak forth, utterance.

d:
**1.** to lay down a load, unlade, discharge
  **a.** of sailors lightening ship during a storm to avoid shipwreck
s: From [G575](G575) and the middle voice of [G5412](G5412); to *unload:* - unlade.
o: from [G575](G575) and the middle voice of [G5412](G5412)

d: **1.** abuse, misuse
s: From a compound of [G575](G575) and [G5530](G5530); the act of *using* *up*, that is, *consumption:* - using.

d: **1.** to go away, depart
s: From [G575](G575) and [G5562](G5562); to *go* *away:* - depart.

d:
**1.** to separate, sever
**2.** to part asunder
**3.** to separate one’s self, depart from
s: From [G575](G575) and [G5563](G5563); to *rend* *apart*; reflexively to *separate:* - depart (asunder).

d:
**1.** to breathe out life, expire
**2.** to faint or swoon away
s: From [G575](G575) and [G5594](G5594); to *breathe* *out*, that is, *faint:* - hearts failing.

d:
Appius = the market place of Appius
**1.** a town in Italy, 39 miles (60 km) from Rome on the Appian way
s: Of Latin origin; (in the genitive, that is, possessive case) *of* *Appius*, the name of a Roman: - Appii.

d: **1.** unapproachable, inaccessible
s: From [G1](G1) (as a negative particle) and a derivative of a compound of [G4314](G4314) and εἶμι eimi (to *go*); *inaccessible:* - which no man can approach.
o: from [G1](G1) (as a negative particle) and a derivative of a comparative of [G4314](G4314) and eimi (to go)

d:
**1.** having nothing to strike against, not causing to stumble
  **a.** of a smooth road
  **b.** metaph. of not leading others to sin by one’s mode of life
**2.** not striking against or stumbling
  **a.** metaph. not led into sin, blameless
**3.** without offense, not troubled by a consciousness of sin
s: From [G1](G1) (as a negative particle) and a presumed derivative of [G4350](G4350); actively *inoffensive*, that is, *not* *leading* *into* *sin*; passively *faultless*, that is, *not* *led* *into* *sin:* - none (void of, without) offence.
o: from [G1](G1) (as a negative particle) and a presumed derivative of [G4350](G4350)

d: **1.** without respect of persons, impartial
s: Adverb from a compound of [G1](G1) (as a negative particle) and a presumed derivative of a presumed compound of [G4383](G4383) and [G2983](G2983) (compare [G4381](G4381)); in a way *not* *accepting* the *person*, that is, *impartially:* - without respect of persons.
o: from a compound of [G1](G1) (as a negative particle) and a presumed derivative of a presumed compound of [G4383](G4383) and [G2983](G2983) \[cf [G4381](G4381)\]

d: **1.** not stumbling, standing firm, exempt from falling
s: From [G1](G1) (as a negative particle) and a derivative of [G4417](G4417); *not* *stumbling*, that is, (figuratively) *without* *sin:* - from falling.
o: from [G1](G1) (as a negative particle) and a derivative of [G4417](G4417)

d:
**1.** to fasten one’s self to, adhere to, cling to
  **a.** to touch
  **b.** of carnal intercourse with a women or cohabitation
  **c.** of levitical practice of having no fellowship with heathen practices. Things not to be touched appear to be both women and certain kinds of food, so celibacy and abstinence of certain kinds of food and drink are recommended.
  **d.** to touch, assail anyone
s: Reflexive of [G681](G681); properly to *attach* oneself to, that is, to *touch* (in many implied relations): - touch.

d:
**1.** to fasten to, adhere to
  **a.** to fasten fire to a thing, kindle, set of fire
s: A primary verb; properly to *fasten* to, that is, (specifically) to *set* on fire: - kindle, light.

d:
Apphia = fruitful
**1.** a Christian member of Philemon’s household
s: Probably of foreign origin; *Apphia*, a woman of Colossae: - Apphia.

d:
**1.** to thrust away, push away, repel
**2.** to thrust away from one’s self, to drive away from one’s self
  **a.** repudiate, reject, refuse
s: From [G575](G575) and the middle voice of ὠθέω ōtheō or ὤθω ōthō (to *shove*); to *push* *off*, figuratively to *reject:* - cast away, put away (from), thrust way (from).
o: from [G575](G575) and the middle voice of otheo or otho (to shove)

d:
**1.** destroying, utter destruction
  **a.** of vessels
**2.** a perishing, ruin, destruction
  **a.** of money
  **b.** the destruction which consists of eternal misery in hell
s: From a presumed derivative of [G622](G622); *ruin* or *loss* (physical, spiritual or eternal): - damnable (-nation), destruction, die, perdition, X perish, pernicious ways, waste.

d:
**1.** a prayer, a supplication
**2.** an imprecation, curse, malediction
s: Probably from [G142](G142); properly *prayer* (as *lifted* to Heaven), that is, (by implication) *imprecation:* - curse.

d: **1.** therefore, so then, wherefore
s: Probably from [G142](G142) (through the idea of *drawing* a conclusion); a particle denoting an *inference* more or less decisive (as follows): - haply, (what) manner (of man), no doubt, perhaps, so be, then, therefore, truly, wherefore. Often used in connection with other particles, especially [G1065](G1065) or [G3767](G3767) (after) or [G1487](G1487) (before). Compare also [G687](G687).
o: probably from [G142](G142) (through the idea of drawing a conclusion)

d: **1.** a Greek interrogative particle that implies anxiety or impatience on the part of the questioner
s: A form of [G686](G686), denoting an *interrogation* to which a negative answer is presumed: - therefore.
o: a form of [G686](G686), denoting an interrogation to which a negative answer is presumed

d:
Arabia = desert or barren
**1.** a well known peninsula of Asia lying towards Africa, and bounded by Egypt, Palestine, Syria, mesopotamia, Babylonia, the Gulf of Arabia, the Persian Gulf, the Red Sea and the Indian Ocean
s: Of Hebrew origin \[[H6152](H6152)\]; *Arabia*, a region of Asia: - Arabia.

d:
Aram or Ram = high
**1.** an ancestor of christ
s: Of Hebrew origin \[[H7410](H7410)\]; *Aram* (that is, *Ram*), an Israelite: - Aram.

d: **1.** an Arabian
s: From [G688](G688); an *Arab* or native of Arabia: - Arabian.

d: **1.** to be idle, inactive, to linger, delay
s: From [G692](G692); to *be* *idle*, that is, (figuratively) to *delay:* - linger.

d:
**1.** free from labour, at leisure
**2.** lazy, shunning the labour which one ought to perform
s: From [G1](G1) (as a negative particle) and [G2041](G2041); *inactive*, that is, *unemployed*; (by implication) *lazy*, *useless:* - barren, idle, slow.

d: **1.** of silver, silvery
s: From [G696](G696); made *of* *silver:* - (of) silver.

d:
**1.** silver
**2.** money
**3.** a silver coin, silver piece, a shekel
s: Neuter of a presumed derivative of [G696](G696); *silvery*, that is, (by implication) *cash*; specifically a *silverling* (that is, *drachma* or *shekel*): - money, (piece of) silver (piece).
o: neuter of a presumed derivative of [G696](G696)

d: **1.** a silversmith
s: From [G696](G696) and [G2875](G2875); a *beater* (that is, *worker*) *of* *silver:* - silversmith.

d:
**1.** silver
  **a.** 1Co 3:12 refers to the silver with which the columns of noble buildings were covered and the rafters adorned
  **b.** things made of silver
    **1.** vessels
    **2.** images of Gods
s: From ἀργός argos (*shining*); *silver* (the metal, in the articles or coin): - silver.

d:
Areopagus = martial peak
**1.** a rocky height in the city of Athens, opposite the western end of the Acropolis toward the west.
s: From Ἄρης Arēs (the name of the Greek deity of war) and a derivative of [G4078](G4078); *rock* *of* *Ares*, a place in Athens: - Areopagus, Mars’ Hill.
o: from Ares (the name of the Greek deity of war) and a derivative of [G4078](G4078)

d: **1.** a member of the court of Areopagus, an Areopagite
s: From [G697](G697); an *Areopagite* or member of the court held on Mars’ Hill: - Areopagite.

d: **1.** desire to please
s: From a derivative of [G700](G700); *complaisance:* - pleasing.

d:
**1.** to please
**2.** to strive to please
  **a.** to accommodate one’s self to the opinions desires and interests of others
s: Probably from [G142](G142) (through the idea of *exciting* emotion); to *be* *agreeable* (or by implication to seek to be so): - please.
o: probably from [G142](G142) (through the idea of exciting emotion)

d: **1.** pleasing, agreeable
s: From [G700](G700); *agreeable*; by implication *fit:* - (things that) please (-ing), reason.

d:
Aretes = graver
**1.** An Arabian king
s: Of foreign origin; *Aretas*, an Arabian: - Aretas.

d:
**1.** a virtuous course of thought, feeling and action
  **a.** virtue, moral goodness
**2.** any particular moral excellence, as modesty, purity
s: From the same as [G730](G730); properly *manliness* (*valor*), that is, *excellence* (intrinsic or attributed): - praise, virtue.

d: **1.** a sheep, a lamb
s: Perhaps the same as [G730](G730); a *lamb* (as a *male*): - lamb.

d: **1.** to number
s: From [G706](G706); to *enumerate* or *count:* - number.

d:
**1.** a fixed and definite number
**2.** an indefinite number, a multitude
s: From [G142](G142); a *number* (as reckoned *up*): - number.

d:
Arimathaea = heights
**1.** the name of several cities in Palestine the one mentioned in Mat 27:57, Mar 15:43, Luk 23:51, Joh 19:38 appears to have been the same as the birthplace of Samuel in Mount Ephraim.
s: Of hebrew origin \[[H7414](H7414)\]; *Arimathaea* (or *Ramah*), a place in Palestine: - Arimatha.

d:
Aristarchus = the best ruler
**1.** a certain Christian of thessalonica, and accompanied Paul on his third missionary journey
s: From the same as [G712](G712) and [G757](G757); *best* *ruling*; *Aristarchus*, a Macedonian: - Aristarchus.

d:
**1.** to breakfast
**2.** by later usage, to dine
s: From [G712](G712); to *take* *the* *principal* *meal:* - dine.

d: **1.** left
s: Apparently a compound of the same as [G712](G712); the *left* hand (as *second* *best*): - left \[hand\].
o: apparently a comparative of the same as [G712](G712)

d:
Aristobulus = the best councillor
**1.** a certain Christian
s: From the same as [G712](G712) and [G1012](G1012); *best* *counselling*; *Aristoboulus*, a Christian: - Aristobulus.

d:
**1.** the first food taken early in the morning before work, breakfast
**2.** later usage: dinner
s: Apparent neuter of a superlative from the same as [G730](G730); the *best* meal \[or *breakfast*; perhaps from ἦρι ēri (“early”)\], that is, *luncheon:* - dinner.
o: apparently neuter of a superlative from the same as [G730](G730)

d: **1.** sufficient, enough
s: From [G714](G714); *satisfactory:* - enough, suffice (-ient).

d:
**1.** to be possessed of unfailing strength
  **a.** to be strong, to suffice, to be enough
    **1.** to defend, ward off
  **b.** to be satisfied, to be contented
s: Apparently a primary verb (but probably akin to [G142](G142) through the idea of *raising* a barrier); properly to *ward* *off*, that is, (by implication) to *avail* (figuratively *be* *satisfactory*): - be content, be enough, suffice, be sufficient.
o: apparently a primary word \[but probably akin to [G142](G142) through the idea of raising a barrier\]

d: **1.** a bear
s: Probably from [G714](G714); a *bear* (as *obstructing* by ferocity): - bear.

d:
**1.** a chariot
**2.** of war chariots (i.e. armed with scythes)
**3.** chariots (drawn with many horses)
s: Probably from [G142](G142) (perhaps with [G1](G1) (as a particle of union) prefixed); a *chariot* (as *raised* or fitted *together* (compare [G719](G719))): - chariot.
o: probably from [G1](G1)42>142) \[perhaps with 1 (as a particle of union) prefixed\]

d:
Armageddon = the hill or city of megiddo
**1.** In Rev 16:16 the scene of a the struggle of good and evil is suggested by that battle plain of Esdraelon, which was famous for two great victories, of Barak over the Canaanites, and of Gideon over the Midianites; and for two great disasters, the deaths of Saul and Josiah. Hence in Revelation a place of great slaughter, the scene of a terrible retribution upon the wicked. The RSV translates the name as Har-Magedon, i.e. the hill (as Ar is the city) of megiddo.
s: Of Hebrew origin \[[H2022](H2022)\] and \[[H4023](H4023)\]; *Armageddon* (or *Har-Megiddon*), a symbolical name: - Armageddon.

d:
**1.** to join, to fit together
  **a.** of carpenter’s, fastening together beams and planks to build houses, ships, etc.
**2.** to betroth a daughter to any one
  **a.** to join to one’s self, i.e. to marry the daughter of any one
  **b.** to betroth, to give one in marriage to any one
s: From [G719](G719); to *joint*, that is, (figuratively) to *woo* (reflexively to *betroth*): - espouse.

d: **1.** a joining, a joint
s: From the same as [G716](G716); an *articulation* (of the body): - joint.

d:
**1.** to deny
**2.** to deny someone
  **a.** to deny one’s self
    **1.** to disregard his own interests or to prove false to himself
    **2.** act entirely unlike himself
**3.** to deny, abnegate, abjure
**4.** not to accept, to reject, to refuse something offered
s: Perhaps from [G1](G1) (as a negative particle) and the middle of [G4483](G4483); to *contradict*, that is, *disavow*, *reject*, *abnegate:* - deny, refuse.
o: perhaps from [G1](G1) (as a negative particle) and the middle voice of [G4483](G4483)

d: **1.** a little lamb, a lamb
s: Diminutive from [G704](G704); a *lambkin:* - lamb.

d: **1.** to plough
s: From [G723](G723); to *plough:* - plow.

d: **1.** a plough
s: From ἀρόω aroō (to *till*); a *plough:* - plow.

d:
**1.** the act of plundering, robbery
**2.** plunder spoil
s: From [G726](G726); *pillage* (properly abstract): - extortion, ravening, spoiling.

d:
**1.** the act of seizing, robbery
**2.** a thing seized or to be seized
  **a.** booty to deem anything a prize
  **b.** a thing to be seized upon or to be held fast, retained
s: From [G726](G726); *plunder* (properly concrete): - robbery.

d:
**1.** to seize, carry off by force
**2.** to seize on, claim for one’s self eagerly
**3.** to snatch out or away
s: From a derivative of [G138](G138); to *seize* (in various applications): - catch (away, up), pluck, pull, take (by force).

d:
**1.** rapacious, ravenous
**2.** a extortioner, a robber
s: From [G726](G726); *rapacious:* - extortion, ravening.

d:
**1.** an earnest
  **a.** money which in purchases is given as a pledge or downpayment that the full amount will subsequently be paid
s: Of Hebrew origin \[[H6162](H6162)\]; a *pledge*, that is, part of the purchase money or property given in advance as *security* for the rest: - earnest.

d: **1.** not sewed together, without a seam
s: From [G1](G1) (as a negative particle) and a presumed derivative of the same as [G4476](G4476); *unsewed*, that is, of a single piece: - without seam.
o: from [G1](G1) (as a negative particle) and a presumed derivative of the same as [G4476](G4476)

d: **1.** a male
s: Probably from [G142](G142); *male* (as stronger for *lifting*): - male, man.

d:
**1.** unsaid, unspoken
**2.** unspeakable (on account of its sacredness)
s: From [G1](G1) (as a negative particle) and the same as [G4490](G4490); *unsaid*, that is, (by implication) *inexpressible:* - unspeakable.
o: from [G1](G1) (as a negative particle) and the same as [G4490](G4490)

d: **1.** without strength, weak, sick
s: From [G1](G1) (as a negative particle) and a presumed derivative of [G4517](G4517); *infirm:* - sick (folk, -ly).
o: from [G1](G1) (as a negative particle) and a presumed derivative of [G4517](G4517)

d: **1.** one who lies with a male as with a female, sodomite, homosexual
s: From [G730](G730) and [G2845](G2845); a *sodomite:* - abuser of (that defile) self with mankind.

d:
Artemas = gift of Artemis
**1.** a friend of Paul the apostle
s: Contracted from a compound of [G735](G735) and [G1435](G1435); *gift* *of* *Artemis*; *Artemas* (or *Artemidorus*), a Christian: - Artemas.
o: contracted from a compound of [G735](G735) and [G1435](G1435)

d: Diana = complete light: flow restrained
s: Probably from the same as [G736](G736); *prompt*; *Artemis*, the name of a Grecian goddess borrowed by the Asiatics for one of their deities: - Diana.

d: **1.** a top-sail or foresail of a ship
s: From a derivative of [G737](G737); properly something *ready* (or else more remotely from [G142](G142) (compare [G740](G740)); something *hung* up), that is, (specifically) the *topsail* (rather *foresail* or *jib*) of a vessel: - mainsail.

d:
**1.** just now, this moment
**2.** now at this time, at this very time, this moment
s: Adverb from a derivative of [G142](G142) (compare [G740](G740)) through the idea of *suspension*; just *now:* - this day (hour), hence \[-forth\], here \[-after\], hither \[-to\], (even) now, (this) present.
o: from a derivative of [G142](G142) (cf [G740](G740)) through the idea of suspension

d: **1.** just born, newborn
s: From [G737](G737) and [G1084](G1084); *just* *born*, that is, (figuratively) a *young* *convert:* - new born.

d:
**1.** fitted
**2.** complete, perfect
  **a.** having reference apparently to special aptitude for given uses
s: From [G737](G737); *fresh*, that is, (by implication) *complete:* - perfect.

d:
**1.** food composed of flour mixed with water and baked
  **a.** the Israelites made it in the form of an oblong or round cake, as thick as one’s thumb, and as large as a plate or platter hence it was not to be cut but broken
  **b.** loaves were consecrated to the Lord
  **c.** of the bread used at the love-feasts and at the Lord’s Table
**2.** food of any kind
s: From [G142](G142); *bread* (as *raised*) or a *loaf:* - (shew-) bread, loaf.

d:
**1.** to prepare, arrange, with respect to food
**2.** to season, make savory
s: From a presumed derivative of [G142](G142); to *prepare*, that is, *spice* (with *stimulating* condiments): - season.

d:
Arphaxad = stronghold of Chaldees
**1.** the son of Shem and ancestor of Eber
s: Of Hebrew origin \[[H775](H775)\]; *Arphaxad*, a post diluvian patriarch: - Arphaxad.

d: **1.** archangel, or chief of the angels
s: From [G757](G757) and [G32](G32); a *chief* *angel:* - archangel.

d:
**1.** that has been from the beginning, original, primal, old ancient
  **a.** of men, things, times, conditions
s: From [G746](G746); *original* or *primeval:* - (them of) old (time).

d:
Archelaus = prince of the people
**1.** A son of herod the great by Malthace, the Samaritan woman. He and his brother Antipas were brought up with a certain private man in Rome. After the death of his father, he ruled as ethnarch over Judaea, Samaria and Idumaea, (with the exception of the cities of Gaza, Gadara and Hipo). The Jews and the Samaritans having accused him at Rome of tyranny, he was banished by the emperor Augustus to Vienna of the Allobroges and died there.
s: From [G757](G757) and [G2994](G2994); *people* *ruling*; *Archelaus*, a Jewish king: - Archelaus.

d:
**1.** beginning, origin
**2.** the person or thing that commences, the first person or thing in a series, the leader
**3.** that by which anything begins to be, the origin, the active cause
**4.** the extremity of a thing
  **a.** of the corners of a sail
**5.** the first place, principality, rule, magistracy
  **a.** of angels and demons
s: From [G756](G756); (properly abstract) a *commencement*, or (concrete) *chief* (in various applications of order, time, place or rank): - beginning, corner, (at the, the) first (estate), magistrate, power, principality, principle, rule.

d:
**1.** the chief leader, prince
  **a.** of christ
**2.** one that takes the lead in any thing and thus affords an example, a predecessor in a matter, pioneer
**3.** the author
s: From [G746](G746) and [G71](G71); a *chief* *leader:* - author, captain, prince.

d: **1.** high priestly, pontifical
s: From [G746](G746) and a derivative of [G2413](G2413); *high* *priestly:* - of the high-priest.

d: **1.** chief priest, high priest
s: From [G746](G746) and [G2409](G2409); the *high* *priest* (literally of the Jews, typically Christ); by extension a *chief* *priest:* - chief (high) priest, chief of the priests.

d:
**1.** chief shepherd
  **a.** of christ the head of the church
s: From [G746](G746) and [G4166](G4166); a *head* *shepherd:* - chief shepherd.

d:
Archippus = master of the horse
**1.** a certain Christian teacher in Colosse
s: From [G746](G746) and [G2462](G2462); *horse* *ruler*; *Archippus*, a Christian: - Archippus.

d: **1.** ruler of the synagogue. It was his duty to select the readers or teachers in the synagogue, to examine the discourses of the public speakers, and to see that all things were done with decency and in accordance with ancestral usage.
s: From [G746](G746) and [G4864](G4864); *director* *of* the *synagogue* services: - (chief) ruler of the synagogue.

d: **1.** a master builder, an architect, the superintendent in the erection of buildings
s: From [G746](G746) and [G5045](G5045); a *chief* *constructor*, that is, “architect”: - masterbuilder.

d: **1.** a chief of tax collectors, chief publican
s: From [G746](G746) and [G5057](G5057); a *principal* *tax* *gatherer:* - chief among the publicans.

d: **1.** the superintendent of the dining room, a table master.
s: From [G746](G746) and a compound of [G5140](G5140) and [G2827](G2827) (a *dinner* *bed*, because composed of three couches); *director* *of* the *entertainment:* - governor (ruler) of the feast.
o: from [G746](G746) and a compound of [G5140](G5140) and [G2827](G2827) (a dinner-bed, because composed of three couches)

d:
**1.** to be the first to do (anything), to begin
**2.** to be chief, leader, ruler
**3.** to begin, make a beginning
s: Middle voice of [G757](G757) (through the implication of *precedence*); to *commence* (in order of time): - rehearse from the) begin (-ning).
o: middle voice of [G757](G757) (through the implication of precedence)

d: **1.** to be chief, to lead, to rule
s: A primary verb; to be *first* (in political rank or power): - reign (rule) over.

d: **1.** a ruler, commander, chief, leader
s: Present participle of [G757](G757); a *first* (in rank or power): - chief (ruler), magistrate, prince, ruler.

d: **1.** spice, perfume
s: From [G142](G142) (in the sense of *sending* off scent); an *aromatic:* - (sweet) spice.
o: from [G142](G142) (in the sense of sending off scent)

d:
Asa = physician, or cure
**1.** son of Abijah and king of Judah
s: Of Hebrew origin \[[H609](H609)\]; *Asa*, an Israelite: - Asa.

d:
**1.** unshaken, unmoved
**2.** metaph. not liable to overthrow and disorder, firm stable
s: From [G1](G1) (as a negative particle) and a derivative of [G4531](G4531); *unshaken*, that is, (by implication) *immovable* (figuratively): - which cannot be moved, ummovable.
o: from [G1](G1) (as a negative particle) and a derivative of [G4531](G4531)

d:
**1.** unquenched, unquenchable
  **a.** of eternal hell fire to punish the damned
s: From [G1](G1) (as a negative particle) and a derivative of [G4570](G4570); *not* *extinguished*, that is, (by implication) *perpetual:* - not to be quenched, unquenchable.
o: from [G1](G1) (as a negative particle) and a derivative of [G4570](G4570)

d: **1.** want of reverence towards God, impiety, ungodliness
s: From [G765](G765); *impiety*, that is, (by implication) *wickedness:* - ungodly (-liness).

d: **1.** to be ungodly, act impiously
s: From [G765](G765); to *be* (by implication *act*) *impious* or *wicked:* - commit (live, that after should live) ungodly.

d: **1.** destitute of reverential awe towards God, condemning God, impious
s: From [G1](G1) (as a negative particle) and a presumed derivative of [G4576](G4576); *irreverent*, that is, (by extension) *impious* or *wicked:* - ungodly (man).
o: from [G1](G1) (as a negative particle) and a presumed derivative of [G4576](G4576)

d: **1.** unbridled lust, excess, licentiousness, lasciviousness, wantonness, outrageousness, shamelessness, insolence
s: From a compound of [G1](G1) (as a negative particle) and a presumed σελγής selgēs (of uncertain derivation, but apparently meaning *continent*); *licentiousness* (sometimes including other vices): - filthy, lasciviousness, wantonness.
o: from a compound of [G1](G1) (as a negative particle) and a presumed selges (of uncertain derivation, but apparently meaning continent)

d:
**1.** unmarked or unstamped
  **a.** of money
**2.** unknown, of no mark, insignificant, ignoble
s: From [G1](G1) (as a negative particle) and the base of [G4591](G4591); *unmarked*, that is, (figuratively) *ignoble:* - mean.
o: from [G1](G1) (as a negative particle) and the base of [G4591](G4591)

d:
Asher = blessed
**1.** the eighth son of Jacob
s: Of Hebrew origin \[[H836](H836)\]; *Aser* (that is, *Asher*), an Israelite tribe: - Aser.

d:
**1.** want of strength, weakness, infirmity
  **a.** of the body
    **1.** its native weakness and frailty
    **2.** feebleness of health or sickness
  **b.** of the soul
    **1.** want of strength and capacity requisite
  **c.** to understand a thing
  **d.** to do things great and glorious
  **e.** to restrain corrupt desires
  **f.** to bear trials and troubles
s: From [G772](G772); *feebleness* (of body or mind); by implication *malady*; moral *frailty:* - disease, infirmity, sickness, weakness.

d:
**1.** to be weak, feeble, to be without strength, powerless
**2.** to be weak in means, needy, poor
**3.** to be feeble, sick
s: From [G772](G772); to *be* *feeble* (in any sense): - be diseased, impotent folk (man), (be) sick, (be, be made) weak.

d:
**1.** infirmity
  **a.** of error arising from weakness of mind
s: From [G770](G770); a *scruple* of conscience: - infirmity.

d: **1.** weak, infirm, feeble
s: From [G1](G1) (as a negative particle) and the base of [G4599](G4599); *strengthless* (in various applications, literally, or figuratively and morally): - more feeble, impotent, sick, without strength, weak (-er, -ness, thing).
o: from [G1](G1) (as a negative particle) and the base of [G4599](G4599)

d:
Asia = orient
**1.** Asia proper or proconsular Asia embracing mysia, Lydia, Phrygia, and Caria, corresponding closely to Turkey today
s: Of uncertain derivation; *Asia*, that is, *Asia* *Minor*, or (usually) only its western shore: - Asia.

d: **1.** a native of Asia, Asian, Asiatic
s: From [G773](G773); an *Asian* (that is, *Asiatic*) or inhabitant of Asia: - of Asia.

d: **1.** an Asiarch, President of Asia.
s: From [G773](G773) and [G746](G746); an *Asiarch* or president of the public festivities in a city of Asia Minor: - chief of Asia.

d: **1.** abstinence from food (whether voluntary or enforced)
s: From [G777](G777); *fasting* (the state): - abstinence.

d: **1.** fasting, without having eaten
s: From [G1](G1) (as a negative particle) and [G4621](G4621); *without* (taking) *food:* - fasting.

d:
**1.** to form by art, to adorn
**2.** to exercise (one’s) self, take pains, labour, strive
s: Probably from the same as [G4632](G4632); to *elaborate*, that is, (figuratively) *train* (by implication *strive*): - exercise.

d: **1.** a leathern bag or bottle, in which water or wine was kept
s: From the same as [G778](G778); a leathern (or skin) *bag* used as a bottle: - bottle.

d: **1.** with joy, gladness
s: Adverb from a derivative of the base of [G2237](G2237); *with* *pleasure:* - gladly.
o: from a derivative of the base of [G2237](G2237)

d: **1.** unwise, foolish
s: From [G1](G1) (as a negative particle) and [G4680](G4680); *unwise:* - fool.

d:
**1.** to draw to one’s self
  **a.** to salute one, greet, bid welcome, wish well to
  **b.** to receive joyfully, welcome
s: From [G1](G1) (as a particle of union) and a presumed form of [G4685](G4685); to *enfold* in the arms, that is, (by implication) to *salute*, (figuratively) to *welcome:* - embrace, greet, salute, take leave.
o: from [G1](G1) (as a particle of union) and a presumed form of [G4685](G4685)

d: **1.** a salutation, either oral or written
s: From [G782](G782); a *greeting* (in person or by letter): - greeting, salutation.

d:
**1.** spotless
**2.** metaph.
  **a.** free from censure, irreproachable
  **b.** free from vice, unsullied
s: From [G1](G1) (as a negative particle) and [G4695](G4695); *unblemished* (physically or morally): - without spot, unspotted.

d: **1.** an asp, a small and most venomous serpent, the bite of which is fatal unless the bitten part be immediately cut away
s: Of uncertain derivation; a *buckler* (or *round* shield); used of a serpent (as *coiling* itself), probably the “asp”: - asp.

d:
**1.** without a treaty or covenant
  **a.** of things not mutually agreed upon e.g. abstinences from hostilities
**2.** that cannot be persuaded to enter into a covenant, implacable
s: From [G1](G1) (as a negative particle) and a derivative of [G4689](G4689); literally *without* *libation* (which usually accompanied a treaty), that is, (by implication) *truceless:* - implacable, truce-breaker.
o: from [G1](G1) (as a negative particle) and a derivative of [G4689](G4689)

d: **1.** an assarium or assarius, the name of a coin equal to the tenth part of a drachma
s: Of Latin origin; an *assarius* or *as*, a Roman coin: - farthing.

d: **1.** nearer
s: Neuter comparative of the base of [G1451](G1451); *more* *nearly*, that is, *very* *near:* - close.
o: neuter comparative of the base of [G1451](G1451)

d:
Assos = approaching
**1.** a seaport of the Roman province of Asia in the district anciently called mysia, on the north shore of the Gulf of Adramyttium, and about 7 miles (11 km) from Lesbos
s: Probably of foreign origin; *Assus*, a city of Asia Minor: - Assos.

d: **1.** to wander about, to rove without a settled abode
s: From [G1](G1) (as a negative particle) and a derivative of [G2476](G2476); to *be* *non* *stationary*, that is, (figuratively) *homeless:* - have no certain dwelling-place.
o: from [G1](G1) (as a negative particle) and a derivative of [G2476](G2476)

d:
**1.** of the city
**2.** of polished manners
**3.** elegant (of body), comely, fair
s: Fromἄστυ astu (a *city*); *urbane*, that is, (by implication) *handsome:* - fair.

d: **1.** a star
s: Probably from the base of [G4766](G4766); a *star* (as *strown* over the sky), literally or figuratively: - star.

d: **1.** unstable, unsteadfast
s: From [G1](G1) (as a negative particle) and a presumed derivation of [G4741](G4741); *unfixed*, that is, (figuratively) *vacillating:* - unstable.
o: from [G1](G1) (as a negative particle) and a presumed derivative of [G4741](G4741)

d: **1.** without natural affection, unsociable (Rom 1:31 marg.), inhuman (2Ti 3:3 RSV), unloving (2Ti 3:3 NKJV)
s: From [G1](G1) (as a negative particle) and a presumed derivative of στέργω stergō (to *cherish* affectionately); *hard* *hearted* towards kindred: - without natural affection.
o: from [G1](G1) (as a negative particle) and a presumed derivative of stergo (to cherish affectionately)

d: **1.** to deviate from, miss (the mark)
s: From a compound of [G1](G1) (as a negative particle) and στόιχος stoichos (an *aim*); to *miss* the mark, that is, (figuratively) *deviate* from truth: - err, swerve.
o: from a compound of [G1](G1) (as a negative particle) and stoichos (an aim)

d:
**1.** lightning
  **a.** of the gleam of a lamp
s: From [G797](G797); *lightning*; by analogy *glare:* - lightning, bright shining.

d:
**1.** to lighten
  **a.** of dazzling objects
s: Probably from [G792](G792); to *flash* as lightning: - lighten, shine.

d:
**1.** a group of stars, a constellation
**2.** a star
s: Neuter from [G792](G792); properly a *constellation*; put for a single *star* (natural or artificial): - star.

d:
Asyncritus = incomparable
**1.** an unknown Christian at Rome saluted by Paul
s: From [G1](G1) (as a negative particle) and a derivative of [G4793](G4793); *incomparable*; *Asyncritus*, a Christian: - Asyncritus.
o: from [G1](G1) (as a negative particle) and a derivative of [G4793](G4793)

d: **1.** not agreeing in sound, dissonant, inharmonious, at variance
s: From [G1](G1) (as a negative particle) and [G4859](G4859); *inharmonious* (figuratively): - agree not.

d: **1.** unintelligent, without understanding, stupid
s: From [G1](G1) (as a negative particle) and [G4908](G4908); *unintelligent*; by implication *wicked:* - foolish, without understanding.

d:
**1.** uncompounded, simple
**2.** covenant breaking, faithless
s: From [G1](G1) (as a negative particle) and a derivative of [G4934](G4934); properly *not* *agreed*, that is, *treacherous* to compacts: - covenant-breaker
o: from [G1](G1) (as a negative particle) and a derivative of [G4934](G4934)

d:
**1.** firmness, stability
**2.** certainty, undoubted truth
**3.** security from enemies and dangers, safety
s: From [G804](G804); *security* (literally or figuratively): - certainty, safety.

d:
**1.** firm (that which can be relied on)
**2.** certain, true
**3.** suited to confirm
s: From [G1](G1) (as a negative particle) and σφάλλω sphallō (to “fail”); *secure* (literally or figuratively): - certain (-ty), safe, sure.
o: from [G1](G1) (as a negative particle) and sphallo (to fail)

d:
**1.** to make firm, to make secure (against harm)
**2.** to be made secure
s: From [G804](G804); to *render* *secure:* - make fast (sure).

d: **1.** safety (so as to prevent escape), assuredly
s: Adverb from [G804](G804); *securely* (literally or figuratively): - assuredly, safely.

d: **1.** to act unbecomingly
s: From [G809](G809); to *be* (that is, *act*) *unbecoming:* - behave self uncomely (unseemly).

d:
**1.** unseemliness, an unseemly deed
  **a.** of a woman’s genitals
  **b.** of one’s nakedness, shame
s: From [G809](G809); an *indecency*; by implication the *pudenda:* - shame, that which is unseemly.

d:
**1.** deformed
**2.** indecent, unseemly
s: From [G1](G1) (as a negative particle) and a presumed derivative of [G2192](G2192) (in the sense of its congener [G4976](G4976)); properly *shapeless*, that is, (figuratively) *inelegant:* - uncomely.
o: from [G1](G1) (as a negative particle) and a presumed derivative of [G2192](G2192) (in the sense of its congener [G4976](G4976))

d:
**1.** an abandoned, dissolute life
**2.** profligacy, prodigality
s: From a compound of [G1](G1) (as a negative particle) and a presumed derivative of [G4982](G4982); properly *unsavedness*, that is, (by implication) *profligacy:* - excess, riot.
o: from a compound of [G1](G1) (as a negative particle) and a presumed derivative of [G4982](G4982)

d: **1.** dissolutely, profligately
s: Adverb from the same as [G810](G810); *dissolutely:* - riotous.

d:
**1.** to be disorderly
  **a.** of soldiers marching out of order or quitting ranks
  **b.** to be neglectful of duty, to be lawless
  **c.** to lead a disorderly life
s: From [G813](G813); to *be* (that is, *act*) *irregular:* - behave self disorderly.

d:
**1.** disorderly, out of ranks (often so of soldiers)
**2.** irregular, inordinate, immoderate pleasures
**3.** deviating from the prescribed order or rule used in Greek society of those who did not show up for work.
s: From [G1](G1) (as a negative particle) and a derivative of [G5021](G5021); *unarranged*, that is, (by implication) *insubordinate* (religiously): - unruly.
o: from [G1](G1) (as a negative particle) and a derivative of [G5021](G5021)

d:
**1.** disorderly, out of ranks (often so of soldiers)
**2.** irregular, inordinate, immoderate pleasures
**3.** deviating from the prescribed order or rule
s: Adverb from [G813](G813); *irregularly* (morally): - disorderly.

d: **1.** without offspring, childless
s: From [G1](G1) (as a negative particle) and [G5043](G5043); *childless:* - childless, without children.

d:
**1.** to fix the eyes on, gaze upon
**2.** to look into anything
**3.** metaph. to fix one’s mind on one as an example
s: From a compound of [G1](G1) (as a particle of union) and τείνω teinō (to *stretch*); to *gaze* intently: - behold earnestly (stedfastly), fasten (eyes), look (earnestly, stedfastly, up stedfastly), set eyes.
o: from a compound of [G1](G1) (as a particle of union) and teino (to stretch)

d: **1.** without, apart from
s: A particle probably akin to [G427](G427); *aloof*, that is, *apart* from (literally or figuratively): - in the absence of, without.

d:
**1.** to dishonour, insult, treat with contempt
  **a.** whether in word, deed or thought
s: From [G820](G820); to *render* *infamous*, that is, (by implication) *contemn* or *maltreat:* - despise, dishonour, suffer shame, entreat shamefully.

d: **1.** dishonour, ignominy, disgrace
s: From [G820](G820); *infamy*, that is, (subjectively) comparative *indignity*, (objectively) *disgrace:* - dishonour, reproach, shame, vile.

d:
**1.** without honour, unhonoured, dishonoured
**2.** base, of less esteem
s: From [G1](G1) (as a negative particle) and [G5092](G5092); (negatively) *unhonoured* or (positively) *dishonoured*. May show a comparative degree such as *less* *honourable:* - despised, without honour, less honourable \[comparative degree\].

d: **1.** to dishonour, mark with disgrace
s: From [G820](G820); used like [G818](G818), to *maltreat:* - handle shamefully.

d: **1.** vapour
s: From the same as [G109](G109); *mist:* - vapour.

d:
**1.** that cannot be cut in two, or divided, indivisible
  **a.** of a moment of time
s: From [G1](G1) (as a negative particle) and the base of [G5114](G5114); *uncut*, that is, (by implication) *indivisible* (an “atom” of time): - moment.
o: from [G1](G1) (as a negative particle) and the base of [G5114](G5114)

d:
**1.** out of place, not befitting, unbecoming
**2.** improper, wicked
**3.** unrighteous
**4.** inconvenient, harmful
s: From [G1](G1) (as a negative particle) and [G5117](G5117); *out* *of* *place*, that is, (figuratively) *improper*, *injurious*, *wicked:* - amiss, harm, unreasonable.

d:
Attalia = Jah’s due season
**1.** a maritime city of Pamphylia in Asia, very near the borders of Lycia, built and named by Attalus Philadelphus, king of Pergamos, now called Antali
s: From Ἄτταλος Attalos (a king of Pergamus); *Attaleia*, a place in Pamphylia: - Attalia.

d:
**1.** to beam upon, irradiate
**2.** to be bright, to shine forth
s: From [G827](G827); to *beam* forth (figuratively): - shine.

d: **1.** brightness, radiance, daylight
s: Of uncertain derivation; a *ray* of light, that is, (by implication) *radiance*, *dawn:* - break of day.

d:
Augustus = venerable
**1.** the first Roman emperor
**2.** title conferred upon Roman emperors
s: From Latin (“august”); *Augustus*, a title of the Roman emperor: - Augustus.

d: **1.** self-pleasing, self-willed, arrogant
s: From [G846](G846) and the base of [G2237](G2237); *self* *pleasing*, that is, *arrogant:* - self-willed.

d: **1.** voluntary, of free choice, of one’s own accord
s: From [G846](G846) and the same as [G140](G140); *self* *chosen*, that is, (by implication) *voluntary:* - of own accord, willing of self.

d:
**1.** one who with his own hands kills another or himself
**2.** one who acts on his own authority, autocratic
**3.** an absolute master
**4.** to govern, exercise dominion over one
s: From a compound of [G846](G846) and ἕντης hentēs (obsolete; a *worker*); to *act* *of* *oneself*, that is, (figuratively) *dominate:* - usurp authority over.
o: from a compound of [G846](G846) and an obsolete hentes (a worker)

d: **1.** to play on the flute, to pipe
s: From [G836](G836); to play the *flute:* - pipe.

d:
**1.** among the Greeks in Homer’s time, an uncovered space around the house, enclosed by a wall, in which the stables stood, hence among the Orientals that roofless enclosure by a wall, in the open country in which the flocks were herded at night, a sheepfold
**2.** the uncovered courtyard of the house. In the O.T. particularly of the courts of the tabernacle and of the temple in Jerusalem. The dwellings of the higher classes usually had two, one exterior, between the door and the street; the other interior, surrounded by the buildings of the dwelling itself. The latter is mentioned Mat 26:69.
**3.** the house itself, a palace
s: From the same as [G109](G109); a *yard* (as open to the *wind*); by implication a *mansion:* - court, (\[sheep-\]) fold, hall, palace.

d: **1.** a flute player
s: From [G832](G832); a *flute* *player:* - minstrel, piper.

d:
**1.** to lodge in the court-yard, esp. at night
  **a.** of flocks and shepherds
**2.** to pass the night in the open air
**3.** to pass the night, lodge
s: Middle voice from [G833](G833); to *pass* *the* *night* (properly in the open air): - abide, lodge.

d: **1.** a pipe
s: From the same as [G109](G109), a *flute* (as *blown*): - pipe.

d:
**1.** to cause to grow, augment
**2.** to increase, become greater
**3.** to grow, increase
  **a.** of plants
  **b.** of infants
  **c.** of a multitude of people
  **d.** of inward Christian growth
s: A prolonged form of a primary verb; to *grow* (“wax”), that is, *enlarge* (literally or figuratively, actively or passively): - grow (up), (give the) increase.
o: a prolonged form of a primary verb

d: **1.** increase, growth
s: From [G837](G837); *growth:* - increase.

d: **1.** tomorrow
s: From a derivative of the same as [G109](G109) (meaning a *breeze*, that is, the morning *air*); properly *fresh*, that is, (adverbially with ellipsis of [G2250](G2250)) *tomorrow:* - (to-) morrow, next day.
o: from a derivative of the same as [G109](G109) (meaning a breeze, i.e. the morning air)

d: **1.** of mind and manners: harsh, rough, rigid
s: From a (presumed) derivative of the same as [G109](G109) (meaning *blown*); *rough* (properly as a *gale*), that is, (figuratively) *severe:* - austere.
o: from a (presumed) derivative of the same as [G109](G109) (meaning blown)

d:
**1.** a perfect condition of life in which no aid or support is needed
**2.** sufficiency of the necessities of life
**3.** a mind contented with its lot, contentment
s: From [G842](G842); *self* *satisfaction*, that is, (abstractly) *contentedness*, or (concretely) a *competence:* - contentment, sufficiency.

d:
**1.** sufficient for one’s self, strong enough or processing enough to need no aid or support
**2.** independent of external circumstances
**3.** contented with one’s lot, with one’s means, though the slenderest
s: From [G846](G846) and [G714](G714); *self* *complacent*, that is, *contented:* - content.

d: **1.** self-condemned
s: From [G846](G846) and a derivative of [G2632](G2632); *self* *condemned:* - condemned of self.

d:
**1.** moved by one’s own impulse, or acting without the instigation or intervention of another
**2.** often used of the earth producing plants of itself, and of the plants themselves and the fruits growing without culture
s: From [G846](G846) and the same as [G3155](G3155); *self* *moved* (“automatic”), that is, *spontaneous:* - of own accord, of self.

d:
**1.** seeing with one’s own eye, an eye-witness
  **a.** a medical term: autopsy, a detailed examination
s: From [G846](G846) and [G3700](G3700); *self* *seeing*, that is, an *eye* *witness:* - eye-witness.

d:
**1.** himself, herself, themselves, itself
**2.** he, she, it
**3.** the same
s: From the particle αὖ au (perhaps akin to the base of [G109](G109) through the idea of a *baffling* wind; *backward*); the reflexive pronoun *self*, used (alone or in the compound of [G1438](G1438)) of the third person, and (with the proper personal pronoun) of the other persons: - her, it (-self), one, the other, (mine) own, said, (\[self-\], the) same, (\[him-, my-, thy-\]) self, \[your-\] selves, she, that, their (-s), them (\[-selves\]), there \[-at, -by, -in, -into, -of, -on, -with\], they, (these) things, this (man), those, together, very, which. Compare [G848](G848).
o: from the particle au \[perhaps akin to the base of [G109](G109) through the idea of a baffling wind\] (backward)

d: **1.** in that place, there, here
s: Genitive (that is, possessive) of [G846](G846), used as an adverb of location; properly belonging to the *same* spot, that is, *in* *this* (or *that*) *place:* - (t-) here.
o: genitive (i.e. possessive) of [G846](G846), used as an adverb of location

d: **1.** of himself, themself, them
s: Contraction for [G1438](G1438); *self* (in some oblique case or reflexive relation): - her (own), (of) him (-self), his (own), of it, thee, their (own), them (-selves), they.

d: **1.** doing a thing with one’s own hands (Often in the tragedians and Attic orators)
s: From [G846](G846) and [G5495](G5495); *self* *handed*, that is, doing *personally:* - with . . . own hands.

d:
**1.** squalid, dirty
  **a.** since dirty things are destitute of brightness: dark
s: From αὐχμός auchmos (probably from a base akin to that of [G109](G109); *dust*, as *dried* by wind); properly *dirty*, that is, (by implication) *obscure:* - dark.
o: from auchmos \[probably from a base akin to that of [G109](G109)\] (dust, as dried by wind)

d:
**1.** to take from, take away, remove, carry off
**2.** to cut off
s: From [G575](G575) and [G138](G138); to *remove* (literally or figuratively): - cut (smite) off, take away.

d: **1.** not manifest, hidden
s: From [G1](G1) (as a negative particle) and [G5316](G5316); *non* *apparent:* - that is not manifest.

d:
**1.** to snatch out of sight, to put out of view, to make unseen
**2.** to cause to vanish away, to destroy, consume
**3.** to deprive of lustre, render unsightly
  **a.** to disfigure
s: From [G852](G852); to *render* *unapparent*, that is, (actively) *consume* (*becloud*), or (passively) *disappear* (*be* *destroyed*): - corrupt, disfigure, perish, vanish away.

d:
**1.** disappearance
**2.** destruction
s: From [G853](G853); *disappearance*, that is, (figuratively) *abrogation:* - vanish away.

d: **1.** taken out of sight, made invisible
s: From [G1](G1) (as a negative particle) and a derivative of [G5316](G5316); *non* *manifested*, that is, *invisible:* - vanished out of sight.
o: from [G1](G1) (as a negative particle) and a derivative of [G5316](G5316)

d:
**1.** a place where the human waste discharges are dumped
  **a.** a privy, sink, toilet
s: From a compound of [G575](G575) and the base of [G1476](G1476); a place of *sitting* *apart*, that is, a *privy:* - draught.
o: from a compound of [G575](G575) and the base of [G1476](G1476)

d: **1.** unsparingly severity
s: From a compound of [G1](G1) (as a negative particle) and [G5339](G5339); *unsparingness*, that is, *austerity* (*ascetism*): - neglecting.
o: from a compound of [G1](G1) (as a negative particle) and [G5339](G5339)

d: **1.** simplicity, singleness
s: From a compound of [G1](G1) (as a negative particle) and φέλλος phellos (in the sense of a *stone* as *stubbing* the foot); *smoothness*, that is, (figuratively) *simplicity:* - singleness.
o: from a compound of [G1](G1) (as a negative particle) and phellos (in the sense of a stone as stubbing the foot)

d:
**1.** release from bondage or imprisonment
**2.** forgiveness or pardon, of sins (letting them go as if they had never been committed), remission of the penalty
s: From [G863](G863); *freedom*; (figuratively) *pardon:* - deliverance, forgiveness, liberty, remission.

d: **1.** bond, connection
s: From [G680](G680); probably a *ligament* (as *fastening*): - joint.

d:
**1.** incorruption, perpetuity
**2.** purity, sincerity, incorrupt
s: From [G862](G862); *incorruptibility*; generally *unending* *existence*; (figuratively) *genuineness:* - immortality, incorruption, sincerity.

d:
**1.** uncorrupted, not liable to corruption or decay, imperishable
  **a.** of things
**2.** immortal
  **a.** of the risen dead
s: From [G1](G1) (as a negative particle) and a derivative of [G5351](G5351); *undecaying* (in essence or continuance): - not (in-, un-) corruptible, immortal.
o: from [G1](G1) (as a negative particle) and a derivative of [G5351](G5351)

d:
**1.** to send away
  **a.** to bid going away or depart
    **1.** of a husband divorcing his wife
  **b.** to send forth, yield up, to expire
  **c.** to let go, let alone, let be
    **1.** to disregard
    **2.** to leave, not to discuss now, (a topic)
**2.** of teachers, writers and speakers
    **1.** to omit, neglect
  **a.** to let go, give up a debt, forgive, to remit
  **b.** to give up, keep no longer
**3.** to permit, allow, not to hinder, to give up a thing to a person
**4.** to leave, go way from one
  **a.** in order to go to another place
  **b.** to depart from any one
  **c.** to depart from one and leave him to himself so that all mutual claims are abandoned
  **d.** to desert wrongfully
  **e.** to go away leaving something behind
  **f.** to leave one by not taking him as a companion
  **g.** to leave on dying, leave behind one
  **h.** to leave so that what is left may remain, leave remaining
  **i.** abandon, leave destitute
s: From [G575](G575) and ἵημι hiēmi (to *send*; an intensive form of εἶμι eimi (to *go*)); to *send* *forth*, in various applications: - cry, forgive, forsake, lay aside, leave, let (alone, be, go, have), omit, put (send) away, remit, suffer, yield up.
o: from [G575](G575) and hiemi (to send, an intens. form of eimi, to go)

d:
**1.** to come from a place
**2.** to come to, arrive
s: From [G575](G575) and the base of [G2425](G2425); to *go* (that is, *spread*) *forth* (by rumor): - come abroad.

d: **1.** opposed to goodness and good men
s: From [G1](G1) (as a negative particle) and [G5358](G5358); *hostile* *to* *virtue:* - depiser of those that are good.

d: **1.** not loving money, not avaricious
s: From [G1](G1) (as a negative particle) and [G5366](G5366); *unavaricious:* - without covetousness, not greedy of filthy lucre.

d:
**1.** arrival
**2.** departure
s: From [G864](G864); properly *arrival*, that is, (by implication) *departure:* - departing.

d:
**1.** to make stand off, cause to withdraw, to remove
  **a.** to excite to revolt
**2.** to stand off, to stand aloof
  **a.** to go away, to depart from anyone
  **b.** to desert, withdraw from one
  **c.** to fall away, become faithless
  **d.** to shun, flee from
  **e.** to cease to vex one
  **f.** to withdraw one’s self from, to fall away
  **g.** to keep one’s self from, absent one’s self from
s: From [G575](G575) and [G2476](G2476); to *remove*, that is, (actively) *instigate* to revolt; usually (reflexively) to *desist*, *desert*, etc.: - depart, draw (fall) away, refrain, withdraw self.

d: **1.** suddenly
s: Adverb from [G852](G852) (contracted); *unawares*, that is, *unexpectedly:* - suddenly.

d: **1.** without fear, boldly
s: Adveb from a compound of [G1](G1) (as a negative particle) and [G5401](G5401); *fearlessly:* - without fear.
o: from a compound of [G1](G1) (as a negative particle) and [G5401](G5401)

d:
**1.** to cause a model to pass off into an image or shape like it
**2.** to express itself in it, to copy
**3.** to produce a facsimile
**4.** to be made like, render similar
s: From [G575](G575) and [G3666](G3666); to *assimilate* closely: - make like.

d: **1.** to turn the eyes away from other things and fix them on something
s: From [G575](G575) and [G3708](G3708); to *consider* attentively: - look.

d:
**1.** to mark off from others by boundaries, to limit, to separate
  **a.** in a bad sense: to exclude as disreputable
  **b.** in a good sense: to appoint, set apart for some purpose
s: From [G575](G575) and [G3724](G3724); to *set* *off* by boundary, that is, (figuratively) *limit*, *exclude*, *appoint*, etc.: - divide, separate, sever.

d:
**1.** a place from which a movement or attack is made, a base of operations
**2.** metaph. that by which endeavour is excited and from which it goes forth
  **a.** that which gives occasion and supplies matter for an undertaking, the incentive
  **b.** the resources we avail ourselves of in attempting or performing anything
s: From a compound of [G575](G575) and [G3729](G3729); a *starting* point, that is, (figuratively) an *opportunity:* - occasion.

d: **1.** to foam
s: From [G876](G876); to *froth* at the mouth (in epilepsy): - foam.

d: **1.** foam
s: Apparently a primary word; *froth*, that is, *slaver:* - foaming.

d:
**1.** foolishness, folly, senselessness
**2.** thoughtlessness, recklessness
s: From [G878](G878); *senselessness*, that is, (euphemistically) *egotism*; (morally) *recklessness:* - folly, foolishly (-ness).

d:
**1.** without reason
**2.** senseless, foolish, stupid
**3.** without reflection or intelligence, acting rashly
s: From [G1](G1) (as a negative particle) and [G5424](G5424); properly *mindless*, that is, *stupid*, (by implication) *ignorant*, (specifically) *egotistic*, (practically) *rash*, or (morally) *unbelieving:* - fool (-ish), unwise.

d:
**1.** to awaken from sleep
**2.** to fall asleep, to fall off to sleep
s: From a compound of [G575](G575) and [G5258](G5258); properly to *become* *awake*, that is, (by implication) to *drop* (off) in slumber: - fall asleep.

d:
**1.** voiceless, dumb
**2.** without faculty of speech
  **a.** of idols
s: From [G1](G1) (as a negative particle) and [G5456](G5456); *voiceless*, that is, *mute* (by nature or choice); figuratively *unmeaning:* - dumb, without signification.

d:
Ahaz = possessor
**1.** the eleventh king of Judah, son of Jotham
s: Of Hebrew origin \[[H271](H271)\]; *Achaz*, an Israelite: - Achaz.

d:
Achaia = trouble
**1.** in a restricted sense, the maritime region of northern Peloponnesus
**2.** in a broader sense, a Roman province embracing all Greece except thessaly
s: Of uncertain derivation; *Achaia* (that is, *Greece*), a country of Europe: - Achaia.

d:
Achaicus = belonging to Achaia
**1.** the name of a Christian in Corinth
s: From [G882](G882); an *Achaian*; *Achaicus*, a Christian: - Achaicus.

d:
**1.** ungracious
  **a.** unpleasing
  **b.** unthankful
s: From [G1](G1) (as a negative particle) and a presumed derivative of [G5483](G5483); *thankless*, that is, *ungrateful:* - unthankful.
o: from [G1](G1) (as a negative particle) and a presumed derivative of [G5483](G5483)

d:
Achim = the Lord will establish
**1.** one of the ancestors of christ, his name is not mentioned in the OT
s: Probably of Hebrew origin (compare \[[H3137](H3137)\]); *Achim*, an Israelite: - Achim.

d: **1.** not made with hands
s: From [G1](G1) (as a negative particle) and [G5499](G5499); *unmanufactured*, that is, *inartificial:* - made without (not made with) hands.

d: **1.** mist, dimness
s: Of uncertain derivation; *dimness* of sight, that is, (probably) a *cataract:* - mist.

d: **1.** useless, good for nothing
s: From [G1](G1) (as a negative particle) and a derivative of [G5534](G5534) (compare [G5532](G5532)); *useless*, that is, (euphemistically) *unmeritorious:* - unprofitable.
o: from [G1](G1) (as a negative particle) and a derivative of [G5534](G5534) \[cf [G5532](G5532)\]

d:
**1.** make useless, render unserviceable
  **a.** of character
s: From [G888](G888); to *render* *useless*, that is, *spoil:* - become unprofitable.

d: **1.** useless, unprofitable
s: From [G1](G1) (as a negative particle) and [G5543](G5543); *inefficient*, that is, (by implication) *detrimental:* - unprofitable.

d: **1.** until, unto, etc.
s: Akin to [G206](G206) (through the idea of a *terminus*); (of time) *until* or (of place) *up* *to*: - as far as, for, in (-to), till, (even, un-) to, until, while. Compare [G3360](G3360).
o: akin to [G206](G206) (through the idea of a terminus)

d:
**1.** a stalk of grain from which the kernels have been beaten out
**2.** straw broken up by a threshing machine, chaff
s: Perhaps remotely from χέω cheō (to *shed* forth); *chaff* (as *diffusive*): - chaff.
o: perhaps remotely from cheo (to shed forth)

d: **1.** without lie, truthful
s: From [G1](G1) (as a negative particle) and [G5579](G5579); *veracious:* - that cannot lie.

d:
**1.** wormwood
**2.** the name of a star which fell into the waters and made them bitter
s: Of uncertain derivation; *wormwood* (as a type of *bitterness*, that is, \[figuratively\] *calamity*): - wormwood.

d: **1.** without a soul, lifeless
s: From [G1](G1) (as a negative particle) and [G5590](G5590); *lifeless*, that is, *inanimate* (*mechanical*): - without life.

d:
Baal = lord
**1.** the supreme male divinity of the Phoenician and Canaanitish nations, as Ashtoreth was their supreme female divinity
s: Of Hebrew origin \[[H1168](H1168)\]; *Baal*, a Phaenician deity (used as a symbol of idolatry): - Baal.

d:
Babylon = confusion
**1.** a very large and famous city, the residence of the Babylonian kings, situated on both banks of the Euphrates. Cyrus had formerly captured it, but Darius Hystaspis threw down its gates and walls, and Xerxes destroyed the temple of Belis. At length the city was reduced to almost solitude, the population having been drawn off by the neighbouring Seleucia, built on the Tigris by Seleucus Nicanor.
**2.** of the territory of Babylonia
**3.** allegorically, of Rome as the most corrupt seat of idolatry and the enemy of Christianity
s: Of Hebrew origin \[[H894](H894)\]; *Babylon*, the capital of Chaldaea (literally or figuratively as a type of tyranny): - Babylon.

d:
**1.** threshold, step
  **a.** of a grade of dignity and wholesome influence in the church
s: From the same as [G899](G899); a *step*, that is, (figuratively) *grade* (of dignity): - degree.

d:
**1.** depth, height
  **a.** of the deep sea
  **b.** metaph.
    **1.** deep, extreme, poverty
    **2.** of the deep things of God
s: From the same as [G901](G901); *profundity*, that is, (by implication) *extent*; (figuratively) *mystery:* - deep (-ness, things), depth.

d:
**1.** ’the deep’ sea (the ’high seas’)
**2.** deep, extreme poverty, the deep things of God, things hidden and above man’s scrutiny, especially divine counsels
**3.** to make deep
s: From [G901](G901); to *deepen:* - deep.

d: **1.** deep
s: From the base of [G939](G939); *profound* (as *going* down), literally or figuratively: - deep, very early.

d: **1.** a palm branch
s: A diminutive of a derivative probably of the base of [G939](G939); a palm *twig* (as *going* out far): - branch.
o: a diminutive of a derivative probably of the base of [G939](G939)

d:
Balaam meaning perhaps
**1.** A native of Pethor a city in mesopotamia, endued by Jehovah with prophetic power. He was hired by Balak to curse the Israelites; and influenced by the love of reward, he wished to gratify Balak; but he was compelled by Jehovah’s power to bless them. Hence later the Jews saw him as a most abandoned deceiver.
s: Of Hebrew origin \[[H1109](H1109)\]; *Balaam*, a mesopotamian (symbolic of a false teacher): - Balaam.

d:
Balak = a devastator or spoiler
**1.** a king of Moab
s: Of Hebrew origin \[[H1111](H1111)\]; *Balak*, a Moabite: - Balac.

d: **1.** a money bag, purse
s: Probably remotely from [G906](G906) (as a *depository*); a *pouch* (for money): - bag, purse.

d:
**1.** to throw or let go of a thing without caring where it falls
  **a.** to scatter, to throw, cast into
  **b.** to give over to one’s care uncertain about the result
  **c.** of fluids
    **1.** to pour, pour into of rivers
    **2.** to pour out
**2.** to put into, insert
s: A primary verb; to *throw* (in various applications, more or less violent or intense): - arise, cast (out), X dung, lay, lie, pour, put (up), send, strike, throw (down), thrust. Compare [G4496](G4496).

d:
**1.** to dip repeatedly, to immerse, to submerge (of vessels sunk)
**2.** to cleanse by dipping or submerging, to wash, to make clean with water, to wash one’s self, bathe
**3.** to overwhelm Not to be confused with 911, bapto. The clearest example that showsthe meaning of baptizo is a text from the Greek poet and physicianNicander, who lived about 200 B.C. It is a recipe for making picklesand is helpful because it uses both words. Nicander says that inorder to make a pickle, the vegetable should first be ’dipped’(bapto) into boiling water and then ’baptised’ (baptizo) in thevinegar solution. Both verbs concern the immersing of vegetables in asolution. But the first is temporary. The second, the act ofbaptising the vegetable, produces a permanent change. When used in the New Testament, this word more often refers to ourunion and identification with christ than to our water baptism. e.g.Mar 16:16. ’He that believes and is baptised shall be saved’.christ is saying that mere intellectual assent is not enough. Theremust be a union with him, a real change, like the vegetable to thepickle! Bible Study Magazine, James Montgomery Boice, May 1989.
s: From a derivative of [G911](G911); to *make* *whelmed* (that is, *fully* *wet*); used only (in the New Testament) of ceremonial *ablution*, especially (technically) of the ordinance of Christian *baptism:* - baptist, baptize, wash.

d:
**1.** immersion, submersion
  **a.** of calamities and afflictions with which one is quite overwhelmed
  **b.** of John’s baptism, that purification rite by which men on confessing their sins were bound to spiritual reformation, obtained the pardon of their past sins and became qualified for the benefits of the messiah’s kingdom soon to be set up. This was valid Christian baptism, as this was the only baptism the apostles received and it is not recorded anywhere that they were ever rebaptised after Pentecost.
  **c.** of Christian baptism; a rite of immersion in water as commanded by christ, by which one after confessing his sins and professing his faith in christ, having been born again by the holy spirit unto a new life, identifies publicly with the fellowship of christ and the church. In Rom 6:3 Paul states we are baptised unto death meaning that weare not only dead to our former ways, but they are buried. To returnto them is as unthinkable for a Christian as for one to dig up a deadcorpse! In Moslem countries a new believer has little trouble withMoslems until he is publicly baptised. It is then, that the Moslems’know he means business, and then the persecution starts. See alsodiscussion of baptism under No. 907.
s: From [G907](G907); *baptism* (technically or figuratively): - baptism.

d:
**1.** a washing, purification effected by means of water
  **a.** of washing prescribed by the Mosaic law (Heb 9:10)
**2.** which seems to mean an exposition of the difference between the washings prescribed by the Mosaic law and Christian baptism
s: From [G907](G907); *ablution* (ceremonially or Christian): - baptism, washing.

d:
**1.** a baptiser
**2.** one who administers the rite of baptism
**3.** the surname of John, the forerunner of christ
s: From [G907](G907); a *baptizer*, as an epithet of Christ’s forerunner: - Baptist.

d:
**1.** to dip, dip in, immerse
**2.** to dip into dye, to dye, colour Not to be confused with 907, baptizo. The clearest example that showsthe meaning of baptizo is a text from the Greek poet and physicianNicander, who lived about 200 B.C. It is a recipe for making picklesand is helpful because it uses both words. Nicander says that inorder to make a pickle, the vegetable should first be ’dipped’(bapto) into boiling water and then ’baptised’ (baptizo) in thevinegar solution. Both verbs concern the immersing of vegetables in asolution. But the first is temporary. The second, the act ofbaptising the vegetable, produces a permanent change.
s: A primary verb; to *whelm*, that is, cover wholly with a fluid; in the New Testament only in a qualified or specific sense, that is, (literally) to *moisten* (a part of one’s person), or (by implication) to *stain* (as with dye): - dip.

d:
Barabbas = son of a father or master
**1.** the captive robber whom the Jews begged Pilate to release instead of christ
s: Of Chaldee origin (\[[H1347](H1347)\] and [G5](G5) (Greek)); *son* *of* *Abba*; *Bar-abbas*, an Israelite: - Barabbas.

d:
Barak = lightning
**1.** a commander of the Israelites
s: Of Hebrew origin \[[H1301](H1301)\]; *Barak*, an Israelite: - Barak.

d:
Barachiah = Jehovah blesses
**1.** said to be the father of the Zachariah slain in the temple
s: Of Hebrew origin \[[H1296](H1296)\]; *Barachias* (that is, *Berechijah*), an Israelite: - Barachias.

d:
**1.** one whose speech is rude, rough and harsh
**2.** one who speaks a foreign or strange language which is not understood by another
**3.** used by the Greeks of any foreigner ignorant of the Greek language, whether mental or moral, with the added notion after the Persian war, of rudeness and brutality. The word is used in the N.T. without the idea of reproachfulness.
s: Of uncertain derivation; a *foreigner* (that is, *non* *Greek*): - barbarian (-rous).

d: **1.** to burden, weigh down, depress
s: From [G926](G926); to *weigh* down (figuratively): - burden, charge, heavy, press.

d: **1.** heavily, with difficulty
s: Adverb from [G926](G926); *heavily* (figuratively): - dull.

d:
Bartholomew = son of Tolmai
**1.** one of the twelve apostles of christ
s: Of Chaldee origin \[[H1247](H1247)\] and \[[H8526](H8526)\]; *son* *of* *Tolmai*; *Bar-tholomaeus*, a Christian apostle: - Bartholomeus.

d:
Barjesus = son of Jesus
**1.** a certain false prophet
s: Of Chaldee origin \[[H1247](H1247)\] and \[[H3091](H3091)\]; *son* *of* *Jesus* (or *Joshua*); *Barjesus*, an Israelite: - Barjesus.

d:
Barjona = son of Jonah
**1.** the surname of the apostle Peter
s: Of Chaldee origin \[[H1247](H1247)\] and \[[H3124](H3124)\]; *son* *of* *Jonas* (or *Jonah*); *Bar-jonas*, an Israelite: - Bar-jona.

d:
Barnabas = son of rest
**1.** the surname of Joses or Joseph, a Levite, a native of Cyprus he was a distinguished Christian teacher and companion and colleague of Paul.
s: Of Chaldee origin \[[H1247](H1247)\] and \[[H5029](H5029)\]; *son* *of* *Nabas* (that is, *prophecy*); *Barnabas*, an Israelite: - Barnabas.

d: **1.** heaviness, weight, burden, trouble
s: Probably from the same as [G939](G939) (through the notion of *going* down; compare [G899](G899)); *weight*; in the New Testament only, figuratively a *load*, *abundance*, *authority:* - burden (-some), weight.
o: probably from the same as [G939](G939) (through the notion of going down; cf [G899](G899))

d:
Barsabas = son of Sabas
**1.** the surname of a certain Joseph (Act 1:23)
**2.** the surname of a certain Judas (Act 15:22)
s: Of Chaldee origin \[[H1247](H1247)\] and probably \[[H6634](H6634)\]; *son* *of* *Sabas* (or *Tsaba*); *Barsabas*, the name of two Israelites: - Barsabas.

d:
Bartimaeus = son of Timaeus
**1.** a certain blind man
s: Of Chaldee origin \[[H1247](H1247)\] and \[[H2931](H2931)\]; *son* *of* *Timaeus* (or the *unclean*); *Bartimaeus*, an Israelite: - Bartimus.

d: **1.** to weigh down, overcharge
s: From [G926](G926); to *burden* (figuratively): - overcharge.

d:
**1.** heavy in weight
**2.** metaph.
  **a.** burdensome
  **b.** severe, stern
  **c.** weighty
    **1.** of great moment
  **d.** violent, cruel, unsparing
s: From the same as [G922](G922); *weighty*, that is, (figuratively) *burdensome*, *grave:* - grievous, heavy, weightier.

d: **1.** of weighty, great value, very precious, costly
s: From [G926](G926) and [G5092](G5092); highly *valuable:* - very precious.

d:
**1.** to test (metals) by the touchstone, which is a black siliceous stone used to test the purity of gold or silver by the colour of the streak produced on it by rubbing it with either metal
**2.** to question by applying torture
**3.** to torture
**4.** to vex with grievous pains (of body or mind), to torment
**5.** to be harassed, distressed
  **a.** of those who at sea are struggling with a head wind
s: From [G931](G931); to *torture:* - pain, toil, torment, toss, vex.

d:
**1.** to torture, a testing by the touchstone, which is a black siliceous stone used to test the purity of gold or silver by the colour of the streak produced on it by rubbing it with either metal
**2.** torment, torture
  **a.** the act of tormenting
  **b.** the state or condition of those tormented
s: From [G928](G928); *torture:* - torment.

d:
**1.** one who elicits the truth by the use of the rack
  **a.** an inquisitor, torturer also used of a jailer doubtless because the business of torturing was also assigned to him
s: From [G928](G928); a *torturer:* - tormentor.

d:
**1.** a touchstone, which is a black siliceous stone used to test the purity of gold or silver by the colour of the streak produced on it by rubbing it with either metal
**2.** the rack or instrument of torture by which one is forced to divulge the truth
**3.** torture, torment, acute pains
  **a.** of the pains of a disease
  **b.** of those in hell after death
s: Perhaps remotely from the same as [G939](G939) (through the notion of *going* to the bottom); a *touch* *stone*, that is, (by analogy) *torture:* - torment.
o: perhaps remotely from the same as [G939](G939) (through the notion of going to the bottom)

d:
**1.** royal power, kingship, dominion, rule
  **a.** not to be confused with an actual kingdom but rather the right or authority to rule over a kingdom
  **b.** of the royal power of Jesus as the triumphant messiah
  **c.** of the royal power and dignity conferred on Christians in the messiah’s kingdom
**2.** a kingdom, the territory subject to the rule of a king
**3.** used in the N.T. to refer to the reign of the messiah
s: From [G935](G935); properly *royalty*, that is, (abstractly) *rule*, or (concretely) a *realm* (literally or figuratively): - kingdom, + reign.

d: **1.** the royal palace
s: Neuter of [G934](G934); a *palace:* - king’s court.

d: **1.** royal, kingly, regal
s: From [G935](G935); *kingly* (in nature): - royal.

d: **1.** leader of the people, prince, commander, Lord of the land, king
s: Probably from [G939](G939) (through the notion of a *foundation* of power); a *sovereign* (abstractly, relatively or figuratively): - king.
o: probably from [G939](G939) (through the notion of a foundation of power)

d:
**1.** to be king, to exercise kingly power, to reign
  **a.** of the governor of a province
  **b.** of the rule of the messiah
  **c.** of the reign of Christians in the millennium
**2.** metaph. to exercise the highest influence, to control
s: From [G935](G935); to *rule* (literally or figuratively): - king, reign.

d:
**1.** of or belong to a king, kingly, royal, regal
  **a.** of a man, the officer or minister of a prince, a courtier
**2.** subject to a king
  **a.** of a country
**3.** befitting or worthy of a king, royal
**4.** metaph. principal, chief
s: From [G935](G935); *regal* (in relation), that is, (literally) belonging to (or befitting) the sovereign (as land, dress, or a *courtier*), or (figuratively) *preeminent:* - king’s, nobleman, royal.

d: **1.** queen
s: Feminine from [G936](G936); a *queen:* - queen.

d:
**1.** a stepping, walking
**2.** that with which one steps, the foot
s: From βαίνω bainō (to *walk*); a *pace* (“base”), that is, (by implication) the *foot:* - foot.

d:
**1.** to speak ill of one, to slander, traduce him
**2.** to bring evil on one by feigning praise or an evil eye
**3.** to charm, to bewitch

d: **1.** hurtful, injurious

**1.** to sprout, bud, put forth new leaves

Boaz = in him is strength

**1.** Boreas, the north-north-east wind

d:

**1.** byssus, a species of Egyptian flax

d:
Gabbatha = elevated or a platform
**1.** a raised place, elevation In the Greek was called Lithostrotos, or the pavement of stones,as the Syrian version renders it: it is thought to be the roomGazith, in which the sanhedrin sat in the temple when they triedcapital causes; and it was so called, because it was paved withsmooth, square hewn stones: it was in the north part; half of itwas holy, and half of it was common: and it had two doors, one forthat part which was holy, and another for that part that was common;and in that half that was common the sanhedrin sat. So that intothis part of it, and by this door, Pilate, though a Gentile, mightenter. This place, in the language of the Jews, who at that time spoke Syrian, was Gabbatha, from its height, as it should seem; though the Syrian and Persian versions read Gaphiphtha, which signifies a fence or enclosure. Mention is made in the Talmud of the upper Gab in the mountain of the house; but whether the same with this Gabbatha, and whether this is the same with the chamber Gazith, is not certain. The Septuagint uses the same word as John here does, and calls by the same name the pavement of the temple on which Israelites fell and worshipped God. (2Ch 7:3)
**•** (Gill)
s: Of Chaldee origin (compare \[[H1355](H1355)\]); *the* *knoll*; *gabbatha*, a vernacular term for the Roman tribunal in Jerusalem: - Gabbatha.

s: Of Hebrew origin \[[H5804](H5804)\]; *Gazah* (that is, *Azzah*), a place in Palestine: - Gaza.

d: **1.** a repository of treasure, especially of public treasure, a treasury
s: From [G1047](G1047) and [G5438](G5438); a *treasure* *house*, that is, a court in the temple for the collection boxes: - treasury.

d:
Gaius = lord
**1.** a Macedonian who accompanied Paul in his travels
**2.** a man from Derbe who went with Paul from Corinth in his last journey to Jerusalem
**3.** a man of Corinth who was his host in his second sojourn in that city
**4.** an unknown Christian to whom John’s third epistle is addressed
s: Of Latin origin; *Gaius* (that is, *Caius*), a Christian: - Gaius.

d:
**1.** milk
**2.** a metaph. for the less difficult Christian truths
s: Of uncertain affinity; *milk* (figuratively): - milk.

d: **1.** a Galatians
s: From [G1053](G1053); a *Galatian* or inhabitant of Galatia: - Galatian.

d:
Galatia = land of the Galli, Gauls
**1.** the Roman province of Galatia my be roughly described as the central region of the peninsula of Asia Minor, bounded on the north by Bithynia and Paphlagonia; on the east by Pontus; on the south by Cappadocia and Lycaonia; on the west by Phrygia
s: Of foreign origin; *Galatia*, a region of Asia: - Galatia.

d: **1.** a citizen of Galatia
s: From [G1053](G1053); *Galatic* or relating to Galatia: - of Galatia.

d: **1.** calmness, stillness of the sea, a calm
s: Of uncertain derivation; *tranquillity:* - calm.

d: Galilee = Circuit
s: Of hebrew origin \[[H1551](H1551)\]; *Galilaea* (that is, the heathen *circle*), a region of Palestine: - Galilee.

d: **1.** a native of Galilee
s: From [G1056](G1056); *Galilaean* or belonging to Galilaea: - Galilan, of Galilee.

d:
Gallio = One who lives on milk
**1.** Junius Annaeus Gallio, the Roman proconsul of Achaia when Paul was at Corinth, 53 A.D., under the emperor Claudius. Act 18:12. He was brother to Jucius Annaeus Seneca, the philosopher. Jerome in the Chronicle of Eusebius says that he committed suicide in 65 A.D. Winer thinks he was put to death by Nero.
s: Of Latin origin; *Gallion* (that is, *Gallio*), a Roman officer: - Gallio

d:
Gamaliel = my recompenser is God
**1.** a Pharisee and celebrated doctor of the law, who gave prudent worldly advice in the Sanhedrin respecting the treatment of the followers of Jesus of Nazareth. Act 5:34 ff. (A.D.29.) We learn from Act 22:3 that he was the preceptor of Paul. He is generally identified with the very celebrated Jewish doctor Gamaliel, grandson of Hillel, and who is referred to as authority in the Jewish Mishna.
s: Of Hebrew origin \[[H1583](H1583)\]; *Gamaliel* (that is, *Gamliel*), an Israelite: - Gamaliel.

d:
**1.** to lead in marriage, take to wife
  **a.** to get married, to marry
  **b.** to give one’s self in marriage
**2.** to give a daughter in marriage
s: From [G1062](G1062); to *wed* (of either sex): - marry (a wife).

d: **1.** give in marriage
s: From [G1062](G1062); to *espouse* (a daughter to a husband): - give in marriage.

d:
**1.** a wedding or marriage festival, a wedding banquet, a wedding feast
**2.** marriage, matrimony
s: Of uncertain affinity; *nuptials:* - marriage, wedding.

A primary particle; properly assigning a *reason* (used in argument, explanation or intensification; often with other particles): - and, as, because (that), but, even, for indeed, no doubt, seeing, then, therefore, verily, what, why, yet.

d:
**1.** the belly
**2.** the womb
**3.** the stomach
  **a.** a glutton, gormandiser, a man who is as it were all stomach
s: Of uncertain derivation; the *stomach*; by analogy the *matrix*; figuratively a *gourmand:* - belly, + with child, womb.

d:
**1.** indeed, truly, at least
**2.** even
**3.** if indeed, seeing that
s: A primary particle of *emphasis* or *qualification* (often used with other particles prefixed): - and besides, doubtless, at least, yet.
o: a primary particle of emphasis or qualification (often used with other particles prefixed)

d:
Gideon = the cutter down
**1.** a of the judge of Israel who delivered them from the Midianites
s: Of Hebrew origin \[[H1439](H1439)\]; *Gedeon* (that is, *Gideon*), an Israelite: - Gedeon.

d: **1.** Hell is the place of the future punishment call Gehenna or Gehenna of fire. This was originally the valley of Hinnom, south of Jerusalem, where the filth and dead animals of the city were cast out and burned; a fit symbol of the wicked and their future destruction.
s: Of Hebrew origin (\[[H1516](H1516)\] and \[[H2011](H2011)\]); *valley* *of* (the son of) *Hinnom*; *gehenna* (or *Ge-Hinnom*), a valley of Jerusalem, used (figuratively) as a name for the place (or state) of everlasting punishment: - hell.

d: Gethsemane = an oil press
s: Of Chaldee origin (compare \[[H1660](H1660)\] and \[[H8081](H8081)\]); *oil* *press*; *Gethsemane*, a garden near Jerusalem: - Gethsemane.

d: **1.** a neighbour
s: From [G1093](G1093); a *neighbor* (as adjoining one’s *ground*); by implication a *friend:* - neighbour.

d: **1.** to laugh
s: Of uncertain affinity; to *laugh* (as a sign of joy or satisfaction): - laugh.

d: **1.** laughter
s: From [G1070](G1070); *laughter* (as a mark of gratification): - laughter.

d: **1.** to fill, fill full
s: Transitive from [G1073](G1073); to *fill* entirely: - fill (be) full.

d: **1.** to be full, filled, full
s: A primary verb; to *swell* out, that is, *be* *full:* - be full.

d:
**1.** fathered, birth, nativity
**2.** that which has been begotten, men of the same stock, a family
  **a.** the several ranks of natural descent, the successive members of a genealogy
