  **b.** metaph. a group of men very like each other in endowments, pursuits, character
    **1.** esp. in a bad sense, a perverse nation
**3.** the whole multitude of men living at the same time
**4.** an age (i.e. the time ordinarily occupied be each successive generation), a space of 30 - 33 years
s: From (a presumed derivative of) [G1085](G1085); a *generation*; by implication an *age* (the period or the persons): - age, generation, nation, time.

d:
**1.** to recount a family’s origin and lineage, trace ancestry
**2.** to draw one’s origin, derive one’s pedigree
s: From [G1074](G1074) and [G3056](G3056); to *reckon* *by* *generations*, that is, *trace* *in* *genealogy:* - count by descent.

d: **1.** a genealogy, a record of descent or lineage
s: From the same as [G1075](G1075); *tracing* *by* *generations*, that is, “genealogy”: - genealogy.

d:
**1.** a birthday celebration, a birthday feast
  **a.** the earlier Greeks used this word of funeral commemorations, a festival commemorative of a deceased friend
s: Neuter plural of a derivative of [G1078](G1078); *birthday* ceremonies: - birthday.

d:
**1.** source, origin
  **a.** a book of one’s lineage, i.e. in which his ancestry or progeny are enumerated
**2.** used of birth, nativity
**3.** of that which follows origin, viz. existence, life
  **a.** the wheel of life (Jas 3:6)
s: From the same as [G1074](G1074); *nativity*; figuratively *nature:* - generation, nature (-ral).

d: **1.** birth, from birth
s: Feminine of a presumed derivative of the base of [G1074](G1074); *birth:* - birth.
o: from a presumed derivative of the base of [G1074](G1074)

d:
**1.** of men who fathered children
  **a.** to be born
  **b.** to be begotten
    **1.** of women giving birth to children
**2.** metaph.
  **a.** to engender, cause to arise, excite
  **b.** in a Jewish sense, of one who brings others over to his way of life, to convert someone
  **c.** of God making christ his son
  **d.** of God making men his sons through faith in christ’s work
s: From a variation of [G1085](G1085); to *procreate* (properly of the father, but by extension of the mother); figuratively to *regenerate:* - bear, beget, be born, bring forth, conceive, be delivered of, gender, make, spring.

d:
**1.** that which has been born or begotten
  **a.** the offspring or progeny of men or animals
  **b.** the fruits of the earth, the produce of agriculture
s: From [G1080](G1080); *offspring*; by analogy *produce* (literally or figuratively): - fruit, generation.

d: Gennesaret = a harp
s: Of Hebrew origin (compare \[[H3672](H3672)\]); *Gennesaret* (that is, *Kinnereth*), a lake and plain in Palestine: - Gennesaret.

d:
**1.** begat, engendering
**2.** nativity, birth
s: From [G1080](G1080); *nativity:* - birth.

d: **1.** begotten, born
s: From [G1080](G1080); *born:* - they that are born.

d:
**1.** kindred
  **a.** offspring
  **b.** family
  **c.** stock, tribe, nation
    **1.** i.e. nationality or descent from a particular people
  **d.** the aggregate of many individuals of the same nature, kind, sort
s: From [G1096](G1096); “kin” (abstractly or concretely, literally or figuratively, individually or collectively): - born, country (-man), diversity, generation, kind (-red), nation, offspring, stock.

d: Gergesenes = a stranger drawing near ?
s: Of Hebrew origin \[[H1622](H1622)\]; a *Gergesene* (that is, *Girgashite*) or one of the aborigines of Palestine: - Gergesene.

d:
**1.** a senate, council of elders
  **a.** to denote the chief council of nations or cities
  **b.** the Sanhedrin
s: From [G1088](G1088); the *eldership*, that is, (collectively) the Jewish *Sanhedrim:* - senate.

d: **1.** an old man
s: Of uncertain affinity (compare [G1094](G1094)); *aged:* - old.

d:
**1.** to taste, to try the flavour of
**2.** to taste
  **a.** i.e. perceive the flavour of, partake of, enjoy
  **b.** to feel, make trial of, experience
**3.** to take food, eat, to take nourishment, eat
s: A primary verb; to *taste*; by implication to *eat*; figuratively to *experience* (good or ill): - eat, taste.

d: **1.** to practise agriculture, to till the ground
s: From [G1092](G1092); to *till* (the soil): - dress.

d: **1.** a cultivated field, husbandry, tillage
s: Neuter of a (presumed) derivative of [G1092](G1092); *cultivable*, that is, a *farm:* - husbandry.

d: **1.** a husbandman, tiller of the soil, a vine dresser
s: From [G1093](G1093) and the base of [G2041](G2041); a *land* *worker*, that is, *farmer:* - husbandman.

d:
**1.** arable land
**2.** the ground, the earth as a standing place
**3.** the main land as opposed to the sea or water
**4.** the earth as a whole
  **a.** the earth as opposed to the heavens
  **b.** the inhabited earth, the abode of men and animals
**5.** a country, land enclosed within fixed boundaries, a tract of land, territory, region
s: Contracted from a primary word; *soil*; by extension a *region*, or the solid part or the whole of the *terrene* globe (including the occupants in each application): - country, earth (-ly), ground, land, world.

d: **1.** old age
s: Akin to [G1088](G1088); *senility:* - old age.

d:
**1.** to grow old
**2.** of things and institutions: to fail from age, be obsolescent
s: From [G1094](G1094); to *be* *senescent:* - be (wax) old.

d:
**1.** to become, i.e. to come into existence, begin to be, receive being
**2.** to become, i.e. to come to pass, happen
  **a.** of events
**3.** to arise, appear in history, come upon the stage
  **a.** of men appearing in public
**4.** to be made, finished
  **a.** of miracles, to be performed, wrought
**5.** to become, be made
s: A prolonged and middle form of a primary verb; to *cause* *to* *be* (“gen” -erate), that is, (reflexively) to *become* (*come* *into* *being*), used with great latitude (literally, figuratively, intensively, etc.): - arise be assembled, be (come, -fall, -have self), be brought (to pass), (be) come (to pass), continue, be divided, be done, draw, be ended, fall, be finished, follow, be found, be fulfilled, + God forbid, grow, happen, have, be kept, be made, be married, be ordained to be, partake, pass, be performed, be published, require, seem, be showed, X soon as it was, sound, be taken, be turned, use, wax, will, would, be wrought.
o: a prolongation and middle voice form of a primary verb

d:
**1.** to learn to know, come to know, get a knowledge of perceive, feel
  **a.** to become known
**2.** to know, understand, perceive, have knowledge of
  **a.** to understand
  **b.** to know
**3.** Jewish idiom for sexual intercourse between a man and a woman
**4.** to become acquainted with, to know
s: A prolonged form of a primary verb; to “know” (absolutely), in a great variety of applications and with many implications (as shown at left, with others not thus clearly expressed): - allow, be aware (of), feel, (have) known (-ledge), perceive, be resolved, can speak, be sure, understand.
o: a prolonged form of a primary verb

d: **1.** the sweet juice pressed the grape, sweet wine
s: Akin to [G1099](G1099); *sweet* wine, that is, (properly) *must* (fresh juice), but used of the more saccharine (and therefore highly inebriating) fermented *wine:* - new wine.

d: **1.** sweet
s: Of uncertain affinity; *sweet* (that is, not bitter nor salt): - sweet, fresh.

d:
**1.** the tongue, a member of the body, an organ of speech
**2.** a tongue
  **a.** the language or dialect used by a particular people distinct from that of other nations
s: Of uncertain affinity; the *tongue*; by implication a *language* (specifically one naturally unacquired): - tongue.

d:
**1.** a case in which to keep mouth-pieces of wind instruments
**2.** a small box for other uses
  **a.** esp. a casket, a purse to keep money in
s: From [G1100](G1100) and the base of [G2889](G2889); properly a *case* (to keep mouthpieces of wind instruments in), that is, (by extension) a *casket* or (specifically) *purse:* - bag.

d: **1.** a fuller
s: By variation for a derivative from κνάπτω knaptō (to *tease* cloth); a cloth *dresser:* - fuller.
o: by variation for a derivative from knapto (to tease cloth)

d:
**1.** legitimately born, not spurious
**2.** true, genuine, sincere
s: From the same as [G1077](G1077); *legitimate* (of birth), that is, *genuine:* - own, sincerity, true.

d: **1.** genuinely, faithfully, sincerely
s: Adverb from [G1103](G1103); *genuinely*, that is, *really:* - naturally.

d: **1.** darkness, gloom
s: Akin to [G3509](G3509); *gloom* (as of a storm): - blackness.

d:
**1.** the faculty of knowledge, mind, reason
**2.** that which is thought or known, one’s mind
  **a.** view, judgment, opinion
  **b.** mind concerning what ought to be done
    **1.** by one’s self: resolve purpose, intention
    **2.** by others: judgment, advice
    **3.** decree
s: From [G1097](G1097); *cognition*, that is, (subjectively) *opinion*, or (objectively) *resolve* (*counsel*, *consent*, etc.): - advice, + agree, judgment, mind, purpose, will.

d:
**1.** to make known
  **a.** to become known, be recognised
**2.** to know, to gain knowledge of, have thorough knowledge of
  **a.** in earlier Greek it means to gain a knowledge of or have thorough knowledge of
s: From a derivative of [G1097](G1097); to *make* *known*; subjectively to *know:* - certify, declare, make known, give to understand, do to wit, wot.

d:
**1.** knowledge signifies in general intelligence, understanding
  **a.** the general knowledge of Christian religion
  **b.** the deeper more perfect and enlarged knowledge of this religion, such as belongs to the more advanced
  **c.** esp. of things lawful and unlawful for Christians
  **d.** moral wisdom, such as is seen in right living
s: From [G1097](G1097); *knowing* (the act), that is, (by implication) *knowledge:* - knowledge, science.

d: **1.** an expert, a connoisseur
s: From [G1097](G1097); a *knower:* - expert.

d: **1.** known, notable
s: From [G1097](G1097); well *known:* - acquaintance, (which may be) known, notable.

d:
**1.** to murmur, mutter, grumble, say anything against in a low tone
  **a.** of the cooing of doves
  **b.** of those who confer secretly together
  **c.** of those who discontentedly complain
s: Of uncertain derivation; to *grumble:* - murmur.

d:
**1.** a murmur, murmuring, muttering
  **a.** a secret debate
  **b.** a secret displeasure not openly avowed
s: From [G1111](G1111); a *grumbling:* - grudging, murmuring.

d: **1.** a murmurer, one who discontentedly complains (against God)
s: From [G1111](G1111); a *grumbler:* - murmurer.

d:
**1.** a wailer, a howler
**2.** a juggler, enchanter (because incantations used to be uttered in a kind of howl)
**3.** a deceiver, imposter
s: From γοάω goaō (to *wail*); properly a *wizard* (as *muttering* spells), that is, (by implication) an *impostor:* - seducer.

d:
Golgotha = skull
**1.** the name of a place outside Jerusalem where Jesus was crucified; so called, apparently because its form resembled a skull
s: Of Chaldee origin (compare \[[H1538](H1538)\]); *the* *skull*; *Golgotha*, a knoll near Jerusalem: - Golgotha.

d:
Gomorrha = submersion
**1.** a city in eastern part of Judah that was destroyed when the Lord rained fire and brimstone on it; now covered by the Dead Sea
s: Of Hebrew origin \[[H6017](H6017)\]; *Gomorrha* (that is, *Amorah*), a place near the Dead Sea: - Gomorrha.

d:
**1.** a lading or freight of a ship, cargo, merchandise conveyed in a ship
**2.** any merchandise
s: From [G1073](G1073); a *load* (as *filling*), that is, (specifically) a *cargo*, or (by extension) *wares:* - burden, merchandise.

d: **1.** fathers, parent, the parents
s: From the base of [G1096](G1096); a *parent:* - parent.

d: **1.** the knee, to kneel down
s: Of uncertain affinity; the “knee”: - knee (X -l).

d: **1.** to fall on the knees, the act of imploring aid, and of expressing reverence and honour
s: From a compound of [G1119](G1119) and the alternate of [G4098](G4098); to *fall* *on* the *knee:* - bow the knee, kneel down.
o: from a compound of [G1119](G1119) and the alternate of [G4098](G4098)

d:
**1.** a letter
**2.** any writing, a document or record
  **a.** a note of hand, bill, bond, account, written acknowledgement of a debt
  **b.** a letter, an epistle
  **c.** the sacred writings (of the OT)
**3.** letters, i.e. learning
  **a.** of sacred learning
s: From [G1125](G1125); a *writing*, that is, a *letter*, *note*, *epistle*, *book*, etc.; plural *learning:* - bill, learning, letter, scripture, writing, written.

d:
**1.** a clerk, scribe, esp.a public servant, secretary, recorder, whose office and influence differed in different states
**2.** in the Bible, a man learned in the Mosaic law and in the sacred writings, an interpreter, teacher. Scribes examined the more difficult and subtle questions of the law; added to the Mosaic law decisions of various kinds thought to elucidate its meaning and scope, and did this to the detriment of religion. Since the advice of men skilled in the law was needed in the examination in the causes and the solution of the difficult questions, they were enrolled in the Sanhedrin; and are mentioned in connection with the priests and elders of the people. See a Bible Dictionary for more information on the scribes.
**3.** a religious teacher: so instructed that from his learning and ability to teach advantage may redound to the kingdom of heaven
s: From [G1121](G1121); a *writer*, that is, (professionally) *scribe* or *secretary:* - scribe, town-clerk.

d: **1.** written
s: From [G1125](G1125); *inscribed* (figuratively): - written.

d:
**1.** a writing, thing written
**2.** the Scripture, used to denote either the book itself, or its contents
**3.** a certain portion or section of the holy Scripture
s: From [G1125](G1125); a *document*, that is, holy *Writ* (or its contents or a statement in it): - scripture.

d:
**1.** to write, with reference to the form of the letters
  **a.** to delineate (or form) letters on a tablet, parchment, paper, or other material
**2.** to write, with reference to the contents of the writing
  **a.** to express in written characters
  **b.** to commit to writing (things not to be forgotten), write down, record
  **c.** used of those things which stand written in the sacred books (of the OT)
  **d.** to write to one, i.e. by writing (in a written epistle) to give information, directions
**3.** to fill with writing
**4.** to draw up in writing, compose
s: A primary verb; to “grave”, especially to *write*; figuratively to *describe:* - describe, write (-ing, -ten).

d: **1.** old womanish, old wives, an old woman
s: From γραῦς graus (an *old* *woman*) and [G1491](G1491); *crone* *like*, that is, *silly:* - old wives’.

d:
**1.** to watch
**2.** metaph. give strict attention to, be cautious, active
  **a.** to take heed lest through remission and indolence some destructive calamity suddenly overtake one
s: From [G1453](G1453); to *keep* *awake*, that is, *watch* (literally or figuratively): - be vigilant, wake, (be) watch (-ful).

d:
**1.** to exercise naked (in a palaestra or school of athletics)
**2.** to exercise vigorously, in any way, either the body or the mind
s: From [G1131](G1131); to *practise* *naked* (in the games), that is, *train* (figuratively): - exercise.

d:
**1.** the exercise of the body in a palaestra or school of athletics
**2.** any exercise whatever
  **a.** the exercise of conscientiousness relative to the body such as is characteristic of ascetics and consists in abstinence from matrimony and certain kinds of food
s: From [G1128](G1128); *training*, that is, (figuratively) *asceticism:* - exercise.

d:
**1.** to be lightly or poorly clad
**2.** to be a light armed soldier
s: From a derivative of [G1131](G1131); to *strip*, that is, (reflexively) *go* *poorly* *clad:* - be naked.

d:
**1.** properly
  **a.** unclad, without clothing, the naked body
  **b.** ill clad
  **c.** clad in undergarments only (the outer garments or cloak being laid aside)
  **d.** of the soul, whose garment is the body, stripped of the body, without a body
**2.** metaph.
  **a.** naked, i.e. open, lay bare
  **b.** only, mere, bare, i.e. mere grain not the plant itself
s: Of uncertain affinity; *nude* (absolutely or relatively, literally or figuratively): - naked.

d: **1.** nakedness of the body
s: From [G1131](G1131); *nudity* (absolutely or comparatively): - nakedness.

d: **1.** a little woman: used contemptuously
s: A diminutive from [G1135](G1135); a *little* (that is, *foolish*) *woman:* - silly woman.

d: **1.** of or belonging to a woman, feminine, female
s: From [G1135](G1135); *feminine:* - wife.

d:
**1.** a woman of any age, whether a virgin, or married, or a widow
**2.** a wife
  **a.** of a betrothed woman
s: Probably from the base of [G1096](G1096); a *woman*; specifically a *wife:* - wife, woman.

d:
Gog = mountain
**1.** the king of the land of Magog who will come from the north and attack the land of Israel
s: Of Hebrew origin \[[H1463](H1463)\]; *Gog*, a symbolic name for some future Antichrist: - Gog.

d:
**1.** corner
  **a.** an external angle, a corner
  **b.** internal corner, i.e. a secret place
s: Probably akin to [G1119](G1119); an *angle:* - corner, quarter.

d: **1.** second king of Israel, and ancestor of Jesus christ
s: Of Hebrew origin \[[H1732](H1732)\]; *Dabid* (that is, *David*), the Israelite king: - David.

d: **1.** to be under the power of a demon.
s: Middle voice from [G1142](G1142); to *be* *exercised* *by* *a* *daemon:* - have a (be vexed with, be possessed with) devil (-s).

d:
**1.** the divine power, deity, divinity
**2.** a spirit, a being inferior to God, superior to men
**3.** evil spirits or the messengers and ministers of the devil
s: Neuter of a derivative of [G1142](G1142); a *daemonic* *being*; by extension a *deity:* - devil, god.

d: **1.** resembling or proceeding from an evil spirit, demon-like
s: From [G1140](G1140) and [G1142](G1142); *daemon* *like:* - devilish.

d:
**1.** a God, a Goddess
  **a.** an inferior deity, whether good or bad
**2.** in the NT, an evil spirit
s: From δαίω daiō (to *distribute* fortunes); a *demon* or super natural spirit (of a bad nature): - devil.

d:
**1.** to bite with the teeth
**2.** metaph., to wound the soul, cut lacerate, rend with reproaches
s: A prolonged form of a primary root; to *bite*, that is, (figuratively) *thwart:* - bite.
o: a prolonged form of a primary root

d: **1.** a tear
s: Of uncertain affinity; a *tear:* - tear.

d: **1.** to weep, shed tears
s: From [G1144](G1144); to *shed* *tears:* - weep. Compare [G2799](G2799).

d: **1.** a ring (on the finger)
s: From [G1147](G1147); a *finger* ring: - ring.

d: **1.** a finger
s: Probably from [G1176](G1176); a *finger:* - finger.

d:
Dalmanutha = slow firebrand
**1.** is a town on the west side of the Sea of Galilee, near Magdala
s: Probably of Chaldee origin; *Dalmanutha*, a place in Palestine: - Dalmanutha.

d:
Dalmatia = a priestly robe
**1.** a part of Illyricum on the Adriatic Sea; on the east adjoining Pannonia and upper Moesia, on the north separated from Liburia by the river Titus, and extending southwards as far as the river Drinus and the city Lissus
s: Probably of foreign derivation; *Dalmatia*, a region of Europe: - Dalmatia.

d:
**1.** to tame
**2.** curb, restrain
s: A variation of an obsolete primary of the same meaning; to *tame:* - tame.
o: a variation of an obsolete primary of the same meaning

d:
**1.** a young cow, heifer
  **a.** of the red heifer with whose ashes, by the Mosaic law, those were to be sprinkled who had become defiled
s: Probably from the base of [G1150](G1150); a *heifer* (as *tame*): - heifer.

d:
Damaris = a heifer
**1.** an Athenian woman converted to Christianity by Paul’s preaching
s: Probably from the base of [G1150](G1150); perhaps *gentle*; *Damaris*, an Athenian woman: - Damaris.

d: **1.** of Damascus
s: From [G1154](G1154); a *Damascene* or inhabitant of Damascus: - Damascene.

d:
Damascus = silent is the sackcloth weaver
**1.** one of the most ancient and most important cities of Syria lying in almost lovely and fertile plain at the eastern base of the Antilibanus
s: Of Hebrew origin \[[H1834](H1834)\]; *Damascus*, a city of Syria: - Damascus.

d:
**1.** to lend money
**2.** to have money lent to one’s self
**3.** to take a loan, borrow
s: From [G1156](G1156); to *loan* on interest; reflexively to *borrow:* - borrow, lend.

d: **1.** a loan
s: From δάνος danos (a *gift*); probably akin to the base of [G1325](G1325); a *loan:* - debt.

d: **1.** a money lender, creditor
s: From [G1155](G1155); a *lender:* - creditor.

d:
Daniel = judgment of God
**1.** the name of a Jewish prophet, noted for his wisdom and prophecies
s: Of Hebrew origin \[[H1840](H1840)\]; *Daniel*, an Israelite: - Daniel.

d:
**1.** to incur expense, expend, spend
**2.** in a bad sense: to waste, squander, consume
s: From [G1160](G1160); to *expend*, that is, (in a good sense) to *incur* *cost*, or (in a bad one) to *waste:* - be at charges, consume, spend.

d: **1.** expense, cost
s: From δάπτω daptō (to *devour*); *expense* (as *consuming*): - cost.

d: **1.** but, moreover, and, etc.
s: A primary particle (adversative or continuative); *but*, *and*, etc.: - also, and, but, moreover, now \[*often* *unexpressed* *in* *English*\].

d:
**1.** need, indigence, want, privation, penury
**2.** a seeking, asking, entreating, entreaty to God or to man
s: From [G1189](G1189); a *petition:* - prayer, request, supplication.

d:
**1.** it is necessary, there is need of, it behooves, is right and proper
  **a.** necessity lying in the nature of the case
  **b.** necessity brought on by circumstances or by the conduct of others toward us.
  **c.** necessity in reference to what is required to attain some end
  **d.** a necessity of law and command, of duty, equity
  **e.** necessity established by the counsel and decree of God, especially by that purpose of his which relates to the salvation of men by the intervention of christ and which is disclosed in the Old Testament prophecies
    **1.** concerning what christ was destined finally to undergo, his sufferings, death, resurrection, ascension
s: Third person singular active present of [G1210](G1210); also δεόν deon which is neuter active participle of the same; both used impersonally; *it* *is* (*was*, etc.) *necessary* (as *binding*): - behoved, be meet, must (needs), (be) need (-ful), ought, should.
o: third person singular active present of [G1210](G1210)

d:
**1.** a thing shown
**2.** a specimen of any thing, example, pattern
s: From the base of [G1166](G1166); a *specimen* (as *shown*): - example.

d: **1.** to make an example of, to show as an example
s: From [G1164](G1164); to *exhibit:* - make a shew.

d:
**1.** to show, expose to the eyes
**2.** metaph.
  **a.** to give evidence or proof of a thing
  **b.** to show by words or teach
s: A prolonged form of an obsolete primary of the same meaning; to *show* (literally or figuratively): - shew.
o: a prolonged form of an obsolete primary of the same meaning

d: **1.** timidity, fearfulness, cowardice
s: From [G1169](G1169); *timidity:* - fear.

d: **1.** to be timid, fearful
s: From [G1167](G1167); to *be* *timid:* - be afraid.

d: **1.** timid, fearful
s: From δέος deos (*dread*); *timid*, that is, (by implication) *faithless:* - fearful.

d: **1.** such a one, a certain one, i.e. one whose name I cannot call on the instant, or whose name it is of no importance to mention
s: Probably from the same as [G1171](G1171) (through the idea of forgetting the name as *fearful*, that is, *strange*); *so* *and* *so* (when the person is not specified): - such a man.
o: probably from the same as [G1171](G1171) (through the idea of forgetting the name as fearful, i.e. strange)

d: **1.** terribly, grievously
s: Adverb from a derivative of the same as [G1169](G1169); *terribly*, that is, *excessively:* - grievously, vehemently.
o: from a derivative of the same as [G1169](G1169)

d: **1.** to sup
s: From [G1173](G1173); to *dine*, that is, take the principal (or evening) meal: - sup (X -per).

d:
**1.** supper, especially a formal meal usually held at the evening,
  **a.** used of the messiah’s feast, symbolising salvation in the kingdom
**2.** food taken at evening
s: From the same as [G1160](G1160); *dinner*, that is, the chief meal (usually in the evening): - feast, supper.

d:
**1.** in a good sense
  **a.** reverencing God or the Gods, pious, religious
**2.** in a bad sense
  **a.** superstitious
s: The compound of a derivative of the base of [G1169](G1169) and [G1142](G1142); *more* *religious* than others: - too superstitious.
o: the compound of a derivative of the base of [G1169](G1169) and [G1142](G1142)

d:
**1.** in a good sense
  **a.** reverencing God or the Gods, pious, religious
**2.** in a bad sense
  **a.** superstitious
**3.** religious
s: From the same as [G1174](G1174); *religion:* - superstition.
A primary number; *ten:* - \[eight-\] een, ten.

d: **1.** twelve
s: From [G1176](G1176) and [G1417](G1417); *two* and *ten*, that is, *twelve:* - twelve.

d: **1.** fifteen
s: From [G1176](G1176) and [G4002](G4002); *ten* and *five*, that is, *fifteen:* - fifteen.

d:
Decapolis = ten cities
**1.** a track of land so called from the ten cities that were in it
  **a.** according to Pliny, these cities were: Damascus, Opoton, Philadelphia, Raphana, Scythopolis, Gadara, Hippondion, Pella, Galasa, and Canatha (Gill)
s: From [G1176](G1176) and [G4172](G4172); the *ten* *city* region; the *Decapolis*, a district in Syria: - Decapolis.

d: **1.** fourteen
s: From [G1176](G1176) and [G5064](G5064); *ten* and *four*, that is, *fourteen:* - fourteen.

d:
**1.** a tenth part of anything, a tithe
  **a.** the tenth party of booty taken from an enemy
  **b.** the tithes of fruits of the earth and of flocks, which by the law of Moses were presented to the Levites in the congregation of Israel
s: Feminine of [G1182](G1182); a *tenth*, that is, as a percentage or (technically) *tithe:* - tenth (part), tithe.

d: **1.** the tenth
s: Ordinal from [G1176](G1176); *tenth:* - tenth.

d:
**1.** to exact or receive the tenth part
**2.** to pay tithes
s: From [G1181](G1181); to *tithe*, that is, to *give* or *take* *a* *tenth:* - pay (receive) tithes.

d: **1.** accepted, acceptable
s: From [G1209](G1209); *approved*; (figuratively) *propitious:* - accepted (-table).

d:
**1.** to bait, catch by a bait
**2.** metaph. to beguile by blanishments, allure, entice, deceive
s: From the baes of [G1388](G1388); to *entrap*, that is, (figuratively) *delude:* - allure, beguile, entice.

d: **1.** a tree
s: Probably from δρύς drus (an *oak*); a *tree:* - tree.

d: **1.** throwing with the right hand, a slinger, an archer, javelinmen
s: From [G1188](G1188) and [G2983](G2983); a *guardsman* (as if *taking* *the* *right*) or light armed soldier: - spearman.

d:
**1.** the right, the right hand
**2.** metaph.
  **a.** a place of honour or authority
s: From [G1209](G1209); the *right* side or (feminine) hand (as that which usually *takes*): - right (hand, side).

d:
**1.** to want, lack
**2.** to desire, long for
**3.** to ask, beg
  **a.** the thing asked for
  **b.** to pray, make supplications
s: Middle voice of [G1210](G1210); to *beg* (as *binding* *oneself*), that is, *petition*: - beseech, pray (to), make request. Compare [G4441](G4441).

d: **1.** a native of Derbe
s: From [G1191](G1191); a *Derbaean* or inhabitant of Derbe: - of Derbe.

d:
Derbe = tanner: tanner of skin: coverer with skin
**1.** a city of Lycaonia, on the confines of Isauria
s: Of foreign origin; *Derbe*, a place in Asia Minor: - Derbe.

d: **1.** a skin, hide, leather
s: From [G1194](G1194); a *hide:* - skin.

d: **1.** made of skin, leathern
s: From [G1192](G1192); made of *hide:* - leathern, of a skin.

d:
**1.** to flay, skin
**2.** to beat, thrash, smite
s: A primary verb; properly to *flay*, that is, (by implication) to *scourge*, or (by analogy) to *thrash:* - beat, smite.

d:
**1.** to put in chains
**2.** to bind up, bind together
s: From a (presumed) derivative of [G1196](G1196); to *be* *a* *binder* (*captor*), that is, to *enchain* (a prisoner), to *tie* *on* (a load): - bind.

d: **1.** to bind, tie
s: From [G1199](G1199); to *tie*, that is, *shackle:* - bind.

d: **1.** a bundle
s: From [G1196](G1196); a *bundle:* - bundle.

d: **1.** bound, in bonds, a captive, a prisoner
s: From [G1199](G1199); a *captive* (as *bound*): - in bonds, prisoner.

d: **1.** a band or bond
s: Neuter and masculine respectively from [G1210](G1210); a *band*, that is, *ligament* (of the body) or *shackle* (of a prisoner); figuratively an *impediment* or *disability:* - band, bond, chain, string.

d: **1.** a keeper of a prison, a jailor
s: From [G1199](G1199) and [G5441](G5441); a *jailer* (as *guarding* the *prisoners*): - jailer, keeper of the prison.

d: **1.** a prison, a jail
s: From a derivative of [G1199](G1199) (equivalent to [G1196](G1196)); a *place* *of* *bondage*, that is, a *dungeon:* - prison.

d: **1.** one bound, a prisoner
s: From the same as [G1201](G1201); (passively) a *captive:* - prisoner.

d: **1.** a master, Lord
s: Perhaps from [G1210](G1210) and πόσις posis (a *husband*); an absolute *ruler* (“despot”): - Lord, master.

d:
**1.** of place,
  **a.** hither to this place
  **b.** in urging and calling, here! come!
**2.** of time, hither to, now
s: Of uncertain affinity; *here*; used also as an imperative *hither!*; and of time, *hitherto:* - come (hither), hither \[-to\].

d:
**1.** come hither, come here, come
**2.** interjection, come!, come now!
s: From [G1204](G1204) and an imperative of εἶμι eimi (to *go*); *come* *hither!*: - come, X follow.
o: from [G1204](G1204) and an imperative form of eimi (to go)

d:
**1.** of or belonging to the second
**2.** of one who comes or does a thing, on the second day
s: From [G1208](G1208); *secondary*, that is, (specifically) on the *second* day: - next day.

d:
**1.** second-first
**2.** the second of the first Sabbaths after the feast of the Passover
s: From [G1208](G1208) and [G4413](G4413); *second* *first*, that is, (specifically) a designation of the Sabbath immediately after the Paschal week (being the *second* after Passover day, and the *first* of the seven Sabbaths intervening before Pentecost): - second . . . after the first.

d: **1.** the second, the other of two
s: As the compound of [G1417](G1417); (ordinal) *second* (in time, place or rank; also adverbially): - afterward, again, second (-arily, time).

d:
**1.** to take with the hand
  **a.** to take hold of, take up
**2.** to take up, receive
  **a.** used of a place receiving one
  **b.** to receive or grant access to, a visitor, not to refuse intercourse or friendship
    **1.** to receive hospitality
    **2.** to receive into one’s family to bring up or educate
  **c.** of the thing offered in speaking, teaching, instructing
    **1.** to receive favourably, give ear to, embrace, make one’s own, approve, not to reject
  **d.** to receive. i.e. to take upon one’s self, sustain, bear, endure
**3.** to receive, get
  **a.** to learn
s: Middle voice of a primary verb; to *receive* (in various applications, literally or figuratively): - accept, receive, take. Compare [G2983](G2983).
o: middle voice of a primary verb

d:
**1.** to bind tie, fasten
  **a.** to bind, fasten with chains, to throw into chains
  **b.** metaph.
    **1.** Satan is said to bind a woman bent together by means of a demon, as his messenger, taking possession of the woman and preventing her from standing upright
    **2.** to bind, put under obligation, of the law, duty etc.
  **c.** to be bound to one, a wife, a husband
    **1.** to forbid, prohibit, declare to be illicit
s: A primary verb; to *bind* (in various applications, literally or figuratively): - bind, be in bonds, knit, tie, wind. See also [G1163](G1163), [G1189](G1189).

d:
**1.** now, then, verily, in truth, really, surely, certainly
**2.** forthwith, at once
s: Probably akin to [G1161](G1161); a particle of emphasis or explicitness; *now*, *then*, etc.: - also, and, doubtless, now, therefore.

d: **1.** clear, evident, manifest
s: Of uncertain derivation; *clear:* - + bewray, certain, evident, manifest.

d:
**1.** to make manifest
**2.** to make known by relating, to declare
**3.** to give one to understand, to indicate, signify
s: From [G1212](G1212); to *make* *plain* (by words): - declare, shew, signify.

d:
Demas = governor of the people
**1.** a companion of Paul, who deserted the apostle when he was a prisoner at Rome and returned to thessalonica
s: Probably for [G1216](G1216); *Demas*, a Christian: - Demas.

d: **1.** to address a public assembly, make a speech to the people
s: From a compound of [G1218](G1218) and [G58](G58); to *be* *a* *people* *gatherer*, that is, to *address* a public assembly: - make an oration.

d:
Demetrius = belonging to Ceres
**1.** a heathen silversmith at Ephesus
**2.** a certain Christian, 3Jn 1:12
s: From Δημήτηρ Dēmētēr (*Ceres*); *Demetrius*, the name of an Ephesian and of a Christian: - Demetrius.

d:
**1.** a workman for the public
**2.** the author of any work, an artisan, framer, builder
s: From [G1218](G1218) and [G2041](G2041); a *worker* for the *people*, that is, *mechanic* (spoken of the *Creator*): - maker.

d: **1.** the people, the mass of people assembled in a public place
s: From [G1210](G1210); the *public* (as *bound* together socially): - people.

d:
**1.** belonging to the people or state, public
**2.** publicly, in public places, in full view of all
s: From [G1218](G1218); *public*; (feminine singular dative as adverb) *in* *public:* - common, openly, publickly.

d:
denarius = containing ten
**1.** A Roman silver coin in NT time. It took its name from it being equal to ten asses, a number after 217 B.C. increased to sixteen (about 3.898 grams or .1375 oz.). It was the principal silver coin of the Roman empire. From the parable of the labourers in the vineyard, it would seem that a denarius was then the ordinary pay for a day’s wages. (Mat 20:1-16)
s: Of Latin origin; a *denarius* (or *ten* *asses*): - pence, penny \[-worth\].

d:
**1.** now at length
**2.** at any time
**3.** at last
**4.** just exactly
s: From [G1211](G1211) and [G4218](G4218); a particle of generalization; *indeed*, *at* *any* *time:* - (what-) soever.

d:
**1.** it is used when something is affirmed in a slightly ironical manner, as if with an pretence of uncertainty
  **a.** perhaps
  **b.** doubtless
  **c.** verily
  **d.** truly
s: From [G1211](G1211) and [G4225](G4225); a particle of asseveration; *indeed* *doubtless:* - verily.

d:
**1.** through
  **a.** of place
    **1.** with
    **2.** in
  **b.** of time
    **1.** throughout
    **2.** during
  **c.** of means
    **1.** by
    **2.** by the means of
**2.** through
  **a.** the ground or reason by which something is or is not done
    **1.** by reason of
    **2.** on account of
    **3.** because of for this reason
    **4.** therefore
    **5.** on this account
s: A primary preposition denoting the *channel* of an act; *through* (in very wide applications, local, causal or occasional). In composition it retains the same general import: - after, always, among, at, to avoid, because of (that), briefly, by, for (cause) . . . fore, from, in, by occasion of, of, by reason of, for sake, that, thereby, therefore, X though, through (-out), to, wherefore, with (-in). In composition it retains the same general import.
o: a primary preposition denoting the channel of an act

d: **1.** to pass through, cross over
s: From [G1223](G1223) and the base of [G939](G939); to *cross:* - come over, pass (through).

d:
**1.** to throw over or across, to send over
**2.** to traduce, calumniate, slander, accuse, defame
s: From [G1223](G1223) and [G906](G906); (figuratively) to *traduce:* - accuse.

d: **1.** to affirm strongly, assert confidently
s: Middle voice of a compound of [G1223](G1223) and [G950](G950); to *confirm* *thoroughly* (by words), that is, *asseverate:* - affirm constantly.
o: middle voice of a compound of [G1223](G1223) and [G950](G950)

d:
**1.** to look through, penetrate by vision
  **a.** to look fixedly, stare straight before one
  **b.** to see clearly
s: From [G1223](G1223) and [G991](G991); to *look* *through*, that is, *recover* full *vision:* - see clearly.

d:
**1.** prone to slander, slanderous, accusing falsely
  **a.** a calumniator, false accuser, slanderer,
**2.** metaph. applied to a man who, by opposing the cause of God, may be said to act the part of the devil or to side with him
s: From [G1225](G1225); a *traducer*; specifically *Satan* (compare \[[H7854](H7854)\]): - false accuser, devil, slanderer.

d:
**1.** to carry a message through, announce everywhere, through places, through assemblies of men etc.
**2.** to publish abroad, declare
s: From [G1223](G1223) and the base of [G32](G32); to *herald* *thoroughly:* - declare, preach, signify.

d:
**1.** to be through, continue
**2.** to be between, intervene, used of time, to have intervened, elapsed, passed meanwhile
s: From [G1223](G1223) and [G1096](G1096); to *elapse* *meanwhile:* - X after, be past, be spent.

d:
**1.** to distinguish, i.e. to know accurately, ascertain exactly
**2.** in a legal sense, to examine, determine, decide
s: From [G1223](G1223) and [G1097](G1097); to *know* *thoroughly*, that is, *ascertain* *exactly:* - (would) enquire, know the uttermost.

d:
**1.** to publish abroad, make known thoroughly
**2.** to discriminate
s: From [G1223](G1223) and [G1107](G1107); to *tell* *abroad:* - make known.

d:
**1.** to distinguish
**2.** in a legal sense, examination, opinion, decision
s: From [G1231](G1231); (magisterial) *examination* (“diagnosis”): - hearing.

d:
**1.** to murmur
  **a.** either of a whole crowd, or among one another
  **b.** always used of many indignantly complaining
s: From [G1223](G1223) and [G1111](G1111); to *complain* *throughout* a crowd: - murmur.

d:
**1.** to watch through
**2.** to remain awake
**3.** to be fully awake
s: From [G1223](G1223) and [G1127](G1127); to *waken* *thoroughly:* - be awake.

d:
**1.** to lead through, lead across, send across
**2.** to pass, to live
s: From [G1223](G1223) and [G71](G71); to *pass* time or life: - lead life, living.

d: **1.** to receive through another, anything left or bequeathed by him, to receive in succession, receive in turn, succeed to
s: From [G1223](G1223) and [G1209](G1209); to *receive* *in* *turn*, that is, (figuratively) *succeed* *to:* - come after.

d:
**1.** a diadem
  **a.** a blue band marked with white which Persian kings used to bind on the turban or tiara
  **b.** the kingly ornament for the head, the crown
s: From a compound of [G1223](G1223) and [G1210](G1210); a “diadem” (as *bound* *about* the head): - crown. Compare [G4735](G4735).

d:
**1.** to distribute, divide among several
**2.** to give over, deliver
s: From [G1223](G1223) and [G1325](G1325); to *give* *throughout* a crowd, that is, *deal* *out*; also to *deliver* over (as to a successor): - (make) distribute (-ion), divide, give.

d: **1.** succeeding, a successor
s: From [G1237](G1237); a *successor* in office: - room.

d:
**1.** to bind or gird all around
**2.** to gird one’s self with a thing, gird a thing around one’s self
s: From [G1223](G1223) and [G2224](G2224); to *gird* *tightly:* - gird.

d:
**1.** a disposition, arrangement, of any sort, which one wishes to be valid, the last disposition which one makes of his earthly possessions after his death, a testament or will
**2.** a compact, a covenant, a testament
  **a.** God’s covenant with Noah, etc.
s: From [G1303](G1303); properly a *disposition*, that is, (specifically) a *contract* (especially a devisory *will*): - covenant, testament.

d:
**1.** division, distribution
**2.** distinction, difference
  **a.** in particular, a distinction arising from a different distribution to different persons
s: From [G1244](G1244); a *distinction* or (concretely) *variety:* - difference, diversity.

d:
**1.** to divide into parts, to part, to tear, cleave or cut asunder
**2.** to distribute
s: From [G1223](G1223) and [G138](G138); to *separate*, that is, *distribute:* - divide.

d: **1.** to cleanse thoroughly
s: From [G1223](G1223) and [G2511](G2511); to *cleanse* *perfectly*, that is, (specifically) *winnow:* - throughly purge.

d: **1.** to confute with rivalry and effort or in a contest
s: Middle voice from [G1223](G1223) and a compound of [G2596](G2596) and [G1651](G1651); to *prove* *downright*, that is, *confute:* - convince.
o: middle voice from [G1223](G1223) and a compound of [G2596](G2596) and [G1651](G1651)

d:
**1.** to be a servant, attendant, domestic, to serve, wait upon
  **a.** to minister to one, render ministering offices to
    **1.** to be served, ministered unto
  **b.** to wait at a table and offer food and drink to the guests,
    **1.** of women preparing food
  **c.** to minister i.e. supply food and necessities of life
    **1.** to relieve one’s necessities (e.g. by collecting alms), to provide take care of, distribute, the things necessary to sustain life
    **2.** to take care of the poor and the sick, who administer the office of a deacon
    **3.** in Christian churches to serve as deacons
  **d.** to minister
    **1.** to attend to anything, that may serve another’s interests
    **2.** to minister a thing to one, to serve one or by supplying any thing
s: From [G1249](G1249); to *be* *an* *attendant*, that is, *wait* *upon* (menially or as a host, friend or \[figuratively\] teacher); technically to *act* *as* *a* Christian *deacon:* - (ad-) minister (unto), serve, use the office of a deacon.

d:
**1.** service, ministering, esp. of those who execute the commands of others
**2.** of those who by the command of God proclaim and promote religion among men
  **a.** of the office of Moses
  **b.** of the office of the apostles and its administration
  **c.** of the office of prophets, evangelists, elders etc.
**3.** the ministration of those who render to others the offices of Christian affection esp. those who help meet need by either collecting or distributing of charities
**4.** the office of the deacon in the church
**5.** the service of those who prepare and present food
s: From [G1249](G1249); *attendance* (as a servant, etc.); figuratively (eleemosynary) *aid*, (official) *service* (especially of the Christian teacher, or technically of the *diaconate*): - (ad-) minister (-ing, -tration, -try), office, relief, service (-ing).

d:
**1.** one who executes the commands of another, esp. of a master, a servant, attendant, minister
  **a.** the servant of a king
  **b.** a deacon, one who, by virtue of the office assigned to him by the church, cares for the poor and has charge of and distributes the money collected for their use
  **c.** a waiter, one who serves food and drink
s: Probably from διάκω diakō (obsolete, to *run* on errands; compare [G1377](G1377)); an *attendant*, that is, (generally) a *waiter* (at table or in other menial duties); specifically a Christian *teacher* and *pastor* (technically a *deacon* or *deaconess*): - deacon, minister, servant.
o: probably from an obsolete diako (to run on errands, cf [G1377](G1377))

d: **1.** two hundred
s: From [G1364](G1364) and [G1540](G1540); *two* *hundred:* - two hundred.

d: **1.** to hear one through, hear to the end, hear with care, hear fully
s: Middle voice from [G1223](G1223) and [G191](G191); to *hear* *throughout*, that is, *patiently* *listen* (to a prisoner’s plea): - hear.

d:
**1.** to separate, make a distinction, discriminate, to prefer
**2.** to learn by discrimination, to try, decide
  **a.** to determine, give judgment, decide a dispute
**3.** to withdraw from one, desert
**4.** to separate one’s self in a hostile spirit, to oppose, strive with dispute, contend
**5.** to be at variance with one’s self, hesitate, doubt
s: From [G1223](G1223) and [G2919](G2919); to *separate* *thoroughly*, that is, (literally and reflexively) to *withdraw* from, or (by implication) *oppose*; figuratively to *discriminate* (by implication *decide*), or (reflexively) *hesitate:* - contend, make (to) differ (-ence), discern, doubt, judge, be partial, stagger, waver.

d: **1.** a distinguishing, discerning, judging
s: From [G1252](G1252); judicial *estimation:* - discern (-ing), disputation.

d: **1.** to hinder, prevent
s: From [G1223](G1223) and [G2967](G2967); to *hinder* *altogether*, that is, *utterly* *prohibit:* - forbid.

d: **1.** to converse together, to talk with
s: From [G1223](G1223) and [G2980](G2980); to *talk* *throughout* a company, that is, *converse* or (generally) *publish:* - commune, noise abroad.

d:
**1.** to think different things with one’s self, mingle thought with thought
  **a.** to ponder, revolve in mind
**2.** to converse, discourse with one, argue, discuss
s: Middle voice from [G1223](G1223) and [G3004](G3004); to *say* *thoroughly*, that is, *discuss* (in argument or exhortation): - dispute, preach (unto), reason (with), speak.

d: **1.** to interpose a delay, to intermit, leave off for a time something already begun
s: From [G1223](G1223) and [G3007](G3007); to *leave* *off* *in* *the* *middle*, that is, *intermit:* - cease.

d:
**1.** conversation, speech, discourse, language
**2.** the tongue or language peculiar to any people
s: From [G1256](G1256); a (mode of) *discourse*, that is, “dialect”: - language, tongue.

d:
**1.** to change
**2.** to change the mind of anyone, to reconcile
**3.** to be reconciled, to renew friendship with one
s: From [G1223](G1223) and [G236](G236); to *change* *thoroughly*, that is, (mentally) to *conciliate:* - reconcile.

d: **1.** to bring together different reasons, to reckon up the reasons, to reason, revolve in one’s mind, deliberate
s: From [G1223](G1223) and [G3049](G3049); to *reckon* *thoroughly*, that is, (generally) to *deliberate* (by reflection or discussion): - cast in mind, consider, dispute, muse, reason, think.

d:
**1.** the thinking of a man deliberating with himself
  **a.** a thought, inward reasoning
  **b.** purpose, design
**2.** a deliberating, questioning about what is true
  **a.** hesitation, doubting
  **b.** disputing, arguing
s: From [G1260](G1260); *discussion*, that is, (internal) *consideration* (by implication *purpose*), or (external) *debate:* - dispute, doubtful (-ing), imagination, reasoning, thought.

d: **1.** to dissolve
s: From [G1223](G1223) and [G3089](G3089); to *dissolve* *utterly:* - scatter.

d:
**1.** to testify
  **a.** earnestly, religiously to charge
**2.** to attest, testify to, solemnly affirm
  **a.** to give solemn testimony to one
  **b.** to confirm a thing by testimony, to testify, cause it to be believed
s: From [G1223](G1223) and [G3140](G3140); to *attest* or *protest* *earnestly*, or (by implication) *hortatively:* - charge, testify (unto), witness.

d:
**1.** to fight out
**2.** contend fiercely
s: From [G1223](G1223) and [G3164](G3164); to *fight* *fiercely* (in altercation): - strive.

d: **1.** to stay permanently, remain permanently, continue
s: From [G1223](G1223) and [G3306](G3306); to *stay* *constantly* (in being or relation): - continue, remain.

d:
**1.** to cleave asunder, cut in pieces
**2.** to be divided into opposing parts, to be at variance, in dissension
**3.** to distribute
s: From [G1223](G1223) and [G3307](G3307); to *partition* *thoroughly* (literally in distribution, figuratively in dissension): - cloven, divide, part.

d:
**1.** a parting, distribution
**2.** disunion, dissension
s: From [G1266](G1266); *disunion* (of opinion and conduct): - division.

d: **1.** to distribute, divide
s: From [G1223](G1223) and the base of [G3551](G3551); to *distribute*, that is, (of information) to *disseminate:* - spread.

d: **1.** to express one’s meaning by a sign, nod to, beckon to, wink at
s: From [G1223](G1223) and [G3506](G3506); to *nod* (or *express* by signs) *across* an intervening space: - beckon.

d: **1.** a thought
s: From a compound of [G1223](G1223) and [G3539](G3539); something *thought* *through*, that is, a *sentiment:* - thought.

d:
**1.** the mind as a faculty of understanding, feeling, desiring
**2.** understanding
**3.** mind, i.e. spirit, way of thinking and feeling
**4.** thoughts, either good or bad
s: From [G1223](G1223) and [G3563](G3563); *deep* *thought*, properly the faculty (*mind* or its *disposition*), by implication its exercise: - imagination, mind, understanding.

d:
**1.** to open by dividing or drawing asunder, to open thoroughly (what had been closed)
  **a.** a male opening the womb (the closed matrix), i.e. the first-born
  **b.** of the eyes and the ears
  **c.** to open the mind of one, i.e. to cause to understand a thing
    **1.** to open one’s soul, i.e. to rouse in one the faculty of understanding or the desire of learning
s: From [G1223](G1223) and [G455](G455); to *open* *thoroughly*, literally (as a first born) or figuratively (to *expound*): - open.

d: **1.** to spend the night, to pass the whole night
s: From [G1223](G1223) and a derivative of [G3571](G3571); to *sit* *up* *the* *whole* *night:* - continue all night.

d: **1.** to accomplish fully, bring quite to an end, finish
s: From [G1223](G1223) and ἀνύω anuō (to *effect*); to *accomplish* *thoroughly:* - finish.

d: **1.** constantly, always, continually
s: From [G1223](G1223) and the genitive of [G3956](G3956); *through* *all* time, that is, (adverbially) *constantly:* - alway (-s), continually.

d: **1.** to pass over, cross over, i.e. a river, a lake
s: From [G1223](G1223) and a derivative of the base of [G4008](G4008); to *cross* *entirely:* - go over, pass (over), sail over.
o: from [G1223](G1223) and a derivative of the base of [G4008](G4008)

d: **1.** to sail across
s: From [G1223](G1223) and [G4126](G4126); to *sail* *through:* - sail over.

d:
**1.** to work out laboriously, make complete by labour
  **a.** to exert one’s self, strive
  **b.** to manage with pains, accomplish with great labour
  **c.** to be troubled, displeased, offended, pained, to be worked up
s: From [G1223](G1223) and a derivative of [G4192](G4192); to *toil* *through*, that is, (passively) *be* *worried:* - be grieved.

d:
**1.** to cause to pass through a place
**2.** to carry across
**3.** to journey through a place, go through
**4.** to travel through
s: From [G1223](G1223) and [G4198](G4198); to *travel* *through:* - go through, journey in, pass by.

d: **1.** to be entirely at loss, to be in perplexity
s: From [G1223](G1223) and [G639](G639); to *be* *thoroughly* *nonplussed:* - (be in) doubt, be (much) perplexed.

d:
**1.** thoroughly, earnestly to undertake a business
**2.** to undertake a business for sake of gain
s: From [G1223](G1223) and [G4231](G4231); to *thoroughly* *occupy* *oneself*, that is, (transitively and by implication) to *earn* in business: - gain by trading.

d:
**1.** to saw asunder or in two, to divide by a saw
**2.** to be sawn through mentally, i.e. to be rent with vexation
s: From [G1223](G1223) and the base of [G4249](G4249); to *saw* *asunder*, that is, (figuratively) to *exasperate:* - cut (to the heart).

d: **1.** to plunder
s: From [G1223](G1223) and [G726](G726); to *seize* *asunder*, that is, *plunder:* - spoil.

d:
**1.** to break asunder, burst through, rend asunder
**2.** to rend, which was done by the Jews to their clothes in cases of extreme indignation or in deep grief
s: From [G1223](G1223) and [G4486](G4486); to *tear* *asunder:* - break, rend.

d:
**1.** to make clear or plain, to explain, unfold, declare
**2.** of things done, to declare i.e. to tell, announce, narrate
s: From [G1223](G1223) andσαφής saphēs (*clear*); to *clear* *thoroughly*, that is, (figuratively) *declare:* - tell unto.

d:
**1.** to shake thoroughly
**2.** to make to tremble
**3.** to terrify
**4.** to agitate
**5.** to extort from one by intimidation money or other property
s: From [G1223](G1223) and [G4579](G4579); to *shake* *thoroughly*, that is, (figuratively) to *intimidate:* - do violence to.

d:
**1.** to scatter abroad, disperse, to winnow
  **a.** to throw the grain a considerable distance, or up into the air, that it may be separated from the chaff
  **b.** to gather the wheat, freed from the chaff into the granary
  **c.** to winnow grain
s: From [G1223](G1223) and [G4650](G4650); to *dissipate*, that is, (generally) to *rout* or *separate*; specifically to *winnow*; figuratively to *squander:* - disperse, scatter (abroad), strew, waste.

d:
**1.** to rend asunder, break asunder
  **a.** of a man, to tear in pieces
s: From [G1223](G1223) and [G4685](G4685); to *draw* *apart*, that is, *sever* or *dismember:* - pluck asunder, pull in pieces.

d: **1.** to scatter abroad, disperse
s: From [G1223](G1223) and [G4687](G4687); to *sow* *throughout*, that is, (figuratively) *distribute* in foreign lands: - scatter abroad.

d:
**1.** a scattering, dispersion
  **a.** of Israelites dispersed among foreign nations
  **b.** of the Christians scattered abroad among the Gentiles
s: From [G1289](G1289); *dispersion*, that is, (specifically and concretely) the (converted) Israelites *resident* in Gentile countries: - (which are) scattered (abroad).

d:
**1.** to draw asunder, divide, distinguish, dispose, order
**2.** to open one’s self i.e. one’s mind, to set forth distinctly
**3.** to admonish, order, charge
s: Middle voice from [G1223](G1223) and [G4724](G4724); to *set* (oneself) *apart* (figuratively *distinguish*), that is, (by implication) to *enjoin:* - charge, that which was (give) commanded (-ment).

d: **1.** an interval, distance, space of time
s: From [G1339](G1339); an *interval:* - space.

d:
**1.** a distinction, difference
  **a.** of the different sounds musical instruments make
s: From [G1291](G1291); a *variation:* - difference, distinction.

d:
**1.** to distort, turn aside
  **a.** to oppose, plot against the saving purposes and plans of God
**2.** to turn aside from the right path, to pervert, corrupt
s: From [G1223](G1223) and [G4762](G4762); to *distort*, that is, (figuratively) *misinterpret*, or (morally) *corrupt:* - perverse (-rt), turn away.

d:
**1.** to preserve through danger, to bring safely through
  **a.** to save, i.e. cure one who is sick, bring him through
**2.** to save, keep from perishing
**3.** to save out of danger, rescue
s: From [G1223](G1223) and [G4982](G4982); to *save* *thoroughly*, that is, (by implication or analogy) to *cure*, *preserve*, *rescue*, etc.: - bring safe, escape (safe), heal, make perfectly whole, save.

d: **1.** a disposition, arrangement, ordinance
s: From [G1299](G1299); *arrangement*, that is, *institution:* - instrumentality.

d: **1.** an injunction, mandate
s: From [G1299](G1299); an *arrangement*, that is, (authoritative) *edict:* - commandment.

d: **1.** to agitate greatly, trouble greatly
s: From [G1223](G1223) and [G5015](G5015); to *disturb* *wholly*, that is, *agitate* (with alarm): - trouble.

d: **1.** to arrange, appoint, ordain, prescribe, give order
s: From [G1223](G1223) and [G5021](G5021); to *arrange* *thoroughly*, that is, (specifically) *institute*, *prescribe*, etc.: - appoint, command, give, (set in) order, ordain.

d: **1.** to bring thoroughly to an end, accomplish
s: From [G1223](G1223) and [G5055](G5055); to *accomplish* *thoroughly*, that is, (subjectively) to *persist:* - continue.

d: **1.** to keep continually or carefully
s: From [G1223](G1223) and [G5083](G5083); to *watch* *thoroughly*, that is, (positively and transitively) to *observe* strictly, or (negatively and reflexively) to *avoid* wholly: - keep.

d: **1.** through, by, with, because of, for the sake of
s: From [G1223](G1223) and [G5101](G5101); *through* *what* cause?, that is, *why?*: - wherefore, why.

d:
**1.** to arrange, dispose of, one’s own affairs
  **a.** of something that belongs to one
  **b.** to dispose of by will, make a testament
**2.** to make a covenant, enter into a covenant, with one
s: Middle voice from [G1223](G1223) and [G5087](G5087); to *put* *apart*, that is, (figuratively) *dispose* (by assignment, compact or bequest): - appoint, make, testator.

d:
**1.** to rub between, rub hard
**2.** to wear away, consume
**3.** to spend, pass time
s: From [G1223](G1223) and the base of [G5147](G5147); to *wear* *through* (time), that is, *remain:* - abide, be, continue, tarry.

d: **1.** sustenance
s: From a compound of [G1223](G1223) and [G5142](G5142); *nourishment:* - food.

d:
**1.** to shine through, to dawn
  **a.** of daylight breaking through the darkness of night
s: From [G1223](G1223) and [G826](G826); to *glimmer* *through*, that is, *break* (as day): - dawn.

d: **1.** transparent, translucent
s: From [G1223](G1223) and [G5316](G5316); *appearing* *through*, that is, “diaphanous”: - transparent.

d:
**1.** to bear or carry through any place
**2.** to carry different ways
  **a.** to carry in different directions, to different places
    **1.** of people who are carried hither and thither in a ship, driven to and fro
  **b.** to differ, to test, prove, the good things that differ,
    **1.** to distinguish between good and evil, lawful and unlawful, to approve of things that excel, to differ from one
    **2.** to excel, surpass one
  **c.** impersonally, it makes a difference, it matters, is of importance
s: From [G1223](G1223) and [G5342](G5342); to *bear* *through*, that is, (literally) *transport*; usually to *bear* *apart*, that is, (objectively) to *toss* *about* (figuratively *report*); subjectively to *“differ”*, or (by implication) *surpass:* - be better, carry, differ from, drive up and down, be (more) excellent, make matter, publish, be of more value.

d: **1.** to flee through danger, to escape
s: From [G1223](G1223) and [G5343](G5343); to *flee* *through*, that is, *escape:* - escape.

d:
**1.** to spread abroad, blaze abroad
**2.** to spread abroad his fame or renown
s: From [G1223](G1223) and a derivative of [G5345](G5345); to *report* *thoroughly*, that is, *divulgate:* - blaze abroad, commonly report, spread abroad, fame.

d:
**1.** to change for the worse, to corrupt
  **a.** of minds, morals
**2.** to destroy, ruin
  **a.** to consume
    **1.** of bodily vigour and strength
    **2.** of the worm or moth that eats provisions, clothing, etc.
  **b.** to destroy, to kill
s: From [G1223](G1223) and [G5351](G5351); to *rot* *thoroughly*, that is, (by implication) to *ruin* (passively *decay* utterly, figuratively *pervert*): - corrupt, destroy, perish.

d:
**1.** corruption, destruction
**2.** in the NT that destruction which is effected by the decay of the body after death
s: From [G1311](G1311); *decay:* - corruption.

d:
**1.** different, varying in kind
**2.** excellent, surpassing
s: From [G1308](G1308); *varying*; also *surpassing:* - differing, divers, more excellent.

d:
**1.** to guard carefully
  **a.** the LXX used this esp. of God’s providential care
s: From [G1223](G1223) and [G5442](G5442); to *guard* *thoroughly*, that is, *protect:* - keep.

d:
**1.** to move by the use of the hands, take in hand, manage, administer, govern
**2.** to lay hands on, slay, kill \[with one’s own hand\]
s: From [G1223](G1223) and a derivative of [G5495](G5495); to *handle* *thoroughly*, that is, *lay* violent *hands* upon: - kill, slay.

d:
**1.** to separate thoroughly or wholly
**2.** to separate one’s self, depart
s: From [G1223](G1223) and the middle voice of [G5563](G5563); to *remove* (oneself) *wholly*, that is, *retire:* - depart.
o: from [G1223](G1223) and the middle voice of [G5563](G5563)

d: **1.** apt and skilful in teaching
s: From [G1318](G1318); *instructive* (“didactic”): - apt to teach.

d:
**1.** that can be taught
**2.** taught, instructed by one
**3.** teachings, precepts
s: From [G1321](G1321); (subjectively) *instructed* or (objectively) *communicated* by teaching: - taught, which . . . teacheth.

d:
**1.** teaching, instruction
**2.** teaching
  **a.** that which is taught, doctrine
  **b.** teachings, precepts
s: From [G1320](G1320); *instruction* (the function or the information): - doctrine, learning, teaching.

d:
**1.** a teacher
**2.** in the NT one who teaches concerning the things of God, and the duties of man
  **a.** one who is fitted to teach, or thinks himself so
  **b.** the teachers of the Jewish religion
  **c.** of those who by their great power as teachers draw crowds around them i.e. John the Baptist, Jesus
  **d.** by preeminence used of Jesus by himself, as one who showed men the way of salvation
  **e.** of the apostles, and of Paul
  **f.** of those who in the religious assemblies of the Christians, undertook the work of teaching, with the special assistance of the holy spirit
  **g.** of false teachers among Christians
s: From [G1321](G1321); an *instructor* (generally or specifically): - doctor, master, teacher.

d:
**1.** to teach
  **a.** to hold discourse with others in order to instruct them, deliver didactic discourses
  **b.** to be a teacher
  **c.** to discharge the office of a teacher, conduct one’s self as a teacher
**2.** to teach one
  **a.** to impart instruction
  **b.** instill doctrine into one
  **c.** the thing taught or enjoined
  **d.** to explain or expound a thing
  **e.** to teach one something
s: A prolonged (causative) form of a primary verb δάω daō (to *learn*); to *teach* (in the same broad application): - teach.
o: a prolonged (causative) form of a primary verb dao (to learn)

d:
**1.** teaching
  **a.** that which is taught
  **b.** doctrine, teaching, concerning something
**2.** the act of teaching, instruction
  **a.** in religious assemblies of the Christians, to speak in the way of teaching, in distinction from other modes of speaking in public
s: From [G1321](G1321); *instruction* (the act or the matter): - doctrine, hath been taught.

d: **1.** a didrachmon or double drachma, a silver coin equal to two Attic drachmas or one Alexandrian, or one half a shekel
s: From [G1364](G1364) and [G1406](G1406); a *double* *drachma* (*didrachm*): - tribute.

d:
Didymus = two fold or twain
**1.** a surname for the apostle Thomas
s: Prolonged from [G1364](G1364); *double*, that is, *twin*; *Didymus*, a Christian: - Didymus.

d:
**1.** to give
**2.** to give something to someone
  **a.** of one’s own accord to give one something, to his advantage
    **1.** to bestow a gift
  **b.** to grant, give to one asking, let have
  **c.** to supply, furnish, necessary things
  **d.** to give over, deliver
    **1.** to reach out, extend, present
    **2.** of a writing
    **3.** to give over to one’s care, intrust, commit
  **e.** something to be administered
  **f.** to give or commit to some one something to be religiously observed
  **g.** to give what is due or obligatory, to pay: wages or reward
  **h.** to furnish, endue
**3.** to give
  **a.** to cause, profuse, give forth from one’s self
    **1.** to give, hand out lots
  **b.** to appoint to an office
  **c.** to cause to come forth, i.e. as the sea, death and hell are said to give up the dead who have been engulfed or received by them
  **d.** to give one to someone as his own
    **1.** as an object of his saving care
    **2.** to give one to someone, to follow him as a leader and master
    **3.** to give one to someone to care for his interests
    **4.** to give one to someone to whom he already belonged, to return
**4.** to grant or permit one
  **a.** to commission
s: A prolonged form of a primary verb (which is used as an alternate in most of the tenses); to *give* (used in a very wide application, properly or by implication, literally or figuratively; greatly modified by the connection): - adventure, bestow, bring forth, commit, deliver (up), give, grant, hinder, make, minister, number, offer, have power, put, receive, set, shew, smite (+ with the hand), strike (+ with the palm of the hand), suffer, take, utter, yield.
o: a prolonged form of a primary verb (which is used as an altern. in most of the tenses)

d:
**1.** to wake up, awaken, arouse (from sleep)
  **a.** of the sea, which begins to be agitated, to rise
  **b.** metaph.
    **1.** to arouse the mind
    **2.** stir up, render active
s: From [G1223](G1223) and [G1453](G1453); to *wake* *fully*, that is, *arouse* (literally or figuratively): - arise, awake, raise, stir up.

d:
**1.** a way out through, outlet, exit
  **a.** literally the ways through which ways go out
  **b.** the places before the city where the roads from the country terminate, therefore outlets of the country highways, also entrances into the city
  **c.** of boundaries of countries
s: From [G1223](G1223) and [G1841](G1841); an *outlet* *through*, that is, probably an open *square* (from which roads diverge): - highway.

d: **1.** an interpreter
s: From [G1329](G1329); an *explainer:* - interpreter.

d:
**1.** to unfold the meaning of what is said, explain, expound
**2.** to translate into one’s native language
s: From [G1223](G1223) and [G2059](G2059); to *explain* *thoroughly*; by implication to *translate:* - expound, interpret (-ation).

d:
**1.** to go through, pass through
  **a.** to go, walk, journey, pass through a place
  **b.** to travel the road which leads through a place, go, pass, travel through a region
**2.** to go different places
  **a.** of people, to go abroad
  **b.** of a report, to spread, go abroad
s: From [G1223](G1223) and [G2064](G2064); to *traverse* (literally): - come, depart, go (about, abroad, every where, over, through, throughout), pass (by, over, through, throughout), pierce through, travel, walk through.

d:
**1.** to ask through
  **a.** ask many, one after another
  **b.** to find out by asking, enquire out
s: From [G1223](G1223) and [G2065](G2065); to *question* *throughout*, that is, *ascertain* by interrogation: - make enquiry for.

d: **1.** of two years, two years old
s: From [G1364](G1364) and [G2094](G2094); *of* *two* *years* (in age): - two years old.

d: **1.** the space of two years
s: From [G1332](G1332); a space of *two* *years* (*biennium*): - two years.

d:
**1.** to lead or carry a narration through to the end
**2.** set forth, recount, relate in full, describe
s: From [G1223](G1223) and [G2233](G2233); to *relate* *fully:* - declare, shew, tell.

d: **1.** a narration, narrative
s: From [G1334](G1334); a *recital:* - declaration.

d: **1.** continuously, continuous
s: Neuter of a compound of [G1223](G1223) and a derivative of an alternate of [G5342](G5342); *carried* *through*, that is, (adverb with [G1519](G1519) and [G3588](G3588) prefixed) *perpetually:* - +continually, for ever.
o: neuter of a compound of [G1223](G1223) and a derivative of an alternate of [G5342](G5342)

d:
**1.** resembling or forming two seas: thus of the Euxine Sea
**2.** lying between two seas, i.e. washed on both sides by the sea
  **a.** an isthmus or tongue of land, the extremity of which is covered by the waves
  **b.** a projecting reef or bar against which the waves dash on both sides
s: From [G1364](G1364) and [G2281](G2281); *having* *two* *seas*, that is, a *sound* with a double outlet: - where two seas met.

d: **1.** to go through, penetrate, pierce
s: From [G1223](G1223) and the base of [G2425](G2425); to *reach* *through*, that is, *penetrate:* - pierce.

d:
**1.** to place separately, put asunder, disjoin
**2.** to stand apart, to part, depart
s: From [G1223](G1223) and [G2476](G2476); to *stand* *apart*, that is, (reflexively) to *remove*, *intervene:* - go further, be parted, after the space of.

d:
**1.** to lean upon
**2.** to affirm stoutly, assert confidently
s: From [G1223](G1223) and a derivative of [G2478](G2478); to *stout* it *through*, that is, *asseverate:* - confidently (constantly) affirm.

d: **1.** righteous judgment
s: From [G1342](G1342) and [G2920](G2920); a *just* *sentence:* - righteous judgment.

d:
**1.** righteous, observing divine laws
  **a.** in a wide sense, upright, righteous, virtuous, keeping the commands of God
    **1.** of those who seem to themselves to be righteous, who pride themselves to be righteous, who pride themselves in their virtues, whether real or imagined
    **2.** innocent, faultless, guiltless
    **3.** used of him whose way of thinking, feeling, and acting is wholly conformed to the will of God, and who therefore needs no rectification in the heart or life
  **b.** only christ truly
    **1.** approved of or acceptable of God
  **c.** in a narrower sense, rendering to each his due and that in a judicial sense, passing just judgment on others, whether expressed in words or shown by the manner of dealing with them
s: From [G1349](G1349); *equitable* (in character or act); by implication *innocent*, *holy* (absolutely or relatively): - just, meet, right (-eous).

d:
**1.** in a broad sense: state of him who is as he ought to be, righteousness, the condition acceptable to God
  **a.** the doctrine concerning the way in which man may attain a state approved of God
  **b.** integrity, virtue, purity of life, rightness, correctness of thinking feeling, and acting
**2.** in a narrower sense, justice or the virtue which gives each his due
s: From [G1342](G1342); *equity* (of character or act); specifically (Christian) *justification:* - righteousness.

d:
**1.** to render righteous or such he ought to be
**2.** to show, exhibit, evince, one to be righteous, such as he is and wishes himself to be considered
**3.** to declare, pronounce, one to be just, righteous, or such as he ought to be
s: From [G1342](G1342); to *render* (that is, *show* or *regard* as) *just* or *innocent:* - free, justify (-ier), be righteous.

d:
**1.** that which has been deemed right so as to have force of law
  **a.** what has been established, and ordained by law, an ordinance
  **b.** a judicial decision, sentence
    **1.** of God
  **c.** either the favourable judgment by which he acquits man and declares them acceptable to him
  **d.** unfavourable: sentence of condemnation
**2.** a righteous act or deed
s: From [G1344](G1344); an *equitable* *deed*; by implication a *statute* or *decision:* - judgment, justification, ordinance, righteousness.

d:
**1.** just, agreeably to right
**2.** properly, as is right
**3.** uprightly, agreeable to the law of rectitude
s: Adverb from [G1342](G1342); *equitably:* - justify, (to) righteously (-ness).

d:
**1.** the act of God declaring men free from guilt and acceptable to him
**2.** abjuring to be righteous, justification
s: From [G1344](G1344); *acquittal* (for Christ’s sake): - justification.

d: **1.** a judge, arbitrator, umpire
s: From a derivative of [G1349](G1349); a *judger:* - judge.

d:
**1.** custom, usage
**2.** right, just
**3.** a suit at law
**4.** a judicial hearing, judicial decision, esp. sentence of condemnation
**5.** execution of a sentence, punishment
  **a.** to suffer punishment
**6.** the Goddess justice, avenging justice
s: Probably from [G1166](G1166); *right* (as self *evident*), that is, *justice* (the principle, a decision, or its execution): - judgment, punish, vengeance.

d: **1.** a net
s: Probably from a primary verb δίκω dikō (to *cast*); a *seine* (for fishing): - net.
o: probably from a primary verb diko (to cast)

d:
**1.** saying the same thing twice, repeating
**2.** double tongued, double in speech, saying one thing with one person another with another (with the intent to deceive)
s: From [G1364](G1364) and [G3056](G3056); *equivocal*, that is, telling a different story: - double-tongued.

d: **1.** wherefore, on account off
s: From [G1223](G1223) and [G3739](G3739); *through* *which* thing, that is, *consequently:* - for which cause, therefore, wherefore.

d:
**1.** to pass or travel through
**2.** to travel here and there, go about
s: From [G1223](G1223) and [G3593](G3593); to *travel* *through:* - go throughout, pass through.

d: Dionysius = devoted to Bacchus
s: From Διόνυσος Dionusos (*Bacchus*); *reveller*; *Dionysius*, an Athenian: - Dionysius.

d: **1.** on which very account
s: From [G1352](G1352) and [G4007](G4007); *on* *which* *very* *account:* - wherefore.

d:
**1.** fallen from Zeus, i.e. from heaven
**2.** an image of the Ephesian Artemis which was supposed to have fallen from heaven
s: From the alternate of [G2203](G2203) and the alternate of [G4098](G4098); *sky* *fallen* (that is, an *aerolite*): - which fell down from Jupiter.
o: from the alternate of [G2203](G2203) and the alternate of [G4098](G4098)

d:
**1.** in a physical sense, a making straight, restoring to its natural and normal condition something which in some way protrudes or has got out of line, as broken or misshapen limbs
**2.** of acts and institutions, reformation
s: From a compound of [G1223](G1223) and a derivative of [G3717](G3717), meaning to *straighten* *thoroughly*; *rectification*, that is, (specifically) the Messianic restoration: - reformation.
o: from a compound of [G1223](G1223) and a derivative of [G3717](G3717), meaning to straighten thoroughly

d: **1.** to dig through: a house
s: From [G1223](G1223) and [G3736](G3736); to penetrate burglariously: - break through (up).

d: **1.** Castor and Pollux, were the twin sons of Jupiter and Leda, and were regarded as the tutelary divinities of sailors
s: From the alternate of [G2203](G2203) and a form of the base of [G2877](G2877); sons of Jupiter, that is, the twins *Dioscuri:* - Castor and Pollux.
o: from the alternate of [G2203](G2203) and a form of the base of [G2877](G2877)

d:
**1.** on this account that, because
**2.** for
s: From [G1223](G1223) and [G3754](G3754); *on* *the* *very* *account* *that*, or *inasmuch* *as:* - because (that), for, therefore.

d:
Diotrephes = nourished by Jove
**1.** a proud arrogant Christian mentioned in 3Jn 1:9
s: From the alternate of [G2203](G2203) and [G5142](G5142); *Jove* *nourished*; *Diotrephes*, an opponent of Christianity: - Diotrephes.

d: **1.** twofold, double
s: From [G1364](G1364) and (probably) the base of [G4119](G4119); *two* *fold:* - double, two-fold more.

d: **1.** to double
s: From [G1362](G1362); to *render* *two* *fold:* - double.

d: **1.** twice
s: Adverb from [G1417](G1417); *twice:* - again, twice.

d: **1.** to doubt, waiver
s: From [G1364](G1364) properly to *duplicate*, that is, (mentally) to *waver* (in opinion): - doubt.

d:
**1.** having a double mouth as a river
  **a.** used of the edge of the sword and of other weapons, so has the meaning of two-edged
s: From [G1364](G1364) and [G4750](G4750); *double* *edged:* - with two edges, two-edged.

d: **1.** two thousand
s: From [G1364](G1364) and [G5507](G5507); *two* *thousand:* - two thousand.

d: **1.** to filter through, strain through, pour through a filter, strain out
s: From [G1223](G1223) and ὑλίζω hulizō (to *filter*); to *strain* *out*. (“strain at” is probably by misprint.): - strain at \[prob. by misprint\].

d: **1.** to cut into two parts, cleave asunder, sever
s: From a derivative of [G1364](G1364); to *make* *apart*, that is, *sunder* (figuratively *alienate*): - set at variance.

d: **1.** dissension, division
s: From a derivative of [G1364](G1364) and [G4714](G4714); *disunion*, that is, (figuratively) *dissension:* - division, sedition.

d:
**1.** to cut into two parts
  **a.** of the cruel method of punishment used by the hebrews and others of cutting one in two
**2.** cut up by scourging, scourge severely
s: From a compound of a derivative of [G1364](G1364) and a derivative of τέμνω temnō (to *cut*); to *bisect*, that is, (by extension) to *flog* severely: - cut asunder (in sunder).
o: from a compound of a derivative of [G1364](G1364) and a derivative of temno (to cut)

d:
**1.** to suffer thirst, suffer from thirst
  **a.** figuratively, those who are said to thirst who painfully feel their want of, and eagerly long for, those things by which the soul is refreshed, supported, strengthened
s: From a variation of [G1373](G1373); to *thirst* for (literally or figuratively): - (be, be a-) thirst (-y).

d: **1.** thirst
s: Of uncertain affinity; *thirst:* - thirst.

d:
**1.** double minded
  **a.** wavering, uncertain, doubting
  **b.** divided in interest
s: From [G1364](G1364) and [G5590](G5590); *two* *spirited*, that is, *vacillating* (in opinion or purpose): - double minded.

d: **1.** persecution
s: From [G1377](G1377); *persecution:* - persecution.

d: **1.** persecutor
s: From [G1377](G1377); a *persecutor:* - persecutor.

d:
**1.** to make to run or flee, put to flight, drive away
**2.** to run swiftly in order to catch a person or thing, to run after
  **a.** to press on: figuratively of one who in a race runs swiftly to reach the goal
  **b.** to pursue (in a hostile manner)
**3.** in any way whatever to harass, trouble, molest one
  **a.** to persecute
  **b.** to be mistreated, suffer persecution on account of something
**4.** without the idea of hostility, to run after, follow after: someone
**5.** metaph., to pursue
  **a.** to seek after eagerly, earnestly endeavour to acquire
s: A prolonged (and causative) form of a primary verb δίω diō (to *flee*; compare the base of [G1169](G1169) and [G1249](G1249)); to *pursue* (literally or figuratively); by implication to *persecute:* - ensue, follow (after), given to, (suffer) persecute (-ion), press toward.
o: a prolonged (and causative) form of a primary verb dio (to flee; cf the base of [G1169](G1169) and [G1249](G1249))

d:
**1.** doctrine, decree, ordinance
  **a.** of public decrees
  **b.** of the Roman Senate
  **c.** of rulers
**2.** the rules and requirements of the law of Moses; carrying a suggestion of severity and of threatened judgment
**3.** of certain decrees of the apostles relative to right living
s: From the base of [G1380](G1380); a *law* (civil, ceremonial or ecclesiastical): - decree, ordinance.

d: **1.** to decree, command, enjoin, lay down an ordinance
s: From [G1378](G1378); to *prescribe* by statute, that is, (reflexively) to *submit* *to* ceremonial *rule:* - be subject to ordinances.

d:
**1.** to be of opinion, think, suppose
**2.** to seem, to be accounted, reputed
**3.** it seems to me
  **a.** I think, judge: thus in question
  **b.** it seems good to, pleased me, I determined
s: A prolonged form of a primary verb δόκω dokō (used only as an alternate in certain tenses; compare the base of [G1166](G1166)); of the same meaning; to *think*; by implication to *seem* (truthfully or uncertainly): - be accounted, (of own) please (-ure), be of reputation, seem (good), suppose, think, trow.
o: a prolonged form of a primary verb, doko dok’-o (used only in an alternate in certain tenses; cf the base of [G1166](G1166)) of the same meaning

d:
**1.** to test, examine, prove, scrutinise (to see whether a thing is genuine or not), as metals
**2.** to recognise as genuine after examination, to approve, deem worthy
s: From [G1384](G1384); to *test* (literally or figuratively); by implication to *approve:* - allow, discern, examine, X like, (ap-) prove, try.

d:
**1.** proving, trial
**2.** approved, tried character
**3.** a proof, a specimen of tried worth
s: From the same as [G1384](G1384); *test* (abstractly or concretely); by implication *trustiness:* - experience (-riment), proof, trial.

d:
**1.** the proving
**2.** that by which something is tried or proved, a test
s: Neuter of a presumed derivative of [G1382](G1382); a *testing*; by implication *trustworthiness:* - trial, trying.

d:
**1.** accepted, particularly of coins and money.
**2.** accepted, pleasing, acceptable In the ancient world there was no banking system as we know ittoday, and no paper money. All money was made from metal, heateduntil liquid, poured into moulds and allowed to cool. When the coinswere cooled, it was necessary to smooth off the uneven edges.
