s: From a compound of [G4253](G4253) and [G5316](G5316); an *outward* *showing*, that is, *pretext:* - cloke, colour, pretence, show.

d: **1.** to bring forth
s: From [G4253](G4253) and [G5342](G5342); to *bear* *forward*, that is, *produce:* - bring forth.

d:
**1.** prophecy
  **a.** a discourse emanating from divine inspiration and declaring the purposes of God, whether by reproving and admonishing the wicked, or comforting the afflicted, or revealing things hidden; esp. by foretelling future events
  **b.** Used in the NT of the utterance of OT prophets
    **1.** of the prediction of events relating to christ’s kingdom and its speedy triumph, together with the consolations and admonitions pertaining to it, the spirit of prophecy, the divine mind, to which the prophetic faculty is due
    **2.** of the endowment and speech of the Christian teachers called prophets
    **3.** the gifts and utterances of these prophets, esp. of the predictions of the works of which, set apart to teach the gospel, will accomplish for the kingdom of christ
s: From [G4396](G4396) (“prophecy”); *prediction* (scriptural or other): - prophecy, prophesying.

d:
**1.** to prophesy, to be a prophet, speak forth by divine inspirations, to predict
  **a.** to prophesy
  **b.** with the idea of foretelling future events pertaining esp. to the kingdom of God
  **c.** to utter forth, declare, a thing which can only be known by divine revelation
  **d.** to break forth under sudden impulse in lofty discourse or praise of the divine counsels
    **1.** under like prompting, to teach, refute, reprove, admonish, comfort others
  **e.** to act as a prophet, discharge the prophetic office
s: From [G4396](G4396); to *foretell* events, *divine*, *speak* under *inspiration*, *exercise* the prophetic *office:* - prophesy.

d:
**1.** in Greek writings, an interpreter of oracles or of other hidden things
**2.** one who, moved by the spirit of God and hence his organ or spokesman, solemnly declares to men what he has received by inspiration, especially concerning future events, and in particular such as relate to the cause and kingdom of God and to human salvation
  **a.** the OT prophets, having foretold the kingdom, deeds and death, of Jesus the messiah.
  **b.** of John the Baptist, the herald of Jesus the messiah
  **c.** of the illustrious prophet, the Jews expected before the advent of the messiah
  **d.** the messiah
  **e.** of men filled with the spirit of God, who by God’s authority and command in words of weight pleads the cause of God and urges salvation of men
  **f.** of prophets that appeared in the apostolic age among Christians
    **1.** they are associated with the apostles
    **2.** they discerned and did what is best for the Christian cause, foretelling certain future events. (Act 11:27)
    **3.** in the religious assemblies of the Christians, they were moved by the holy spirit to speak, having power to instruct, comfort, encourage, rebuke, convict, and stimulate, their hearers
**3.** a poet (because poets were believed to sing under divine inspiration)
  **a.** of Epimenides (Tit 1:12)
s: From a compound of [G4253](G4253) and [G5346](G5346); a *foreteller* (“prophet”); by analogy an *inspired* *speaker*; by extension a *poet:* - prophet.

d:
**1.** proceeding from a prophet
**2.** prophetic
s: From [G4396](G4396); *pertaining* *to* *a* *foreteller* (“prophetic”): - of prophecy, of the prophets.

d:
**1.** a prophetess
**2.** a woman to whom future events or things hidden from others are at times revealed, either by inspiration or by dreams and visions
**3.** a female who declares or interprets oracles
s: Feminine of [G4396](G4396); a *female* *foreteller* or an *inspired* *woman:* - prophetess.

d: **1.** to come before, to anticipate
s: From [G4253](G4253) and [G5348](G5348); to *get* an *earlier* *start* *of*, that is, *anticipate:* - prevent.

d:
**1.** to put into the hand, to deliver into the hands
**2.** to take into one’s hands
**3.** to set before one’s self, to prostrate, to determine
**4.** to choose, to appoint
  **a.** for one’s use
  **b.** for one’s salvation
s: Middle voice from [G4253](G4253) and a derivative of [G5495](G5495); to *handle* for oneself *in* *advance*, that is, (figuratively) to *purpose:* - choose, make.
o: middle voice from [G4253](G4253) and a derivative of [G5495](G5495)

d: **1.** to choose or designate beforehand
s: From [G4253](G4253) and [G5500](G5500); to *elect* *in* *advance:* - choose before.

d:
Prochorus = leader of the chorus
**1.** one of the seven deacons chosen by the church at Jerusalem
s: From [G4253](G4253) and [G5525](G5525); *before* the *dance*; *Prochorus*, a Christian: - Prochorus.

d: **1.** the stern or hinder part of the ship
s: Feminine of πρυμνύς prumnus (*hindmost*); the *stern* of a ship: - hinder part, stern.

d:
**1.** in the morning, early
**2.** the fourth watch of the night, from 3 o’clock in the morning until 6 o’clock approximately
s: Adverb from [G4253](G4253); at *dawn*; by implication the *day* *break* watch: - early (in the morning), (in the) morning.

d: **1.** early, pertaining to the morning, at day break
s: Feminine of a derivative of [G4404](G4404) as noun; *day* *dawn:* - early, morning.
o: feminine of a derivative of [G4404](G4404) as noun

d:
**1.** early
  **a.** of the early rain which fell from October on
s: From [G4404](G4404); *dawning*, that is, (by analogy) *autumnal* (showering, the first of the rainy season): - early.

d: **1.** pertaining to the morning
s: From [G4404](G4404); pertaining to the *dawn*, that is, *matutinal:* - morning.

d: **1.** the prow or forward part of a ship
s: Feminine of a presumed derivation of [G4253](G4253) as noun; the *prow*, that is, forward part of a vessel: - forepart (-ship).
o: feminine of a presumed derivative of [G4253](G4253) as noun

d: **1.** to be first, hold the first place
s: From [G4413](G4413); to *be* *first* (in rank or influence): - have the preeminence.

d: **1.** to sit in the first seat, the first or chief seat
s: From [G4413](G4413) and [G2515](G2515); a *sitting* *first* (in the front row), that is, *preeminence* in council: - chief (highest, uppermost) seat.

d:
**1.** the first reclining place, the chief place at table
**2.** the relative rank of the several places at table varied among the Persians, Greeks, and Romans; and what arrangements the Jews had in the time of christ can not be accurately determined
s: From [G4413](G4413) and [G2828](G2828); a *reclining* *first* (in the place of honor) at the dinner bed, that is, *preeminence* at meals: - chief (highest, uppermost) room.

d:
**1.** first in time or place
  **a.** in any succession of things or persons
**2.** first in rank
  **a.** influence, honour
  **b.** chief
  **c.** principal
**3.** first, at the first
s: Neuter of [G4413](G4413) as an adverb (with or without [G3588](G3588)); *firstly* (in time, place, order, or importance): - before, at the beginning, chiefly, (at, at the) first (of all).
o: neuter of [G4413](G4413) as adverb (with or without [G3588](G3588))

d:
**1.** first in time or place
  **a.** in any succession of things or persons
**2.** first in rank
  **a.** influence, honour
  **b.** chief
  **c.** principal
**3.** first, at the first
s: Contracted superlative of [G4253](G4253); *foremost* (in time, place, order or importance): - before, beginning, best, chief (-est), first (of all), former.

d:
**1.** one who stands in the front rank
  **a.** a leader, chief, champion
s: From [G4413](G4413) and [G2476](G2476); one *standing* *first* in the ranks, that is, a *captain* (*champion*): - ringleader.

d: **1.** the right or advantages of the first born son
s: From [G4416](G4416); *primogeniture* (as a privilege): - birthright.

d:
**1.** the firstborn
  **a.** of man or beast
  **b.** of christ, the first born of all creation
s: From [G4413](G4413) and the alternate of [G5088](G5088); *first* *born* (usually as noun, literally or figuratively): - firstbegotten (-born).

d:
**1.** to cause one to stumble or fall
**2.** to stumble
  **a.** to err, make a mistake, to sin
  **b.** to fall into misery, become wretched
s: A form of [G4098](G4098); to *trip*, that is, (figuratively) to *err*, *sin*, *fail* (of salvation): - fall, offend, stumble.

d:
**1.** the heel (of the foot)
**2.** to lift up the heel against one
  **a.** to injure one by trickery (figure borrowed either from kicking, or from a wrestler tripping up his antagonist)
s: Of uncertain derivation; the *heel* (figuratively): - heel.

d:
**1.** a wing, a little wing
**2.** any pointed extremity
  **a.** of fins of fishes
  **b.** of part of a dress hanging down in the form of a wing
  **c.** of the top of the temple at Jerusalem
s: Neuter of a presumed derivative of [G4420](G4420); a *winglet*, that is, (figuratively) *extremity* (top corner): - pinnacle.

d: **1.** a wing: of birds
s: From a derivative of [G4072](G4072) (meaning a *feather*); a *wing:* - wing.
o: from a derivative of [G4072](G4072) (meaning a feather)

d:
**1.** furnished with wings
**2.** winged, flying
  **a.** of birds
s: Contraction for [G4071](G4071); a *bird:* - bird.

d:
**1.** to terrify
**2.** be terrified
s: Probably akin to the alternate of [G4098](G4098) (through the idea of causing to *fall*) or to [G4072](G4072) (through that of causing to *fly* away); to *scare:* - frighten.
o: probably akin to the alternate of [G4098](G4098) (through the idea of causing to fall) or to [G4072](G4072) (through that of causing to fly away)

d: **1.** to be afraid of with terror
s: From [G4422](G4422); *alarm:* - amazement.

d:
Ptolemais or Accho = warlike
**1.** a maritime city of Phoenicia, which got its name, apparently, from Ptolemy Lathyrus, who captured it 103 BC, and rebuilt it more beautifully
s: From “ptolemaios” (*Ptolemy*, after whom it was named); *Ptolemais*, a place in Palestine: - Ptolemais.
o: from Ptolemaios (Ptolemy, after whom it was named)

d: **1.** a winnowing shovel
s: From [G4429](G4429); a *winnowing* *fork* (as *scattering* like spittle): - fan.

d: **1.** to frighten, affright
s: From a presumed derivative of [G4429](G4429) (and thus akin to [G4422](G4422)); to *frighten:* - terrify.
o: from a presumed derivative of [G4429](G4429) (and thus akin to [G4422](G4422))

d: **1.** spittle
s: From [G4429](G4429); *saliva:* - spittle.

d: **1.** to fold together, roll up
s: Probably akin to πετάννυμι petannumi (to *spread*; and thus apparently allied to [G4072](G4072) through the idea of *expansion*, and to [G4429](G4429) through that of *flattening*; compare [G3961](G3961)); to *fold*, that is, *furl* a scroll: - close.
o: probably akin to petannumi (to spread, and thus apparently allied to [G4072](G4072) through the idea of expansion, and to [G4429](G4429) through that of flattening, cf [G3961](G3961))

d: **1.** to spit
s: A primary verb (compare [G4428](G4428)); to *spit:* - spit.

d:
**1.** a fall, downfall
  **a.** metaph. a failure, defeat, calamity
  **b.** an error, lapse into sin
**2.** that which has fallen
  **a.** the fallen body of one dead or slain, a corpse, a carcase
s: From the alternate of [G4098](G4098); a *ruin*, that is, (specifically) lifeless *body* (*corpse*, *carrion*): - dead body, carcase, corpse.

d: **1.** a falling, downfall
s: From the alternate of [G4098](G4098); a *crash*, that is, *downfall* (literally or figuratively): - fall.

d:
**1.** beggary
**2.** in the NT poverty
  **a.** the condition of one destitute of riches and abundance
s: From [G4433](G4433); *beggary*, that is, *indigence* (literally or figuratively): - poverty.

d: **1.** to be a beggar, to beg, to be poor
s: From [G4434](G4434); to *be* *a* *beggar*, that is, (by implication) to *become* *indigent* (figuratively): - become poor.

d:
**1.** reduced to beggary, begging, asking alms
**2.** destitute of wealth, influence, position, honour
  **a.** lowly, afflicted, destitute of the Christian virtues and eternal riches
  **b.** helpless, powerless to accomplish an end
  **c.** poor, needy
**3.** lacking in anything
  **a.** as respects their spirit
    **1.** destitute of wealth of learning and intellectual culture which the schools afford (men of this class most readily give themselves up to christ’s teaching and proved them selves fitted to lay hold of the heavenly treasure)
s: From πτώσσω ptōssō (to *crouch*; akin to [G4422](G4422) and the alternate of [G4098](G4098)); a *beggar* (as *cringing*), that is, *pauper* (strictly denoting absolute or public *mendicancy*, although also used in a qualified or relative sense; whereas [G3993](G3993) properly means only *straitened* circumstances in private), literally (often as noun) or figuratively (*distressed*): - beggar (-ly), poor.
o: from ptosso to crouch, akin to [G4422](G4422) and the alternate of [G4098](G4098))

d:
**1.** the fist, clenched hand
**2.** up to the elbow
s: From a primary word, πύζ pux, (the *fist* as a weapon); the clenched *hand*, that is, (only in the dative case as adverb) *with* the *fist* (hard *scrubbing*): - oft.
o: from a primary pux (the fist as a weapon)

d:
**1.** in Greek mythology the name of the Pythian serpent or dragon that dwelt in the region of Pytho at the foot of Parnassus in Phocis, and was said to have guarded the oracle at Delphi and been slain by Apollo
**2.** a spirit of divination
s: From Πυθώ Puthō (the name of the region where Delphi, the seat of the famous *oracle*, was located); a *Python*, that is, (by analogy with the supposed *diviner* there) *inspiration* (*soothsaying*): - divination.
o: from Putho (the name of the region where Delphi, the seat of the famous oracle, was located)

d:
**1.** thick, dense, compact
  **a.** in reference to time
    **1.** frequently, often, recurring
  **b.** vigorously, diligently
  **c.** often, more frequently, the oftener
s: From the same as [G4635](G4635); *clasped* (*thick*), that is, (figuratively) *frequent*; neuter plural (as adverb) *frequently:* - often (-er).

d: **1.** to be a boxer, to box
s: From a derivative of the same as [G4435](G4435); to *box* (with the fist), that is, *contend* (as a boxer) at the games (figuratively): - fight.
o: from a derivative of the same as [G4435](G4435)

d:
**1.** a gate
  **a.** of the larger sort
    **1.** in the wall of either a city
    **2.** a palace
    **3.** a town
    **4.** the temple
    **5.** a prison
**2.** the gates of hell (likened to a vast prison)
**3.** metaph. the access or entrance into any state
s: Apparently a primary word; a *gate*, that is, the leaf or wing of a folding *entrance* (literally or figuratively): - gate.

d:
**1.** a large gate: of a palace
**2.** the front part of a house, into which one enters through the gate, porch
s: From [G4439](G4439); a *gateway*, *door* *way* or a building or city; by implication a *portal* or *vestibule:* - gate, porch.

d:
**1.** to enquire, ask
**2.** to ascertain, by enquiry
s: Middle voice prolonged from πύθω puthō, a primary word, (which occurs only as an alternate in certain tenses); to *question*, that is, *ascertain* by inquiry (as a matter of *information* merely; and thus differing from [G2065](G2065), which properly means a *request* as a favor; and from [G154](G154), which is strictly a *demand* of something due; as well as from [G2212](G2212), which implies a *search* for something hidden; and from [G1189](G1189), which involves the idea of urgent *need*); by implication to *learn* (by casual intelligence): - ask, demand, enquire, understand.
o: middle voice prolonged from a primary putho (which occurs only as an alternate in certain tenses)

d: **1.** fire
s: A primary word; “fire” (literally or figuratively, specifically *lightning*): - fiery, fire.

d: **1.** a fire, a pile of burning fuel
s: From [G4442](G4442); a *fire* (concretely): - fire.

d:
**1.** a tower
**2.** a fortified structure rising to a considerable height, to repel a hostile attack or to enable a watchman to see in every direction
s: Apparently a primary word (“burgh”); a *tower* or *castle:* - tower.

d: **1.** to be sick with a fever
s: From [G4443](G4443); to be *on* *fire*, that is, (specifically) to *have* *a* *fever:* - be sick of a fever.

d:
**1.** fiery heat
**2.** fever
s: From [G4445](G4445); *inflamed*, that is, (by implication) *feverish* (as noun, *fever*): - fever.

d:
**1.** fiery
**2.** shining like fire
s: From [G4443](G4443); *fiery*, that is, (by implication) *flaming:* - of fire.

d:
**1.** to burn with fire, to set on fire, kindle
  **a.** to be on fire, to burn
    **1.** to be incensed, indignant
  **b.** make to glow
    **1.** full of fire, fiery, ignited
  **c.** of darts filled with inflammable substances and set on fire
    **1.** melted by fire and purged of dross
s: From [G4442](G4442); to *kindle*, that is, (passively) to *be* *ignited*, *glow* (literally), *be* *refined* (by implication), or (figuratively) to *be* *inflamed* (with anger, grief, lust): - burn, fiery, be on fire, try.

d: **1.** to become glowing, grow red, be red
s: From [G4450](G4450); to *redden* (intransitively): - be red.

d: **1.** having the colour of fire, red
s: From [G4442](G4442); *fire* *like*, that is, (specifically) *flame* *colored:* - red.

d:
**1.** a burning
  **a.** the burning by which metals are roasted and reduced
  **b.** by a figure drawn from a refiners fire
    **1.** calamities or trials that test the character
s: From [G4448](G4448); *ignition*, that is, (specifically) *smelting* (figuratively *conflagration*, *calamity* as a *test*): - burning, trial.

d:
**1.** yet, even
**2.** used only in compound with words 3369, 3380, 3764, 3768, 4455
s: Another form of the base of [G4458](G4458); an enclitic particle of indefiniteness; *yet*, *even*; used only in compounds.
o: another form of the base of [G4458](G4458)

d:
**1.** to barter, to sell
**2.** sellers
s: Probably ultimately from πέλομαι pelomai (to *be* *busy*, to *trade*); to *barter* (as a *pedlar*), that is, to *sell:* - sell, whatever is sold.
o: probably ultimately from pelomai (to be busy, to trade)

d:
**1.** a colt, the young of a horse
**2.** a young creature
  **a.** of a young ass
  **b.** an ass’s colt
s: Apparently a primary word; a “foal” or “filly”, that is, (specifically) a *young* *ass:* - colt.

d: **1.** ever, at any time
s: From [G4452](G4452) and [G4218](G4218); *at* *any* *time*, that is, (with negative particle) *at* *no* *time:* - at any time, + never (. . . to any man), + yet never man.

d:
**1.** to cover with a thick skin, to harden by covering with a callus
**2.** metaph.
  **a.** to make the heart dull
  **b.** to grow hard, callous, become dull, lose the power of understanding
s: Apparently from πῶρος pōros (a kind of *stone*); to *petrify*, that is, (figuratively) to *indurate* (*render* *stupid* or *callous*): - blind, harden.
o: apparently from poros (a kind of stone)

d:
**1.** the covering with a callus
**2.** obtrusiveness of mental discernment, dulled perception
**3.** the mind of one has been blunted
  **a.** of stubbornness, obduracy
s: From [G4456](G4456); *stupidity* or *callousness:* - blindness, hardness.

d: **1.** by any means, at all, perhaps
s: Adverb from the base of [G4225](G4225); an enclitic particle of indefiniteness of manner; *somehow* or *anyhow*; used only in compounds: - haply, by any (some) means, perhaps. See [G1513](G1513), [G3381](G3381). Compare [G4459](G4459).
o: adverb from the base of [G4225](G4225), an enclitic particle of indefiniteness of manner

d: **1.** how, in what way
s: Adverb from the base of [G4226](G4226); an interrogitive particle of manner; *in* *what* *way?* (sometimes the question is indirect, *how?*); also as exclamation, *how* much!: - how, after (by) what manner (means), that. \[*Occasionally* *unexpressed* *in* *English*.\]
o: adverb from the base of [G4226](G4226), an interrogative particle of manner

d:
Rahab = wide
**1.** a harlot of Jericho
s: Of Hebrew origin \[[H7343](H7343)\]; *Raab* (that is, *Rachab*), a Canaanitess: - Rahab. See also [G4477](G4477).

d:
**1.** my great one, my honourable sir
**2.** Rabbi, a title used by the Jews to address their teachers (and also honour them when not addressing them)
s: Of Hebrew origin \[[H7227](H7227)\] with pronominal suffix; *my* *master*, that is, *Rabbi*, as an official title of honor: - Master, Rabbi.
o: of hebrew origin [H7227](H7227) with pronominal suffix

d:
**1.** master, chief, prince
**2.** Rabboni is a title of honour Mary used to address Jesus
s: Of Chaldee origin; corresponding to [G4461](G4461): - Lord, Rabboni.

d: **1.** to beat with rods
s: From [G4464](G4464); to *strike* *with* *a* *stick*, that is, *bastinado:* - beat (with rods).

d:
**1.** a staff, a walking stick, a twig, rod, branch
**2.** a rod with which one is beaten
**3.** a staff
  **a.** as used on a journey, or to lean upon, or by shepherds
  **b.** when applied to kings
    **1.** with a rod of iron, indicates the severest, most rigorous rule
    **2.** a royal sceptre
s: From the base of [G4474](G4474); a *stick* or *wand* (as a *cudgel*, a *cane* or a *baton* of royalty): - rod, sceptre, staff.

d:
**1.** one who carries the rods i.e. the fasces
**2.** a lictor, a public official who bore the fasces or staff and other insignia of office before a magistrate
s: From [G4464](G4464) and [G2192](G2192); a *rod* (the Latin *fasces*) *holder*, that is, a Roman *lictor* (*constable* or *executioner*): - serjeant.

d:
Reu = associate ye: feed ye
**1.** one of the ancestors of christ
s: Of Hebrew origin \[[H7466](H7466)\]; *Ragau* (that is, *Reu*), a patriarch: - Ragau.

d: **1.** a piece of knavery, rascality, villainy
s: From a compound of ῥᾳδιος rhadios (*easy*, that is, *reckless*) and [G2041](G2041); *easy* *going* *behavior*, that is, (by extension) a *crime:* - lewdness.
o: from a comparative of rhaidios (easy, i.e. reckless) and [G2041](G2041)

d:
**1.** ease in doing, faculty
**2.** levity or easiness in thinking or acting
  **a.** love of a lazy effeminate life
**3.** unscrupulous, cunning, mischief
s: From the same as [G4467](G4467); *recklessness*, that is, (by extension) *malignity:* - mischief.

d:
**1.** empty, i.e. a senseless, empty headed man
**2.** a term of reproach used among the Jews in the time of christ
s: Of Chaldee origin (compare \[[H7386](H7386)\]); O *empty* one, that is, thou *worthless* (as a term of utter vilification): - Raca.

d:
**1.** a piece torn off
**2.** a bit of cloth
**3.** cloth
s: From [G4486](G4486); a *“rag”*, i. e. *piece* of cloth: - cloth.

d:
Ramah = a hill
**1.** a town of the tribe of Benjamin, situated about 5 miles (8 km) north of Jerusalem on the road to Bethel
s: Of Hebrew origin \[[H7414](H7414)\]; *Rama* (that is, *Ramah*), a place in Palestine: - Rama.

d:
**1.** to sprinkle
**2.** to cleanse by sprinkling, hence to purify, cleanse
s: From a derivative of ῥαίνω rhainō (to *sprinkle*); to *render* *besprinkled*, that is, *asperse* (ceremonially or figuratively): - sprinkle.
o: from a derivative of rhaino (to sprinkle)

d:
**1.** a sprinkling (purification)
  **a.** blood of sprinkling
    **1.** i.e. appointed for sprinkling (serving to purify)
s: From [G4472](G4472); *aspersion* (ceremonially or figuratively): - sprinkling.

d:
**1.** to smite with a rod or staff
**2.** to smite in the face with the palm of the hand, to box the ear
s: From a derivative of ῥέπω rhepō, a primary word, (to *let* *fall*, “rap”); to *slap* (with the palm of the hand): - smite (with the palm of the hand). Compare [G5180](G5180).
o: from a derivative of a primary rhepo (to let fall, rap)

d:
**1.** a blow with a rod or staff or a scourge
**2.** a blow with the flat of the hand, a slap in the face, box the ear
s: From [G4474](G4474); a *slap:* - (+ strike with the) palm of the hand, smite with the hand.

d: **1.** a needle
s: From ῥάπτω rhaptō, a primary word, (to *sew*; perhaps rather akin to the base of [G4474](G4474) through the idea of *puncturing*); a *needle:* - needle.

d:
Rahab = wide
**1.** a harlot of Jericho
s: From the same as [G4460](G4460); *Rachab*, a Canaanitess: - Rachab.

d:
Rachel = ewe or sheep
**1.** the wife of Jacob
s: Of Hebrew origin \[[H7354](H7354)\]; *Rachel*, the wife of Jacob: - Rachel.

d:
Rebekah = ensnarer
**1.** the wife of Isaac
s: Of Hebrew origin \[[H7259](H7259)\]; *Rebecca* (that is, *Ribkah*), the wife of Isaac: - Rebecca.

d: **1.** a chariot, a type of vehicle having four wheels
s: Of Latin origin; a *rheda*, that is, four wheeled *carriage* (*wagon* for riding): - chariot.

d:
Remphan = the shrunken (as lifeless)
**1.** the name of an idol worshipped secretly by the Israelites in the wilderness
s: By incorrect transliteration for a word of Hebrew origin \[[H3594](H3594)\]; *Remphan* (that is, *Kijun*), an Egyptian idol: - Remphan.
o: by incorrect transliteration for a word of hebrew origin [H3594](H3594)

d: **1.** to flow
s: A primary verb; for some tenses of which a prolonged form (ῥεύω rheuō) is used; to *flow* (“run”, as water): - flow.

d: **1.** to pour forth, to utter
s: For certain tenses of which a prolonged form (ἐρέω ereō) is used; and both as alternate for [G2036](G2036); perhaps akin (or identical) with [G4482](G4482) (through the idea of *pouring* forth); to *utter*, that is, *speak* or *say*: - command, make, say, speak (of). Compare [G3004](G3004).
o: for certain tenses of which a prolonged form ereo er-eh’-o, is used, and both as alternate for [G2036](G2036), perhaps akin (or ident.) with [G4482](G4482) (through the idea of pouring forth)

d:
Rhegium = breach
**1.** an Italian town situated on the Bruttian coast, just at the southern entrance of the Straits of messina
s: Of Latin origin; *Rhegium*, a place in Italy: - Rhegium.

d:
**1.** that which has been broken or rent asunder
  **a.** a fracture, breach, cleft
  **b.** rent clothes
  **c.** fall, ruin
s: From [G4486](G4486); something *torn*, that is, a *fragment* (by implication and abstraction, a *fall*): - ruin.

d:
**1.** to rend, burst or break asunder, break up, break through
  **a.** to tear in pieces
  **b.** to break forth
    **1.** into joy, of infants or dumb persons beginning to speak
  **c.** to distort, convulse
    **1.** of a demon causing convulsions in a man possessed
    **2.** to dash down, hurl to the ground (a common occurrence in cases of demon possession and epilepsy)
s: Both are prolonged forms of ῥήκω rhēko (which appears only in certain forms, and is itself probably a strengthened form of ἄγνυμι agnumi (see in [G2608](G2608))); to “break”, “wreck” or “crack”, that is, (especially) to *sunder* (by *separation* of the parts; [G2608](G2608) being its intensive (with the preposition in compounds), and [G2352](G2352) a *shattering* to minute fragments; but not a *reduction* to the constituent particles, like [G3089](G3089)) or *disrupt*, *lacerate*; by implication to *convulse* (with *spasms*); figuratively to *give* *vent* to joyful emotions: - break (forth), burst, rend, tear.
o: both prolonged forms of rheko (which appears only in certain forms, and is itself probably a strengthened form of agnumi \[see in [G2608](G2608)\])

d:
**1.** that which is or has been uttered by the living voice, thing spoken, word
  **a.** any sound produced by the voice and having definite meaning
  **b.** speech, discourse
    **1.** what one has said
  **c.** a series of words joined together into a sentence (a declaration of one’s mind made in words)
    **1.** an utterance
    **2.** a saying of any sort as a message, a narrative
  **d.** concerning some occurrence
**2.** subject matter of speech, thing spoken of
  **a.** so far forth as it is a matter of narration
  **b.** so far as it is a matter of command
  **c.** a matter of dispute, case at law
s: From [G4483](G4483); an *utterance* (individually, collectively or specifically); by implication a *matter* or *topic* (especially of narration, command or dispute); with a negative *naught* whatever: - + evil, + nothing, saying, word.

d:
Rhesa = head
**1.** the son of Zerubbabel in the genealogy of christ
s: Probably of Hebrew origin (apparently for \[[H7509](H7509)\]); *Resa* (that is, *Rephajah*), an Israelite: - Rhesa.

d:
**1.** a speaker, an orator
  **a.** of a forensic orator or advocate
s: From [G4483](G4483); a *speaker*, that is, (by implication) a forensic *advocate:* - orator.

d: **1.** expressly, in express words
s: Adverb from a derivative of [G4483](G4483); out *spokenly*, that is, *distinctly:* - expressly.

d:
**1.** a root
**2.** that which like a root springs from a root, a sprout, shoot
**3.** metaph. offspring, progeny
s: Apparently a primary word; a “root” (literally or figuratively): - root.

d: **1.** to cause to strike root, to strengthen with roots, to render firm, to fix, establish, cause a person or a thing to be thoroughly grounded
s: From [G4491](G4491); to *root* (figuratively *become* *stable*): - root.

d:
**1.** a throw, stroke, beat
**2.** a moment of time
s: From [G4496](G4496); a *jerk* (of the eye, that is, (by analogy) an *instant*): - twinkling.

d:
**1.** to raise a breeze, put air in motion, whether for the sake of kindling a fire or cooling one’s self
  **a.** to blow up a fire
  **b.** to fan, i.e. cool with a fan
**2.** to toss to and fro, to agitate
  **a.** of the wind
  **b.** of persons whose mind wavers in uncertainty between hope and fear, between doing and not doing a thing
s: From a derivative of [G4496](G4496) (meaning a *fan* or *bellows*); to *breeze* *up*, that is, (by analogy) to *agitate* (into waves): - toss.
o: from a derivative of [G4496](G4496) (meaning a fan or bellows)

d:
**1.** to cast, throw
**2.** throw down
**3.** to cast forward or before
**4.** to set down (with the suggestion of haste and want of care)
**5.** to throw to the ground, prostrate
s: From a derivative of [G4496](G4496); to *toss* up: - cast off.

d:
**1.** to cast, throw
**2.** throw down
**3.** to cast forward or before
**4.** to set down (with the suggestion of haste and want of care)
**5.** to throw to the ground, prostrate
s: A primary verb (perhaps rather akin to the base of [G4474](G4474), through the idea of sudden *motion*); to *fling* (properly with a quick *toss*, thus differing from [G906](G906), which denotes a *deliberate* hurl; and from τείνω teinō (see in [G1614](G1614)), which indicates an *extended* projection); by qualification, to *deposit* (as if a load); by extension to *disperse:* - cast (down, out), scatter abroad, throw.
o: a primary verb (perhaps rather akin to the base of [G4474](G4474), through the idea of sudden motion)

d:
Rehoboam = enlarger of the people
**1.** the son of Solomon by an ammonite princess Naamah
s: Of Hebrew origin \[[H7346](H7346)\]; *Roboam* (that is, *Rechabam*), an Israelite: - Roboam.

d:
Rhoda = rose
**1.** the name of a certain maid servant
s: Probably for ῥόδή rhodē (a *rose*); *Rode*, a servant girl: - Rhoda.

d:
Rhodes = rosy
**1.** a well known island of the Cyclades opposite Caria and Lycia, with a Rhodes as the capital city
s: Probably from ῥόδον rhodon (a *rose*); *Rhodus*, an island of the Mediterranean: - Rhodes.

d: **1.** with a loud noise
s: Adverb from a derivative of ῥοῖζος rhoizos (a *whir*); *whizzingly*, that is, *with* *a* *crash:* - with a great noise.
o: from a derivative of rhoizos (a whir)

d:
**1.** a large sword
**2.** properly a long Thracian javelin, also a kind of long sword wont to be worn on the right shoulder
s: Probably of foreign origin; a *sabre*, that is, a long and broad *cutlass* (any *weapon* of the kind, literally or figuratively): - sword.

d:
Reuben = behold a son
**1.** Jacob’s firstborn child by Leah
s: Of Hebrew origin \[[H7205](H7205)\]; *Ruben* (that is, *Reuben*), an Israelite: - Reuben.

d:
Ruth = a female friend
**1.** the ancestor of David and of christ
s: Of Hebrew origin \[[H7327](H7327)\]; *Ruth*, a Moabitess: - Ruth.

d:
Rufus = red
**1.** name of a certain Christian
s: Of Latin origin; *red*; *Rufus*, a Christian: - Rufus.

d:
**1.** a swing, rush, force, trail, of a body in motion
**2.** a tract of way in a town shut in by buildings on both sides
**3.** a street, a lane
s: Prolonged from [G4506](G4506) in its original sense; an *alley* or *avenue* (as crowded): - lane, street.
o: prolongation from [G4506](G4506) in its original sense

d:
**1.** to draw to one’s self, to rescue, to deliver
**2.** the deliverer
s: Middle voice of an obsolete verb, akin to [G4482](G4482) (through the idea of a *current*; compare [G4511](G4511)); to *rush* or *draw* (for oneself), that is, *rescue:* - deliver (-er).
o: middle voice of an obsolete verb, akin to [G4482](G4482) (through the idea of a current, cf [G4511](G4511))

d:
**1.** to make filthy, befoul
**2.** to defile, dishonour
**3.** to make filthy
s: From [G4508](G4508); *dirtiness* (morally): - filthiness.

d:
**1.** to be dirty, grow filthy
**2.** metaph. to be defiled with iniquity
s: From [G4509](G4509); *dirty*, that is, (relatively) *cheap* or *shabby*; morally *wicked:* - vile.

d: **1.** filthy, dirty
s: Of uncertain affinity; *dirt*, that is, (moral) *depravity:* - filth.

d:
**1.** to make filthy, defile, soil
**2.** to be filthy (morally)
s: From [G4509](G4509); to *soil*, that is, (intransitively) to *become* *dirty* (morally): - be filthy.

d: **1.** a flowing issue
s: From [G4506](G4506) in the sense of its congener [G4482](G4482); a *flux* (of blood): - issue.
o: from [G4506](G4506) in the sense of its congener [G4482](G4482)

d: **1.** a wrinkle
s: From [G4506](G4506); a *fold* (as *drawing* together), that is, a *wrinkle* (especially on the face): - wrinkle.

d:
Latin = of Rome’s strength
**1.** the language spoken by the Romans
s: From [G4514](G4514); *Romaic*, that is, *Latin:* - Latin.

d: **1.** a resident of the city of Rome, a Roman citizen
s: From [G4516](G4516); *Romaean*, that is, *Roman* (as noun): - Roman, of Rome.

d:
Latin = of Rome’s strength
**1.** the language spoken by the Romans
s: Adverb from a presumed derivative of [G4516](G4516); *Romaistically*, that is, *in* the *Latin* language: - Latin.

d:
Rome = strength
**1.** the famous capital of the ancient world
s: From the base of [G4517](G4517); *strength*; *Roma*, the capital of Italy: - Rome.

d:
**1.** to make strong, strengthen
**2.** to be strong, to thrive, prosper
**3.** in the usual formula in closing of a letter, farewell
s: Prolonged from ῥώομαι rhōomai (to *dart*; probably akin to [G4506](G4506)); to *strengthen*, that is, (imperative passive) *have* *health* (as parting exclamation, *good* *bye*): - farewell.
o: prolongation from rhoomai (to dart, probably akin to [G4506](G4506))

d: **1.** thou hast forsaken me
s: Of Chaldee origin \[[H7662](H7662)\] with pronominal suffix; *thou* *hast* *left* *me*; *sabachthani* (that is, *shebakthani*), a cry of distress: - sabachthani.
o: of Aramaic or [G7662](G7662) with pronominal suffix

d:
**1.** Lord of Sabaoth
  **a.** Lord of the armies of Israel, as those who are under the leadership and protection of Jehovah maintain his cause in war
s: Of Hebrew origin (\[[H6635](H6635)\] in feminine plural); *armies*; *sabaoth* (that is, *tsebaoth*), a military epithet of God: - sabaoth.
o: of hebrew origin [H6635](H6635) in feminine plural

d:
**1.** a keeping sabbath
**2.** the blessed rest from toils and troubles looked for in the age to come by the true worshippers of God and true Christians
s: From a derivative of [G4521](G4521); a “sabbatism”, that is, (figuratively) the *repose* of Christianity (as a type of heaven): - rest.

d:
**1.** the seventh day of each week which is a sacred rest on which the whole world is required to abstain from all secular work
  **a.** the institution of the sabbath, the law for keeping holy every seventh day of the week
  **b.** a single sabbath, sabbath day
**2.** seven days, a week
s: Of Hebrew origin \[[H7676](H7676)\]; the *Sabbath* (that is, *Shabbath*), or day of weekly *repose* from secular avocations (also the observance or institution itself); by extension a *se’nnight*, that is, the interval between two Sabbaths; likewise the plural in all the above applications: - sabbath (day), week.

d: **1.** a large fishing net, a drag net
s: From a derivative of σάττω sattō (to *equip*) meaning *furniture*, especially a *pack* *saddle* (which in the East is merely a bag of *netted* rope); a “seine” for fishing: - net.
o: from a derivative of satto (to equip) meaning furniture, especially a pack-saddle (which in the East is merely a bag of netted rope)

d:
Sadducees = the righteous
**1.** a religious party at the time of christ among the Jews, who denied that the oral law was a revelation of God to the Israelites, and who deemed the written law alone to be obligatory on the nation, as the divine authority. They denied the following doctrines:
  **a.** resurrection of the body
  **b.** immortality of the soul
  **c.** existence of spirits and angels
  **d.** divine predestination, affirmed free will
s: Probably from [G4524](G4524); a *Sadducaean* (that is, *Tsadokian*), or follower of a certain heretical Israelite: - Sadducee.

d:
Sadoc = just
**1.** a descendant of Zerubbabel in the genealogy of christ
s: Of Hebrew origin \[[H6659](H6659)\]; *Sadoc* (that is, *Tsadok*), an Israelite: - Sadoc.

d:
**1.** to wag the tail
  **a.** of dogs
**2.** metaph.
  **a.** to flatter, fawn upon
  **b.** to move (the mind of one)
    **1.** agreeably
    **2.** to agitate, disturb, trouble
s: Akin to [G4579](G4579); to *wag* (as a dog its tail fawningly), that is, (generally) to *shake* (figuratively *disturb*): - move.

d:
**1.** a sack
  **a.** a receptacle for holding or carrying various things, as money, food, etc.
  **b.** a course cloth, a dark course stuff made especially from the hair of animals
  **c.** a garment of the like material, and clinging to the person like a sack, which was wont to be worn (or drawn over the tunic instead of the cloak or mantle) by mourners, penitents, suppliants and also by those who like the hebrew prophets, lead an austere life
s: Of Hebrew origin \[[H8242](H8242)\]; “sack” *cloth*, that is, *mohair* (the material or garments made of it, worn as a sign of grief): - sackcloth.

d:
Salah = sprout
**1.** the son of Arphaxad, and father of Eber
s: Of Hebrew origin \[[H7974](H7974)\]; *Sala* (that is, *Shelach*), a patriarch: - Sala.

d:
Shealtiel = I have asked of God
**1.** the son of Jeconiah in the genealogy of christ
s: Of Hebrew origin \[[H7597](H7597)\]; *Salathiel* (that is, *Shealtiel*), an Israelite: - Salathiel.

d:
Salmis = salt
**1.** a principal city at the east end of the island of Cyprus
s: Probably from [G4535](G4535) (from the *surge* on the shore); *Salamis*, a place in Cyprus: - Salamis.
o: probably from [G4535](G4535) (from the surge on the shore)

d:
Salim = peace
**1.** a well known town 8 miles (11 km) south of Scythopolis
s: Probably from the same as [G4531](G4531); *Salim*, a place in Palestine: - Salim.

d:
**1.** a motion produced by winds, storms, waves, etc
  **a.** to agitate or shake
  **b.** to cause to totter
  **c.** to shake thoroughly, of a measure filled by shaking its contents together
**2.** to shake down, overthrow
  **a.** to cast down from one’s (secure and happy) state
  **b.** to move, agitate the mind, to disturb one
s: From [G4535](G4535); to *waver*, that is, *agitate*, *rock*, *topple* or (by implication) *destroy*; figuratively to *disturb*, *incite:* - move, shake (together), which can \[-not\] be shaken, stir up.

d:
Salem = peace
**1.** the place where melchizedek was king and thought to be the ancient name of Jerusalem
s: Of Hebrew origin \[[H8004](H8004)\]; *Salem* (that is, *Shalem*), a place in Palestine: - Salem.

d:
Salmon = raiment: a garment
**1.** the father of Boaz in the genealogy of christ
s: Of Hebrew origin \[[H8012](H8012)\]; *Salmon*, an Israelite: - Salmon.

d:
Salmone = clothed
**1.** a bold promontory on the east point of the island of Crete
s: Perhaps of similar origin to [G4529](G4529); *Salmone*, a place in Crete: - Salmone.

d: **1.** the tossing or swell of the sea
s: Probably from the base of [G4525](G4525); a *vibration*, that is, (specifically) *billow:* - wave.

d: **1.** a trumpet
s: Perhaps from [G4535](G4535) (through the idea of *quavering* or *reverberation*); a *trumpet:* - trump (-et).
o: perhaps from [G4535](G4535) (through the idea of quavering or reverberation)

d: **1.** to sound a trumpet
s: From [G4536](G4536); to *trumpet*, that is, *sound* *a* *blast* (literally or figuratively): - (which are yet to) sound (a trumpet).

d: **1.** a trumpeter
s: From [G4537](G4537); a *trumpeter:* - trumpeter.

d:
Salome = peaceful
**1.** the wife of Zebedee and the mother of the apostle James the elder and John
s: Probably of Hebrew origin (feminine from \[[H7965](H7965)\]); *Salome* (that is, *Shelomah*), an Israelitess: - Salome.

d:
Samaria = guardianship
**1.** a territory in Palestine, which had Samaria as its capital
s: Of Hebrew origin \[[H8111](H8111)\]; *Samaria* (that is, *Shomeron*), a city and region of Palestine: - Samaria.

d:
**1.** a Samaritan,
  **a.** an inhabitant of the city of Samaria
  **b.** an inhabitant of the region of Samaria
s: From [G4540](G4540); a *Samarite*, that is, inhabitants of Samaria: - Samaritan.

d: **1.** a Samaritan woman
s: Feminine of [G4541](G4541); a *Samaritess*, that is, woman of Samaria: - of Samaria.

d:
Samothracia = a sign of rags
**1.** an island on the Aegean Sea, about 38 Miles (60 km) from the coast of Thrace at the mouth of the river hebrus
s: From [G4544](G4544) and Θρᾴκη Thrakē (*Thrace*); *Samo-thrace* (*Samos* *of* *Thrace*), an island in the Mediterranean: - Samothrace.

d:
Samos = a sandy bluff
**1.** an island off that part of Asia Minor where Ionia touches Caria
s: Of uncertain affinity; *Samus*, an island of the Mediterranean: - Samos.

d:
Samuel = his name is of God
**1.** the son of Elkanah and Hannah, the last of the judges, a distinguished prophet, and a founder of the prophetic order, he gave the Jews there first kings, Saul, David
s: Of Hebrew origin \[[H8050](H8050)\]; *Samuel* (that is, *Shemuel*), an Israelite: - Samuel.

d:
Samson = like the sun
**1.** a famous judge of Israel renowned for his physical strength
s: Of Hebrew origin \[[H8123](H8123)\]; *Sampson* (that is, *Shimshon*), an Israelite: - Samson.

d: **1.** a sandal, a sole made of wood or leather, covering the bottom of the foot and bound on with thongs
s: Neuter of a derivative of σάνδαλον sandalon (a “sandal”; of uncertain origin); a *slipper* or *sole* *pad:* - sandal.
o: from a derivative of sandalon (a sandal; of uncertain origin)

d: **1.** a board, a plank
s: Of uncertain affinity; a *plank:* - board.

d:
Saul = desired
**1.** the Jewish name of the apostle Paul
**2.** the son of Kish and the first king of Israel
s: Of Hebrew origin \[[H7586](H7586)\]; *Saul* (that is, *Shaul*), the Jewish name of *Paul*: - Saul. Compare [G4569](G4569).

d:
**1.** rotten, putrefied
**2.** corrupted by one and no longer fit for use, worn out
**3.** of poor quality, bad, unfit for use, worthless
s: From [G4595](G4595); *rotten*, that is, *worthless* (literally or morally): - bad, corrupt. Compt. [G4190](G4190).

d:
Sapphira = a sapphire
**1.** the wife of Ananias
s: Feminine of [G4552](G4552); *Sapphire*, an Israelitess: - Sapphira.

d: **1.** sapphire, a precious stone
s: Of Hebrew origin \[[H5601](H5601)\]; a “sapphire” or *lapis-lazuli* gem: - sapphire.

d:
**1.** a braided rope, a band
**2.** a basket, a basket made of ropes, a hamper
s: Apparently of Hebrew origin \[[H8276](H8276)\]; a *basket* (as *interwoven* or *wicker* work): - basket.

d:
Sardis = red ones
**1.** a luxurious city in Asia Minor, the capital of Lydia
s: Plural of uncertain derivation; *Sardis*, a place in Asia Minor: - Sardis.

d: **1.** a sardius, a precious stone of which there are two types, the former is called a carnelian (because flesh coloured) and the latter a sard
s: From the same as [G4556](G4556); *sardine* ([G3037](G3037) being implied), that is, a gem, so called: - sardine.

d: **1.** a sardius, a precious stone of which there are two types, the former is called a carnelian (because flesh coloured) and the latter a sard
s: Proper adjective from an uncertain base; *sardian* ([G3037](G3037) being implied), that is, (as noun) the gem so called: - sardius.
o: properly, an adjective from an uncertain base

d: **1.** a sardonyx, a precious stone marked by the red colours of the carnelian (sard) and the white of the onyx
s: From the base of [G4556](G4556) and ὄνυξ onux (the *nail* of a finger; hence the “onyx” stone); a “sardonyx”, that is, the gem so called: - sardonyx.
o: from the base of [G4556](G4556) and onux (the nail of a finger, hence the onyx stone)

d:
Sarepta = smelting
**1.** the Greek name for Zarephath, a Phoenician town between Tyre and Sidon, but nearer Sidon
s: Of Hebrew origin \[[H6886](H6886)\]; *Sarepta* (that is, *Tsarephath*), a place in Palestine: - Sarepta.

d:
**1.** fleshly, carnal
  **a.** having the nature of flesh, i.e. under the control of the animal appetites
    **1.** governed by mere human nature not by the spirit of God
    **2.** having its seat in the animal nature or aroused by the animal nature
    **3.** human: with the included idea of depravity
  **b.** pertaining to the flesh
    **1.** to the body: related to birth, linage, etc
s: From [G4561](G4561); *pertaining* *to* *flesh*, that is, (by extension) *bodily*, *temporal*, or (by implication) *animal*, *unregenerate:* - carnal, fleshly.

d:
**1.** fleshly, consisting of flesh, composed of flesh
**2.** pertaining to the body (as earthly and perishable material)
**3.** wholly given up to the flesh, rooted in the flesh as it were
s: From [G4561](G4561); *similar* *to* *flesh*, that is, (by analogy) *soft:* - fleshly.

d:
**1.** flesh (the soft substance of the living body, which covers the bones and is permeated with blood) of both man and beasts
**2.** the body
  **a.** the body of a man
  **b.** used of natural or physical origin, generation or relationship
    **1.** born of natural generation
  **c.** the sensuous nature of man, the animal nature
    **1.** without any suggestion of depravity
    **2.** the animal nature with cravings which incite to sin
    **3.** the physical nature of man as subject to suffering
**3.** a living creature (because possessed of a body of flesh) whether man or beast
**4.** the flesh, denotes mere human nature, the earthly nature of man apart from divine influence, and therefore prone to sin and opposed to God
s: Probably from the base of [G4563](G4563); *flesh* (as *stripped* of the skin), that is, (strictly) the *meat* of an animal (as food), or (by extension) the *body* (as opposed to the soul (or spirit), or as the symbol of what is external, or as the means of kindred, or (by implication) *human* *nature* (with its frailties (physically or morally) and passions), or (specifically) a *human* *being* (as such): - carnal (-ly, + -ly minded), flesh (\[-ly\]).

d:
Serug = intertwined
**1.** the son of Reu in the genealogy of christ
s: Of Hebrew origin \[[H8286](H8286)\]; *Saruch* (that is, *Serug*), a patriarch: - Saruch.

d: **1.** to sweep, clean by sweeping
s: From a derivative of σαιρω sairō (to *brush* off; akin to [G4951](G4951)) meaning a *broom*; to *sweep:* - sweep.
o: from a derivative of sairo (to brush off, akin to [G4951](G4951))

d:
Sarah = princess
**1.** the wife of Abraham
s: Of Hebrew origin \[[H8283](H8283)\]; *Sarra* (that is, *Sarah*), the wife of Abraham: - Sara, Sarah.

d:
Sharon = plain or level
**1.** a level region extending from Caesarea of Palestine as far as Joppa, abounding in good pasture and famous for its fertility
s: Of Hebrew origin \[[H8289](H8289)\]; *Saron* (that is, *Sharon*), a district of Palestine: - Saron.

d:
**1.** adversary (one who opposes another in purpose or act), the name given to
  **a.** the prince of evil spirits, the inveterate adversary of God and christ
    **1.** he incites apostasy from God and to sin
    **2.** circumventing men by his wiles
    **3.** the worshippers of idols are said to be under his control
    **4.** by his demons he is able to take possession of men and inflict them with diseases
    **5.** by God’s assistance he is overcome
    **6.** on christ’s return from heaven he will be bound with chains for a thousand years, but when the thousand years are finished he will walk the earth in yet greater power, but shortly after will be given over to eternal punishment
  **b.** a Satan-like man
s: Of Hebrew origin \[[H7854](H7854)\]; *Satan*, that is, the *devil:* - Satan. Compare [G4567](G4567).

d:
**1.** adversary (one who opposes another in purpose or act), the name given to
  **a.** the prince of evil spirits, the inveterate adversary of God and christ
    **1.** he incites apostasy from God and to sin
    **2.** circumventing men by his wiles
    **3.** the worshippers of idols are said to be under his control
    **4.** by his demons he is able to take possession of men and inflict them with diseases
    **5.** by God’s assistance he is overcome
    **6.** on christ’s return from heaven he will be bound with chains for a thousand years, but when the thousand years are finished he will walk the earth in yet greater power, but shortly after will be given over to eternal punishment
  **b.** a Satan-like man
s: Of Chaldee origin corresponding to [G4566](G4566) (with the definite article affixed); *the* *accuser*, that is, the *devil:* - Satan.
o: of Aramaic origin corresponding to [G4566](G4566) (with the definite affix)

d: **1.** a kind of dry measure, 3 gallons (14 litres)
s: Of Hebrew origin \[[H5429](H5429)\]; a certain *measure* for things dry: - measure.

d:
Saul = desired
**1.** the Jewish name of the apostle Paul
s: Of Hebrew origin, the same as [G4549](G4549); *Saulus* (that is, *Shaul*), the Jewish name of *Paul:* - Saul.
o: of hebrew origin, the same as [G4549](G4549)

d:
**1.** to extinguish, quench
  **a.** of fire or things on fire
    **1.** to be quenched, to go out
  **b.** metaph. to quench, to suppress, stifle
    **1.** of divine influence
s: A prolonged form of an apparently primary verb; to *extinguish* (literally or figuratively): - go out, quench.
o: a prolonged form of an apparently primary verb

d: **1.** thou, thee
s: Accusative singular of [G4771](G4771); *thee:* - thee, thou, X thy house.

d: **1.** thyself, thee
s: The genitive case from [G4571](G4571) and [G846](G846), with the dative and accusative of the same with contractions, respectively, *of* (*with*, *to*) *thyself:* - thee, thine own self, (thou) thy (-self).

d:
**1.** to fear, be afraid
**2.** to honour religiously, to worship
s: Middle voice from a derivative of [G4576](G4576); to *venerate*, that is, *adore:* - worship.
o: middle voice from a derivative of [G4576](G4576)

d:
**1.** whatever is religiously honoured, an object of worship
  **a.** of temples, altars, statues, idolatrous images
s: From [G4573](G4573); something *adored*, that is, an *object* *of* *worship* (god, altar, etc.): - devotion, that is worshipped.

d:
**1.** reverend, venerable
**2.** the title of the Roman emperors
  **a.** Augustan, i,e, taking its name from the emperor
  **b.** a title of honour which used to be given certain legions, or cohorts, or battalions, for valour
s: From [G4573](G4573); *venerable* (*august*), that is, (as noun) a title of the Roman *Emperor*, or (as adjective) *imperial:* - Augustus (-’).

d: **1.** to revere, to worship
s: Middle voice of an apparently primary verb; to *revere*, that is, *adore:* - devout, religious, worship.
o: middle voice of an apparently primary verb

d:
**1.** a line, a rope
**2.** a chain
s: Probably from [G4951](G4951) through its congener εἴρω eirō (to *fasten*; akin to [G138](G138)); a *chain* (as *binding* or *drawing*): - chain.
o: probably from [G4951](G4951) through its congener eiro (to fasten, akin to [G138](G138))

d:
**1.** a shaking, a commotion
**2.** a tempest
**3.** an earthquake
s: From [G4579](G4579); a *commotion*, that is, (of the air) a *gale*, (of the ground) an *earthquake:* - earthquake, tempest.

d:
**1.** to shake, agitate, cause to tremble
  **a.** of men, to be thrown into a tremor, to quake for fear
  **b.** metaph. to agitate the mind
s: Apparently a primary verb; to *rock* (*vibrate*, properly sideways or to and fro), that is, (generally) to *agitate* (in any direction; cause to *tremble*); figuratively to throw into a *tremor* (of fear or concern): - move, quake, shake.

d:
Secundus = fortunate
**1.** a thessalonian Christian
s: Of Latin origin; “second”; *Secundus*, a Christian: - Secundus.

d:
Seleucia = white light
**1.** a city of Syria near the mouth of the Orontes, about 16 miles (25 km) from Antioch
s: From Σέλευκος Seleukos (*Seleucus*, a Syran king); *Seleuceia*, a place in Syria: - Seleucia.

d: **1.** the moon
s: From σέλας selas (*brilliancy*; probably akin to the alternate of [G138](G138), through the idea of *attractiveness*); the *moon:* - moon.
o: from selas (brilliancy, probably akin to the alternate of [G138](G138), through the idea of attractiveness)

d:
**1.** to be moon-struck or lunatic
**2.** to be epileptic
  **a.** epilepsy being supposed to return and increase with the increase of the moon. This meaning is doubtful as the Greeks knew nothing of epilepsy.
s: Middle or passive voice from a presumed derivative of [G4582](G4582); to *be* *moon* *struck*, that is, *crazy:* - be lunatic.
o: middle voice or passive from a presumed derivative of [G4582](G4582)

d:
Shimei = harkeners: my report
**1.** the father of Mattathias in the genealogy of christ
s: Of Hebrew origin \[[H8096](H8096)\]; *Semei* (that is, *Shimi*), an Israelite: - Semei.

d: **1.** the finest wheat flour
s: Probably of foreign origin; fine wheaten *flour:* - fine flour.

d:
**1.** august, venerable, reverend
**2.** to be venerated for character, honourable
  **a.** of persons
  **b.** of deeds
s: From [G4576](G4576); *venerable*, that is, *honorable:* - grave, honest.

d:
**1.** the characteristic of a thing or person which entitles to reverence and respect, dignity, majesty, sanctity
**2.** honour, purity
s: From [G4586](G4586); *venerableness*, that is, *probity:* - gravity, honesty.

d:
Sergius = earth-born: born a wonder
**1.** surnamed Paulus, a deputy or proconsul of Cyprus and converted to Christianity by Paul
s: Of Lat origin; *Sergius*, a Roman: - Sergius.

d:
Seth = compensation
**1.** the third son of Adam and the father of Enos
s: Of Hebrew origin \[[H8352](H8352)\]; *Seth* (that is, *Sheth*), a patriarch: - Seth.

d:
Shem meaning name
**1.** the eldest son of Noah
s: Of Hebrew origin \[[H8035](H8035)\]; *Sem* (that is, *Shem*), a patriarch: - Sem.

d:
**1.** to give a sign, to signify, indicate
**2.** to make known
s: From σῆμα sēma (a *mark*; of uncertain derivation); to *indicate:* - signify.
o: from sema (a mark, of uncertain derivation)

d:
**1.** a sign, mark, token
  **a.** that by which a person or a thing is distinguished from others and is known
  **b.** a sign, prodigy, portent, i.e. an unusual occurrence, transcending the common course of nature
    **1.** of signs portending remarkable events soon to happen
    **2.** of miracles and wonders by which God authenticates the men sent by him, or by which men prove that the cause they are pleading is God’s
s: Neuter of a presumed derivative of the base of [G4591](G4591); an *indication*, especially ceremonially or supernaturally: - miracle, sign, token, wonder.
o: from a presumed derivative of the base of [G4591](G4591)

d:
**1.** to mark, to note, distinguish by marking
**2.** to mark or note for one’s self
s: From [G4592](G4592); to *distinguish*, that is, *mark* (for avoidance): - note.

d:
**1.** this (very) day)
**2.** what has happened today
s: Neuter (as adverb) of a presumed compound of the article [G3588](G3588) (“tau” changed to “sigma”) and [G2250](G2250); on *the* (that is, *this*) *day* (or *night* current or just passed); genitively *now* (that is, at *present*, *hitherto*): - this (to-) day.
o: neuter (as adverb) of a presumed compound of the art. [G3588](G3588) and [G2250](G2250), on the (i.e. this) day (or night current or just passed)

d:
**1.** to make corrupt, to destroy
**2.** to become corrupt, corrupted, rotten
s: Apparently a primary verb; to *putrefy*, that is, (figuratively) *perish:* - be corrupted.

d:
**1.** made of silk
**2.** silk, i.e. the fabric, silken garments
s: From Σήρ Sēr (an Indian tribe from whom *silk* was procured; hence the name of the *silkworm*); *Seric*, that is, *silken* (neuter as noun, a *silky* fabric): - silk.
o: from Ser (an Indian tribe from whom silk was procured, hence the name of the silk-worm)

d: **1.** a moth, the clothes moth
s: Apparently of Hebrew origin \[[H5580](H5580)\]; a *moth:* - moth.

d: **1.** moth eaten
s: From [G4597](G4597) and a derivative of [G977](G977); *moth* *eaten:* - motheaten.

d:
**1.** to make strong, strengthen
  **a.** of one’s soul
s: From σθένος sthenos (bodily *vigor*; probably akin to the base of [G2476](G2476)); to *strengthen*, that is, (figuratively) *confirm* (in spiritual knowledge and power): - strengthen.
o: from sthenos (bodily vigour, probably akin to the base of [G2476](G2476))

d: **1.** the jaw, the jaw bone
s: Of uncertain derivation; the *jaw* bone, that is, (by implication) the *cheek* or side of the face: - cheek.

d:
**1.** to keep silence, hold one’s peace
**2.** to be kept in silence, be concealed
s: From [G4602](G4602); to *keep* *silent* (transitive or intransitive): - keep close (secret, silence), hold peace.

d: **1.** silence
s: Apparently from σίζω sizō (to *hiss*, that is, *hist* or *hush*); *silence:* - silence. Compare [G4623](G4623).
o: appr. from sizo (to hiss, i.e. hist or hush)

d: **1.** made of iron
s: From [G4604](G4604); made *of* *iron:* - (of) iron.

d: **1.** iron
s: Of uncertain derivation; *iron:* - iron.

d:
Sidon or Zidon = hunting
**1.** an ancient and wealthy city of Phoenicia, on the east coast of the mediterranean Sea, less than 20 miles (30 km) north of Tyre
s: Of Hebrew origin \[[H6721](H6721)\]; *Sidon* (that is, *Tsidon*), a place in Palestine: - Sidon.

d: **1.** an inhabitant of Sidon, a Sidonian
s: From [G4605](G4605); a *Sidonian*, that is, inhabitant of Sidon: - of Sidon.

d:
**1.** an assassin
  **a.** one who carries a dagger or short sword under his clothing, that he may kill secretly and treacherously any one he wishes to
  **b.** a cutthroat
s: Of Latin origin; a *dagger* *man* or *assassin*; a *freebooter* (Jewish *fanatic* outlawed by the Romans): - murderer. Compare [G5406](G5406).

d: **1.** strong drink, an intoxicating beverage, different from wine; it was a artificial product, made of a mixture of sweet ingredients, whether derived from grain and vegetables, or from the juice of fruits (dates), or a decoction of honey
s: Of Hebrew origin \[[H7941](H7941)\]; an *intoxicant*, that is, intensely fermented *liquor:* - strong drink.

d:
Silas = woody
**1.** a Roman citizen, the companion of the apostle Paul on several of his missionary journeys
s: Contraction for [G4610](G4610); *Silas*, a Christian: - Silas.

d:
Silas = woody
**1.** a Roman citizen, the companion of the apostle Paul on several of his missionary journeys
s: Of Latin origin; “silvan”; *Silvanus*, a Christian: - Silvanus. Compare [G4609](G4609).

d:
Siloam = sent
**1.** the Pool of Siloam, a fountain of water in Jerusalem, also called Shiloah in Isa 8:6
**2.** the Tower of Siloam, may have been a tower near or over the Pool of Siloam, which fell down killing 18 men; very likely they were purifying themselves. (Gill)
s: Of Hebrew origin \[[H7975](H7975)\]; *Siloam* (that is, *Shiloach*), a pool of Jerusalem: - Siloam.

d: **1.** a narrow apron, or linen covering, which workmen and servants were accustomed to wear
s: Of Latin origin; a *semicinctium* or *half* *girding*, that is, narrow covering (*apron*): - apron.

d:
Peter = a rock or stone
**1.** Peter was one of the apostles
**2.** Simon called Zelotes or the Kanaites
**3.** Simon, father of Judas who betrayed Jesus.
**4.** Simon Magus, the Samaritan wizard
**5.** Simon the tanner, Ac.
**6.** Simon the Pharisee, Luk 7:40-
**7.** Simon of Cyrene who carried the cross of christ
**8.** Simon the cousin of Jesus, the son of Cleophas
**9.** Simon the leper, so called to distinguish him from others of the same name
s: Of Hebrew origin \[[H8095](H8095)\]; *Simon* (that is, *Shimon*), the name of nine Israelites: - Simon. Compare [G4826](G4826).

d:
sinai = thorny
**1.** a mountain or rather a mountainous region in the peninsula of Arabia Petraea, made famous by the giving of the Mosaic law
s: Of Hebrew origin \[[H5514](H5514)\]; *Sina* (that is, *Sinai*), a mountain in Arabia: - Sina.

d: **1.** mustard, the name of a plant which in oriental countries grows from a very small seed and attains to the height of a tree, 10 feet (3 m) and more; hence a very small quantity of a thing is likened to a mustard seed, and also a thing which grows to a remarkable size
s: Perhaps from σίνομαι sinomai (to *hurt*, that is, *sting*); *mustard* (the plant): - mustard.
o: perhaps from sinomai (to hurt, i.e. sting)

d:
**1.** linen cloth, esp. that which was fine and costly, in which the bodies of the dead were wrapped
**2.** thing made of fine cloth
  **a.** of a light and loose garment worn at night over a naked body
s: Of uncertain (perhaps foreign) origin; *byssos*, that is, bleached *linen* (the cloth or a garment of it): - (fine) linen (cloth).

d:
**1.** to sift, shake in a sieve
**2.** fig. by inward agitation to try one’s faith to the verge of overthrow
s:
sin-ee-ad’-zo
From σινιον sinion (a *sieve*); to *riddle* (figuratively): - sift.

d: **1.** fattened, fatted
s: From a derivative of [G4621](G4621); *grain* *fed*, that is, *fattened:* - fatted.

d: **1.** fattened
s: From a derivative of [G4621](G4621); *grained* that is, *fatted:* - fatling.

d: **1.** a measured ’portion of’ grain or ’food’
s: From [G4621](G4621) and [G3358](G3358); a *grain* *measure*, that is, (by implication) *ration* (*allowance* of food): - portion of meat.

d: **1.** wheat, grain
s: σῖτα sita *see’-tah* is the plural irregular neuter of the first form. Of uncertain derivation; *grain*, especially *wheat:* - corn, wheat.
o: plural irregular neuter sita see’-tah, of uncertain derivation

d:
Sion or Zion = a parched place
**1.** the hill on which the higher and more ancient part of Jerusalem was built
  **a.** the southwestern most and highest of the hills on which the city was built
**2.** often used of the entire city of Jerusalem
**3.** since Jerusalem because the temple stood there, was called the dwelling place of God
s: Of Hebrew origin \[[H6726](H6726)\]; *Sion* (that is, *Tsijon*), a hill of Jerusalem; figuratively the *Church* (militant or triumphant): - Sion.

d:
**1.** to be silent, hold one’s peace
  **a.** used of one’s silence because dumb
**2.** metaph. of a calm, quiet sea
s: From σιωπη siōpē (*silence*, that is, a *hush*; properly *muteness*, that is, *involuntary* stillness, or *inability* ot speak; and thus differing from [G4602](G4602), which is rather a voluntary *refusal* or *indisposition* to speak, although the terms are often used synonymously); to *be* *dumb* (but not *deaf* also, like [G2974](G2974) properly); figuratively to *be* *calm* (as *quiet* water): - dumb, (hold) peace.
o: from siope (silence, i.e. a hush, properly, muteness, i.e. involuntary stillness, or inability to speak, and thus differing from [G4602](G4602), which is rather a voluntary refusal or indisposition to speak, although the terms are often used synonymously)

d:
**1.** to put a stumbling block or impediment in the way, upon which another may trip and fall, metaph. to offend
  **a.** to entice to sin
  **b.** to cause a person to begin to distrust and desert one whom he ought to trust and obey
    **1.** to cause to fall away
    **2.** to be offended in one, i.e. to see in another what I disapprove of and what hinders me from acknowledging his authority
    **3.** to cause one to judge unfavourably or unjustly of another
  **c.** since one who stumbles or whose foot gets entangled feels annoyed
    **1.** to cause one displeasure at a thing
    **2.** to make indignant
    **3.** to be displeased, indignant
s: To “scandalize”; from [G4625](G4625); to *entrap*, that is, *trip* up (figuratively *stumble* \[transitively\] or *entice* to sin, apostasy or displeasure): - (make to) offend.

d:
**1.** the movable stick or trigger of a trap, a trap stick
  **a.** a trap, snare
  **b.** any impediment placed in the way and causing one to stumble or fall, (a stumbling block, occasion of stumbling) i.e. a rock which is a cause of stumbling
  **c.** fig. applied to Jesus christ, whose person and career were so contrary to the expectations of the Jews concerning the messiah, that they rejected him and by their obstinacy made shipwreck of their salvation
**2.** any person or thing by which one is (entrapped) drawn into error or sin
s: A “scandal”; probably from a derivative of [G2578](G2578); a *trap* *stick* (*bent* sapling), that is, *snare* (figuratively *cause* of displeasure or sin): - occasion to fall (of stumbling), offence, thing that offends, stumbling-block.

d: **1.** to dig
s: Apparently a primary verb; to *dig:* - dig.

d:
**1.** anything dug out, hollow vessel, trough, tray, tub
**2.** of a boat
s: A “skiff” (as if *dug* out), or *yawl* (carried aboard a large vessel for landing): - boat.

d: **1.** the leg, from the hip to the toes inclusive
s: Apparently from σκέλλω skellō (to *parch*; through the idea of *leanness*); the *leg* (as *lank*): - leg.
o: apparently from skello (to parch, through the idea of leanness)

d: **1.** a covering, spec. clothing
s: From a derivative of “skepas” (a *covering*; perhaps akin to the base of [G4649](G4649) through the idea of *noticeableness*); *clothing:* - raiment.
o: from a derivative of skepas (a covering

d:
Sceva = mind reader
**1.** a certain chief priest residing at Ephesus
s: Apparently of Latin origin; *left* *handed*; *Scevas* (that is, *Scaevus*), an Israelite: - Sceva.

d:
**1.** any apparatus, equipment, or furniture
  **a.** of the utensils or tackling of a ship
s: From [G4632](G4632); *furniture*, that is, spare *tackle:* - tackling.

d:
**1.** a vessel
**2.** an implement
  **a.** in the plural
    **1.** household utensils, domestic gear
    **2.** the tackle and armament of vessels, used specifically of sails and ropes
**3.** metaph.
  **a.** a man of quality, a chosen instrument
  **b.** in a bad sense, an assistant in accomplishing an evil deed Vessel was a common Greek metaphor for body since Greeks thoughtof souls living temporarily in bodies.
s: Of uncertain affinity; a *vessel*, *implement*, *equipment* or *apparatus* (literally or figuratively \[specifically a *wife* as contributing to the usefulness of the husband\]): - goods, sail, stuff, vessel.

d:
**1.** tent, tabernacle, (made of green boughs, or skins or other materials)
**2.** of that well known movable temple of God after the pattern of which the temple at Jerusalem was built
s: Apparently akin to [G4632](G4632) and [G4639](G4639); a *tent* or cloth hut (literally or figuratively): - habitation, tabernacle.

d:
**1.** the construction of a tabernacle or tabernacles
**2.** the feast of tabernacles; this festival was observed by the Jews yearly for seven days, beginning with the 15th of the month Tisri (approx. our Oct.) partly to perpetuate the memory of the time when their ancestors after leaving Egypt dwelt in tents on their way through the Arabian desert, and partly as a season of festivity and joy on the completion of the harvest and the vintage (the festival of ingatherings) In celebrating the festival the Jews were accustomed to construct booths of the leafy branches of trees, -- either on the roofs or in the courts of their dwellings, or in the streets and squares, and to adorn them with flowers and fruits of all kinds -- under which, throughout the period of the festival, they feasted and gave themselves up to rejoicing.
s: From [G4636](G4636) and [G4078](G4078); the *Festival* *of* *Tabernacles* (so called from the custom of erecting booths for temporary homes): - tabernacles.

d:
**1.** a tentmaker
**2.** one that makes small portable tents, of leather or cloth of goat’s hair or linen, for the use of travellers
s: From [G4633](G4633) and [G4160](G4160); a *manufacturer* *of* *tents:* - tentmaker.

d:
**1.** a tabernacle, a tent
**2.** metaph. of the human body, in which the soul dwells as in a tent, and which is taken down at death
s: From [G4633](G4633); a *hut* or temporary residence, that is, (figuratively) the human *body* (as the abode of the spirit): - tabernacle.

d:
**1.** to fix one’s tabernacle, have one’s tabernacle, abide (or live) in a tabernacle (or tent), tabernacle
**2.** to dwell
s: From [G4636](G4636); to *tent* or *encamp*, that is, (figuratively) to *occupy* (as a mansion) or (specifically) to *reside* (as God did in the Tabernacle of old, a symbol fo protection and communion): - dwell.

d:
**1.** a tent, a tabernacle
  **a.** of the temple as God’s habitation
  **b.** of the tabernacle of the covenant
  **c.** metaph. of the human body as the dwelling of the soul
s: From [G4637](G4637); an *encampment*, that is, (figuratively) the *Temple* (as God’s residence), the *body* (as a tenement for the soul): - tabernacle.

d:
**1.** shadow
  **a.** shade caused by the interception of light
  **b.** an image cast by an object and representing the form of that object
  **c.** a sketch, outline, adumbration
s: Apparently a primary word; “shade” or a shadow (literally or figuratively \[darkness of *error* or an *adumbration*\]): - shadow.

d: **1.** to leap
s: Akin to σκαίρω skairō (to *skip*); to *jump*, that is, sympathetically *move* (as the *quickening* of a fetus): - leap (for joy).

d: **1.** hardness of heart
s: Feminine of a compound of [G4642](G4642) and [G2588](G2588); *hard* *heartedness*, that is, (specifically) *destitution* *of* (spiritual) *perception:* - hardness of heart.

d:
**1.** hard, harsh, rough, stiff
  **a.** of men: metaph. harsh, stern, hard
  **b.** of things: violent, rough, offensive, intolerable
s: From the base of [G4628](G4628); *dry*, that is, *hard* or *tough* (figuratively *harsh*, *severe*): - fierce, hard.

d:
**1.** hardness
**2.** obstinacy, stubbornness
s: From [G4642](G4642); *callousness*, that is, (figuratively) *stubbornness:* - hardness.

d:
**1.** stiffnecked
**2.** stubborn, headstrong, obstinate
s: From [G4642](G4642) and [G5137](G5137); *hard* *naped*, that is, (figuratively) *obstinate:* - stiffnecked.

d:
**1.** to make hard, harden
**2.** metaph.
  **a.** to render obstinate, stubborn
  **b.** to be hardened
  **c.** to become obstinate or stubborn
s: From [G4642](G4642); to *indurate*, that is, (figuratively) *render* *stubborn:* - harden.

d:
**1.** crooked, curved
**2.** metaph.
  **a.** perverse, wicked
  **b.** unfair, surly, froward
s: From the base of [G4628](G4628); *warped*, that is, *winding*; figuratively *perverse:* - crooked, froward, untoward.

d:
**1.** a pointed piece of wood, a pale, a stake
**2.** a sharp stake, splinter
s: Perhaps form the base of [G4628](G4628) and [G3700](G3700); *withered* at the *front*, that is, a *point* or *prickle* (figuratively a bodily *annoyance* or *disability*): - thorn.
o: perhaps from the base of [G4628](G4628) and [G3700](G3700)

d:
**1.** to look at, observe, contemplate
**2.** to mark
**3.** to fix one’s eyes upon, direct one’s attention to, any one
**4.** to look to, take heed to thyself
s: From [G4649](G4649); to take *aim* at (*spy*), that is, (figuratively) *regard:* - consider, take heed, look at (on), mark. Compare [G3700](G3700).

d:
**1.** an observer, a watchman
**2.** the distant mark looked at, the goal or end one has in view
s: (“scope”); From σκέπτομαι skeptomai (to *peer* about \[“skeptic”\]; perhaps akin to [G4626](G4626) through the idea of *concealment*; compare [G4629](G4629)); a *watch* (*sentry* or *scout*), that is, (by implication) a *goal:* - mark.
o: from skeptomai (to peer about \[skeptic\], perhaps akin to [G4626](G4626) through the idea of concealment, cf [G4629](G4629))

d:
**1.** to scatter
  **a.** of those who, routed or terror stricken or driven by some other impulses, fly in every direction
  **b.** to scatter abroad (what others may collect for themselves), or one dispensing blessings literally
s: Apparently from the same as [G4651](G4651) (through the idea of *penetrating*); to *dissipate*, that is, (figuratively) *put* *to* *flight*, *waste*, *be* *liberal:* - disperse abroad, scatter (abroad).
o: apparently from the same as [G4651](G4651) (through the idea of penetrating)

d: **1.** a scorpion, the name of a little animal, somewhat resembling a lobster, which in warm regions lurk, esp. in stone walls; it has a poisonous sting in its tail
s: Probably from σκέρπω skerpō, an obsolete word, (perhaps strengthened from the base of [G4649](G4649) and meaning to *pierce*); a “scorpion” (from its *sting*): - scorpion.
o: probably from an obsolete skerpo (perhaps strengthened from the base of [G4649](G4649) and meaning to pierce)

d: **1.** full of darkness, covered with darkness
s: From [G4655](G4655); *opaque*, that is, (figuratively) *benighted:* - dark, full of darkness.

d:
**1.** darkness
**2.** the darkness due to want of light
**3.** metaph. used of ignorance of divine things, and its associated wickedness, and the resultant misery in hell
s: From [G4655](G4655); *dimness*, *obscurity* (literally or figuratively): - dark (-ness).

d:
**1.** to cover with darkness, to darken
**2.** to be covered with darkness, be darkened
  **a.** of heavenly bodies as deprived of light
  **b.** metaph.
    **1.** of the eyes
    **2.** of the understanding
    **3.** of the mind
s: From [G4655](G4655); to *obscure* (literally or figuratively): - darken.

d:
**1.** darkness
  **a.** of night darkness
  **b.** of darkened eyesight or blindness
**2.** metaph.
  **a.** of ignorance respecting divine things and human duties, and the accompanying ungodliness and immorality, together with their consequent misery in hell
  **b.** persons in whom darkness becomes visible and holds sway
s: From the base of [G4639](G4639); *shadiness*, that is, *obscurity* (literally or figuratively): - darkness.

d:
**1.** to darken, cover with darkness
**2.** metaph. to darken or blind the mind
s: From [G4655](G4655); to *obscure* or *blind* (literally or figuratively): - be full of darkness.

d:
**1.** any refuse, as the excrement of animals, offscourings, rubbish, dregs
  **a.** of things worthless and detestable
s: Neuter of a presumed derivative of [G1519](G1519) and [G2965](G2965) and [G906](G906); what is *thrown* *to* the *dogs*, that is, *refuse* (*ordure*): - dung.
o: neuter of a presumed derivative of [G1519](G1519) and [G2965](G2965) and [G906](G906)

d:
Scythian = rude or rough
**1.** a Scythian, an inhabitant of Scythia or modern day Russia
  **a.** by the more civilised nations of antiquity the Scythians were regarded as the wildest of barbarians
s: Probably of foreign origin; a *Scythene* or *Scythian*, that is, (by implication) a *savage:* - Scythian.

d: **1.** of a sad and gloomy countenance
s: From σκυθρός skuthros (*sullen*) and a derivative of [G3700](G3700); *angry* *visaged*, that is, *gloomy* or affecting a *mournful* appearance: - of a sad countenance.
o: from skuthros (sullen) and a derivative of [G3700](G3700)

d:
**1.** to skin, flay
**2.** to rend, mangle
  **a.** to vex, trouble, annoy
  **b.** to give one’s self trouble, trouble one’s self
s: Apparently a primary verb; to *flay*, that is, (figuratively) to *harass:* - trouble (self).

d:
**1.** a (beast’s) skin stripped off, a pelt
**2.** the weapons and valuables stripped off from an enemy, spoils
s: Neuter from [G4660](G4660); something *stripped* (as a *hide*), that is, *booty:* - spoil.

d: **1.** eaten of worms
s: From [G4663](G4663) and a derivative of [G977](G977); *worm* *eaten*, that is, *diseased* *with* *maggots:* - eaten of worms.

d: **1.** a worm, spec. that kind which preys upon dead bodies
s: Of uncertain derivative; a *grub*, *maggot* or *earth* *worm:* - worm.

d: **1.** of emerald, made of emerald
s: From [G4665](G4665); consisting *of* *emerald:* - emerald.

d: **1.** a transparent precious stone noted especially for its light green colour
s: Of uncertain derivation; the *emerald* or green gem so called: - emerald.

d: **1.** myrrh, a bitter gum and costly perfume which exudes from a certain tree or shrub in Arabia and Ethiopia, or is obtained by incisions made in the bark: as an antiseptic it was used for embalming
s: Apparently strengthened for [G3464](G3464); *myrrh:* - myrrh.

d:
Smyrna = myrrh
**1.** an Ionian city of Asia Minor, on the Aegean Sea, 40 miles (65 km) north of Ephesus
s: The same as [G4666](G4666); *Smyrna*, a place in Asia Minor: - Smyrna.

d: **1.** of or belonging to Smyrna, an inhabitant of Smyrna
s: From [G4667](G4667); a *Smyrnaean:* - in Smyrna.

d:
**1.** to be like myrrh
**2.** to mix and so flavour with myrrh
  **a.** wine with myrrh: i.e. wine flavoured with myrrh. The ancients used to infuse myrrh into wine to give it a more agreeable fragrance and flavour
s: From [G4667](G4667); to *tincture* *with* *myrrh*, that is, *embitter* (as a narcotic): - mingle with myrrh.

d:
Sodom = burning
**1.** a city destroyed by the Lord raining fire and brimstone on it
**2.** metaph. Jerusalem Rev 11:8
s: Plural, of Hebrew origin \[[H5467](H5467)\]; *Sodoma* (that is, *Sedom*), a place in Palestine: - Sodom.

d: **1.** to you
s: Dative case of [G4771](G4771); *to* *thee:* - thee, thine own, thou, thy.

d:
Solomon = peaceful
**1.** the son of David and was the wisest and richest king that ever lived
s: Of Hebrew origin \[[H8010](H8010)\]; *Solomon* (that is, *Shelomoh*), the son of David: - Solomon.

d:
**1.** an urn or receptacle for keeping the bones of the dead
**2.** the funeral couch or bier on which the Jews carried their dead forth to burial
s: Probably akin to the base of [G4987](G4987); a *funereal* *receptacle* (*urn*, *coffin*), that is, (by analogy) a *bier:* - bier.
o: probably akin to the base of [G4987](G4987)

d: **1.** thy, thine
s: From [G4771](G4771); *thine:* - thine (own), thy (friend).

d: **1.** thy, thee
s: Genitive case of [G4771](G4771); *of* *thee*, *thy:* - X home, thee, thine (own), thou, thy.

d:
**1.** a handkerchief
**2.** a cloth for wiping perspiration from the face and for cleaning the nose and also used in swathing the head of a corpse
s: Of Latin origin; a *sudarium* (*sweat* *cloth*), that is, *towel* (for wiping the perspiration from the face, or binding the face of a corpse): - handerchief, napkin.

d:
Susanna = a lily
**1.** one of the women who ministered to christ
s: Of Hebrew origin \[[H7799](H7799)\] (feminine); *lily*; *Susannah* (that is, *Shoshannah*), an Israelitess: - Susanna.

d:
**1.** wisdom, broad and full of intelligence; used of the knowledge of very diverse matters
  **a.** the wisdom which belongs to men
    **1.** spec. the varied knowledge of things human and divine, acquired by acuteness and experience, and summed up in maxims and proverbs
    **2.** the science and learning
    **3.** the act of interpreting dreams and always giving the sagest advice
    **4.** the intelligence evinced in discovering the meaning of some mysterious number or vision
    **5.** skill in the management of affairs
    **6.** devout and proper prudence in intercourse with men not disciples of christ, skill and discretion in imparting Christian truth
