    **7.** the knowledge and practice of the requisites for Godly and upright living
  **b.** supreme intelligence, such as belongs to God
    **1.** to christ
    **2.** the wisdom of God as evinced in forming and executing counsels in the formation and government of the world and the scriptures
s: From [G4680](G4680); *wisdom* (higher or lower, worldly or spiritual): - wisdom.

d:
**1.** to make wise, teach
**2.** to become wise, to have understanding
  **a.** to invent, play the sophist
  **b.** to devise cleverly or cunningly
s: From [G4680](G4680); to *render* *wise*; in a sinister acceptation, to *form* “sophisms”, that is, *continue* *plausible* *error:* - cunningly devised, make wise.

d:
**1.** wise
  **a.** skilled, expert: of artificers
  **b.** wise, skilled in letters, cultivated, learned
    **1.** of the Greek philosophers and orators
    **2.** of Jewish theologians
    **3.** of Christian teachers
  **c.** forming the best plans and using the best means for their execution
s: Akin to σαφής saphēs (*clear*); *wise* (in a most general application): - wise. Compare [G5429](G5429).

d:
Spain = scarceness
**1.** the whole peninsula south of the Pyrenees
s: Probably of foreign origin; *Spania*, a region of Europe: - Spain.

d: **1.** to convulse, tear
s: Prolongation from σπαίρω spairō̄ (to *gasp*; apparently strengthened from [G4685](G4685) through the idea of *spasmodic* contraction); to *mangle*, that is, *convulse* with epilepsy: - rend, tear.
o: prolongation from spairo (to grasp, apparently strengthened from [G4685](G4685) through the idea of spasmodic contraction)

d:
**1.** to wrap in swaddling clothes
  **a.** of an infant just born
s: From σπάργανον sparganon (a *strip*; from a derivative of the base of [G4682](G4682) meaning to *strap* or *wrap* with strips); to *swathe* (an infant after the Oriental custom): - wrap in swaddling clothes.
o: from sparganon (a strip, from a derivative of the base of [G4682](G4682) meaning to strap or wrap with strips)

d: **1.** to live luxuriously, lead a voluptuous life, (give one’s self to pleasure)
s: From σπατάλη spatalē (*luxury*); to *be* *voluptuous:* - live in pleasure, be wanton.

d:
**1.** to draw
**2.** to draw (one’s sword)
s: A primary verb; to *draw:* - draw (out).

d:
**1.** anything rolled into a circle or ball, anything wound, rolled up, folded together
**2.** a military cohort
  **a.** the tenth part of legion
    **1.** about 600 men i.e. legionaries
    **2.** if auxiliaries either 500 or 1000
    **3.** a maniple, or the thirtieth part of a legion
  **b.** any band, company, or detachment, of soldiers
s: Of immediate Latin origin, but ultimately a derivative of [G138](G138) in the sense of its cognate, [G1507](G1507); a *coil* (*spira*, “spire”), that is, (figuratively) a *mass* of men (a Roman military *cohort*; also \[by analogy\] a *squad* of Levitical janitors): - band.
o: of immed. Latin origin, but ultimately a derivative of [G138](G138) in the sense of its cognate [G1507](G1507)

d:
**1.** to sow, scatter, seed
**2.** metaph. of proverbial sayings
s: Probably strengthened from [G4685](G4685) (through the idea of *extending*); to *scatter*, that is, *sow* (literally or figuratively): - sow (-er), receive seed.
o: probably strengthened from [G4685](G4685) (through the idea of extending)

d:
**1.** a spy, scout
**2.** under the emperors an attendant and member of the body guard, employed as messengers, watchers, and executioners
**3.** the name is transferred to an attendant of herod Antipas that acted as executioner
s: Of Latin origin; a *speculator*, that is, military *scout* (*spy* or \[by extension\] *life* *guardsman*): - executioner.

d:
**1.** to pour out as a drink offering, make a libation
**2.** in the NT to be offered as a libation
**3.** fig. used of one whose blood is poured out in a violent death for the cause of God
s: Apparently a primary verb; to *pour* out as a libation, that is, (figuratively) to *devote* (one’s life or blood, as a sacrifice) (“spend”): - (be ready to) be offered.

d:
**1.** from which a plant germinates
  **a.** the seed i.e. the grain or kernel which contains within itself the germ of the future plants
    **1.** of the grains or kernels sown
  **b.** metaph. a seed i.e. a residue, or a few survivors reserved as the germ of the next generation (just as seed is kept from the harvest for the sowing)
**2.** the semen virile
  **a.** the product of this semen, seed, children, offspring, progeny
  **b.** family, tribe, posterity
  **c.** whatever possesses vital force or life giving power
    **1.** of divine energy of the holy spirit operating within the soul by which we are regenerated
s: From [G4687](G4687); somethng *sown*, that is, *seed* (including the male “sperm”); by implication *offspring*; specifically a *remnant* (figuratively as if kept over for planting): - issue, seed.

d:
**1.** picking up seed
  **a.** of birds, esp. of the crow or daw that picks up grain in fields
**2.** metaph.
  **a.** lounging about the market place and picking up a substance by whatever may chance to fall from the loads of merchandise
  **b.** hence, beggarly, abject, vile, (a parasite)
  **c.** getting a living by flattery and bufferoonery
  **d.** an empty talker, babbler
s: From [G4690](G4690) and [G3004](G3004); a *seed* *picker* (as the crow), that is, (figuratively) a *sponger*, *loafer* (specifically a *gossip* or *trifler* in talk): - babbler.

d:
**1.** to haste, make haste
**2.** to desire earnestly
s: Probably strengthened from [G4228](G4228); to “speed” (“study”), that is, *urge* on (diligently or earnestly); by implication to *await* eagerly: - (make, with) haste unto.

d: **1.** a cave, den
s: Neuter of a presumed derivation of σπέος speos (a *grotto*); a *cavern*; by implication a *hiding* *place* or *resort:* - cave, den.
o: from a presumed derivative of speos (a grotto)

d:
**1.** a rock in the sea, ledge, reef
**2.** metaph. of men who by their conduct damage others morally, wreck them as it were
s: Of uncertain derivation; a *ledge* or *reef* of rock in the sea: - spot \[by confusion with [G4696](G4696)\].

d: **1.** to defile, spot
s: From [G4696](G4696); to *stain* or *soil* (literally or figuratively): - defile, spot.

d:
**1.** a spot
**2.** a fault, moral blemish
  **a.** of base and gluttonous men
s: Of uncertain derivation; a *stain* or *blemish*, that is, (figuratively) *defect*, *disgrace:* - spot.

d: **1.** to be moved as to one’s bowels, hence to be moved with compassion, have compassion (for the bowels were thought to be the seat of love and pity)
s: Middle voice from [G4698](G4698); to have the *bowels* yearn, that is, (figuratively) *feel* *sympathy*, to *pity:* - have (be moved with) compassion.

d:
**1.** bowels, intestines, (the heart, lungs, liver, etc.)
  **a.** bowels
  **b.** the bowels were regarded as the seat of the more violent passions, such as anger and love; but by the hebrews as the seat of the tenderer affections, esp. kindness, benevolence, compassion; hence our heart (tender mercies, affections, etc.)
  **c.** a heart in which mercy resides
s:
Probably strengthened from σπλήν
splēn
(the “spleen”); an *intestine* (plural); figuratively *pity* or *sympathy:* - bowels, inward affection, + tender mercy.

d: **1.** sponge
s: Perhaps of foreign origin; a “sponge”: - spunge.

d: **1.** ashes: placed on sackcloth as a token of grief
s: Of uncertain derivation; *ashes:* - ashes.

d: **1.** seed
s: From [G4687](G4687); a *sowing*, that is, (by implication) *parentage:* - seed.

d:
**1.** fit for sowing, sown
**2.** sown fields, growing crops
s: From [G4703](G4703); *sown*, that is, (neuter plural) a planted *field:* - corn (-field).

d:
**1.** a sowing
**2.** seed (used in sowing)
s: From [G4687](G4687); a *scattering* (of seed), that is, (concretely) *seed* (as sown): - seed (X sown).

d:
**1.** to hasten, make haste
**2.** to exert one’s self, endeavour, give diligence
s: From [G4710](G4710); to *use* *speed*, that is, to *make* *effort*, *be* *prompt* or *earnest:* - do (give) diligence, be diligent (forward), endeavour, labour, study.

d:
**1.** active, diligent, zealous, earnest
**2.** very diligent
s: From [G4710](G4710); *prompt*, *energetic*, *earnest:* - diligent.

d: **1.** very diligently
s: Neuter of [G4707](G4707) as adverb; *more* *earnestly* than others), that is, very *promptly:* - very diligently.

d:
**1.** active, diligent, zealous, earnest
**2.** very diligent
s: Comparative of [G4705](G4705); *more* *prompt*, *more* *earnest:* - more diligent (forward).

d:
**1.** hastily, with haste
**2.** diligently, earnestly
s: Adverb from [G4707](G4707); *more* *speedily*, that is, *sooner* than otherwise: - more carefully.

d:
**1.** hastily, with haste
**2.** diligently
**3.** earnestly
s: Adverb from [G4705](G4705); *earnestly*, *promptly:* - diligently, instantly.

d:
**1.** haste, with haste
**2.** earnestness, diligence
  **a.** earnestness in accomplishing, promoting, or striving after anything
  **b.** to give all diligence, interest one’s self most earnestly
s: From [G4692](G4692); “speed”, that is, (by implication) *despatch*, *eagerness*, *earnestness:* - business, (earnest) care (-fulness), diligence forwardness, haste.

d: **1.** a reed basket, (a plaited basket, a lunch basket, hamper)
s: From [G4687](G4687) (as *woven*); a *hamper* or *lunch* *receptacle:* - basket.

d:
**1.** a space or distance of about 600 feet (185 m)
**2.** a race course
  **a.** place in which contests in running were held, the one who outstripped the rest and reached the goal first, receiving the prize. Courses of this description were found in most of the larger Greek cities, and were like that at Olympia, 600 Greek feet in length
s:
Or the masculine plural form, στάδιος stadios *stad’-ee-os*.
From the base of [G2476](G2476) (as *fixed*); a *stade* or certain measure of distance; by implication a *stadium* or *race* *course:* - furlong, race.
o: or masculine (in plural) stadios stad’-ee-os, from the base of [G2476](G2476) (as fixed)

d:
**1.** among the Greeks an earthen jar, into which wine was drawn off for keeping but also used for other purposes
  **a.** of the little jar in which the manna was kept, laid up in the ark of the covenant
s: From the base of [G2476](G2476) (as *stationary*); a *jar* or earthen *tank:* - pot.

d:
**1.** a standing, station, state
**2.** an insurrection
**3.** strife, insurrection
s: From the base of [G2476](G2476); a *standing* (properly the act), that is, (by analogy) *position* (*existence*); by implication a popular *uprising*; figuratively *controversy:* - dissension, insurrection, X standing, uproar.

d:
**1.** a stater, a coin
  **a.** in the NT a silver stater equal to four Attic or two Alexandrian drachmas, a Jewish shekel
s: From the base of [G2746](G2746); a *stander* (*standard* of value), that is, (specifically) a *stater* or certain coin: - piece of money.

d:
**1.** an upright stake, esp. a pointed one
**2.** a cross
  **a.** a well known instrument of most cruel and ignominious punishment, borrowed by the Greeks and Romans from the Phoenicians; to it were affixed among the Romans, down to the time of Constantine the great, the guiltiest criminals, particularly the basest slaves, robbers, the authors and abetters of insurrections, and occasionally in the provinces, at the arbitrary pleasure of the governors, upright and peaceable men also, and even Roman citizens themselves
  **b.** the crucifixion which christ underwent
s: From the base of [G2476](G2476); a *stake* or *post* (as *set* upright), that is, (specifically) a *pole* or *cross* (as an instrument of capital punishment); figuratively *exposure* *to* *death*, that is, *self* *denial*; by implication the *atonement* of Christ: - cross.

d:
**1.** to stake, drive down stakes
**2.** to fortify with driven stakes, to palisade
**3.** to crucify
  **a.** to crucify one
  **b.** metaph. to crucify the flesh, destroy its power utterly (the nature of the figure implying that the destruction is attended with intense pain)
s: From [G4716](G4716); to *impale* on the cross; figuratively to *extinguish* (*subdue*) passion or selfishness: - crucify.

d: **1.** grapes, bunch of grapes
s: Probably from the base of [G4735](G4735); a *cluster* of grapes (as if *intertwined*): - grapes.

d: **1.** an ear of corn or of growing grain
s: From the base of [G2476](G2476); a *head* of grain (as *standing* out from the stalk): - ear (of corn).

d:
Stachys = a head of grain
**1.** a man with a Greek name, he is said to be one of the seventy disciples, and bishop of Byzantium (Gill)
s: The same as [G4719](G4719); *Stachys*, a Christian: - Stachys.

d: **1.** a roof: of a house
s: Strengthened from a primary word τέγος tegos (a “thatch” or “deck” of building); a *roof:* - roof.
o: strengthened from a primary tegos (a thatch or deck of a building)

d:
**1.** deck, thatch, to cover
  **a.** to protect or keep by covering, to preserve
**2.** to cover over with silence
  **a.** to keep secret
  **b.** to hide, conceal
    **1.** of the errors and faults of others
**3.** by covering to keep off something which threatens, to bear up against, hold out against, and so endure, bear, forbear
s: From [G4721](G4721); to *roof* over, that is, (figuratively) to *cover* with silence (*endure* patiently): - (for-) bear, suffer.

d:
**1.** hard, stiff
  **a.** of men and animals
**2.** barren
  **a.** of woman who does not conceive
s: A contraction from [G4731](G4731) (as *stiff* and *unnatural*); “sterile”: - barren.
o: a contraction from [G4731](G4731) (as stiff and unnatural)

d:
**1.** to set, place, set in order, arrange
  **a.** to fit out, to prepare, equip
  **b.** to prepare one’s self, to fit out for one’s self
  **c.** to fit out for one’s own use
  **d.** to prepare one’s self, to fit out for one’s self
  **e.** to fit out for one’s own use
    **1.** arranging, providing for this, etc.
**2.** to bring together, contract, shorten
  **a.** to diminish, check, cause to cease
  **b.** to cease to exist
  **c.** to remove one’s self, withdraw one’s self, to depart
  **d.** to abstain from familiar intercourse with one
s: Probably strengthened from the base of [G2476](G2476); properly to *set* fast (“stall”), that is, (figuratively) to *repress* (reflexively *abstain* from associating with): - avoid, withdraw self.
o: probably strengthened from the base of [G2476](G2476)

d: **1.** a fillet, a garland, put upon victims
s: From the base of [G4735](G4735); a *wreath* for show: - garland.

d: **1.** a groaning, a sigh
s: From [G4727](G4727); a *sigh:* - groaning.

d: **1.** a sigh, to groan
s: From [G4728](G4728); to *make* (intransitively *be*) *in* *straits*, that is, (by implication) to *sigh*, *murmur*, *pray* inaudibly: - with grief, groan, grudge, sigh.

d: **1.** narrow, strait
s: Probably from the base of [G2476](G2476); *narrow* (from obstacles *standing* close about): - strait.

d:
**1.** to be in a narrow place
**2.** to straiten, compress, cramp, reduce to straits
  **a.** to be sorely straitened in spirit
s: From the same as [G4730](G4730); to *hem* in closely, that is, (figuratively) *cramp:* - distress, straiten.

d:
**1.** narrowness of place, a narrow place
**2.** metaph. dire calamity, extreme affliction
s: From a compound of [G4728](G4728) and [G5561](G5561); *narrowness* *of* *room*, that is, (figuratively) *calamity:* - anguish, distress.

d:
**1.** strong, firm, immovable, solid, hard, rigid
  **a.** in a bad sense, cruel, stiff, stubborn, hard
  **b.** in a good sense, firm, steadfast
s: From [G2476](G2476); *stiff*, that is, *solid*, *stable* (literally or figuratively): - stedfast, strong, sure.

d:
**1.** to make solid, make firm, strengthen, make strong
  **a.** of the body of anyone
s: From [G4731](G4731); to *solidify*, that is, *confirm* (literally or figuratively): - establish, receive strength, make strong.

d:
**1.** that which has been made firm
  **a.** the firmament, the arch of the sky, which in early times was thought to be solid
    **1.** a fortified place
  **b.** that which furnishes a foundation
    **1.** on which a thing rests firmly, support
  **c.** firmness, steadfastness
    **1.** metaph. in a military sense: solid front
s: From [G4732](G4732); something *established*, that is, (abstractly) *confirmation* (*stability*): - stedfastness.

d:
Stephanas = crowned
**1.** a Christian convert of Corinth
s: Probably contraction for στεφανωτός stephanōtos (*crowned*; from [G4737](G4737)); *Stephanas*, a Christian: - Stephanas.

d:
**1.** a crown
  **a.** a mark of royal or (in general) exalted rank
    **1.** the wreath or garland which was given as a prize to victors in public games
  **b.** metaph. the eternal blessedness which will be given as a prize to the genuine servants of God and christ: the crown (wreath) which is the reward of the righteousness
  **c.** that which is an ornament and honour to one
s: From an apparently primary “stepho” (to *twine* or *wreathe*); a *chaplet* (as a badge of royalty, a prize in the public games or a symbol of honor generally; but more conspicuous and elaborate than the simple *fillet*, [G1238](G1238)), literally or figuratively: - crown.
o: from an apparently primary stepho (to twine or wreathe)

d:
Stephen = crowned
**1.** one of the seven deacons in Jerusalem and the first Christian martyr
s: The same as [G4735](G4735); *Stephanus*, a Christian: - Stephen.

d:
**1.** to encircle with a crown, to crown: the victor in a contest
**2.** to adorn, to honour
s: From [G4735](G4735); to *adorn* *with* an honorary *wreath* (literally or figuratively): - crown.

d: **1.** the breast
s: From [G2476](G2476) (as *standing* prominently); the (entire external) *bosom*, that is, *chest:* - breast.

d:
**1.** to stand firm
**2.** to persevere, to persist
**3.** to keep one’s standing
s: From the perfect tense of [G2476](G2476); to *be* *stationary*, that is, (figuratively) to *persevere:* - stand (fast).

d: **1.** firm condition, steadfastness: of mind
s: From [G4741](G4741); *stability* (figuratively): - stedfastness

d:
**1.** to make stable, place firmly, set fast, fix
**2.** to strengthen, make firm
**3.** to render constant, confirm, one’s mind
s: From a presumed derivative of [G2476](G2476) (like [G4731](G4731)); to *set* *fast*, that is, (literally) to *turn* *resolutely* in a certain direction, or (figuratively) to *confirm:* - fix, (e-) stablish, stedfastly set, strengthen.

d: **1.** a mark pricked in or branded upon the body. To ancient oriental usage, slaves and soldiers bore the name or the stamp of their master or commander branded or pricked (cut) into their bodies to indicate what master or general they belonged to, and there were even some devotee’s who stamped themselves in this way with the token of their Gods
s: From a primary word στίζω stizō (to “stick”, that is, *prick*); a *mark* incised or punched (for recognition of ownership), that is, (figuratively) *scar* of service: - mark.
o: from a primary stizo (to stick, i.e. prick)

d: **1.** an instant (i.e. a moment) of time
s: Feminine of [G4742](G4742); a *point* of *time*, that is, an *instant:* - moment.

d:
**1.** to shine, glisten
  **a.** of garments
s: Apparently a primary verb; to *gleam*, that is, *flash* intensely: - shining.

d:
**1.** a portico, a covered colonnade where people can stand or walk protected from the weather and the heat of the sun
**2.** the portico built by Solomon in the eastern part of the temple (which in the temple’s destruction by the Babylonians was left uninjured, and remained down to the time of king Agrippa, to whom the care of the temple was entrusted by the emperor Claudius, and who on account of its antiquity dare not demolish it and build anew.
s: Probably from [G2476](G2476); a *colonnade* or interior *piazza:* - porch.

d: **1.** branch, leafy limb
s: From a primary word στείβω steibō (to “step” or “stamp”); a *spread* (as if *tramped* flat) of loose materials for a couch, that is, (by implication) a *bough* of a tree so employed: - branch.
o: from a primary steibo (to step or stamp)

d:
**1.** any first thing, from which the others belonging to some series or composite whole take their rise, an element, first principal
  **a.** the letters of the alphabet as the elements of speech, not however the written characters, but the spoken sounds
  **b.** the elements from which all things have come, the material causes of the universe
  **c.** the heavenly bodies, either as parts of the heavens or (as others think) because in them the elements of man, life and destiny were supposed to reside
  **d.** the elements, rudiments, primary and fundamental principles of any art, science, or discipline
    **1.** i.e. of mathematics, Euclid’s geometry
s: Neuter of a presumed derivative of the base of [G4748](G4748); something *orderly* in arrangement, that is, (by implication) a *serial* (*basal*, *fundamental*, *initial*) constituent (literally), proposition (figuratively): - element, principle, rudiment.
o: from a presumed derivative of the base of [G4748](G4748)

d:
**1.** to proceed in a row as the march of a soldier, go in order
  **a.** metaph. to go on prosperously, to turn out well
**2.** to walk
  **a.** to direct one’s life, to live
s: From a derivative of στείχω steichō̄ (to *range* in regular line); to *march* in (military) rank (*keep* *step*), that is, (figuratively) to *conform* to virtue and piety: - walk (orderly).
o: from a derivative of steicho (to range in regular line)

d:
**1.** an equipment
**2.** an equipment in clothes, clothing
  **a.** spec. a loose outer garment for men extending to the feet, worn by kings, priests, and persons of rank
s: From [G4724](G4724); *equipment*, that is, (specifically) a “stole” or long fitting *gown* (as a mark of dignity): - long clothing (garment), (long) robe.

d:
**1.** the mouth, as part of the body: of man, of animals, of fish, etc.
  **a.** since thoughts of a man’s soul find verbal utterance by his mouth, the heart or soul and the mouth are distinguished
**2.** the edge of a sword
s: Probably stregthened from a presumed derivative of the base of [G5114](G5114); the *mouth* (as if a *gash* in the face); by implication *language* (and its relations); figuratively an *opening* (in the earth); specifically the *front* or *edge* (of a weapon): - edge, face, mouth.
o: probably strengthened from a presumed derivative of the base of [G5114](G5114)

d:
**1.** the throat
**2.** an opening, orifice, esp. of the stomach
**3.** the stomach
s: From [G4750](G4750); an *orifice* (the *gullet*), that is, (specifically) the “stomach”: - stomach.

d:
**1.** an expedition, campaign, military service, warfare
**2.** metaph. Paul likens his contest with the difficulties that oppose him in the discharge of his apostolic duties, as warfare
s: From [G4754](G4754); military *service*, that is, (figuratively) the apostolic *career* (as one of hardship and danger): - warfare.

d:
**1.** an army
**2.** a band of soldiers
**3.** bodyguard, guards men
s: From [G4754](G4754); an *armament*, that is, (by implication) a body of *troops* (more or less extensive or systematic): - army, soldier, man of war.

d:
**1.** to make a military expedition, to lead soldiers to war or to battle, (spoken of a commander)
**2.** to do military duty, be on active service, be a soldier
**3.** to fight
s: Middle voice from the base of [G4756](G4756); to *serve* in a military campaign; figuratively to *execute* *the* *apostolate* (with its arduous duties and functions), to *contend* with carnal inclinations: - soldier, (go to) war (-fare).
o: middle voice from the base of [G4756](G4756)

d:
**1.** the commander of an army
**2.** in the NT a civic commander, a governor
  **a.** the name the highest magistrate in the municipia or colonies; they had the power of administering justice in the less important cases
  **b.** of civil magistrates
**3.** captain of the temple, i.e. the commander of the Levites who kept guard in and around the temple
s: From the base of [G4756](G4756) and [G71](G71) or [G2233](G2233); a *general*, that is, (by implication or analogy) a (military) *governor* (*praetor*), the *chief* (*praefect*) of the (Levitical) temple wardens: - captain, magistrate.
o: from the base of [G4756](G4756) and [G71](G71) or [G2233](G2233)

d:
**1.** an army, band of soldiers
**2.** in the NT, the hosts of heaven
  **a.** troops of angels
  **b.** the heavenly bodies, stars of heaven (so called on account of their number and their order)
s: Feminine of a derivative of στρατός stratos (an *army*; from the base of [G4766](G4766), as *encamped*); *camp* *likeness*, that is, an *army*, that is, (figuratively) the *angels*, the celestial *luminaries:* - host.
o: from a derivative of stratos (an army from the base of [G4766](G4766), as encamped)

d:
**1.** a (common) soldier
**2.** metaph. a champion of the cause of christ
s: From a presumed derivative of the same as [G4756](G4756); a *camperout*, that is, a (common) *warrior* (literally or figuratively): - soldier.
o: from a presumed derivative of the same as [G4756](G4756)

d:
**1.** to gather (collect) an army, to enlist soldiers
  **a.** of the commander
s: From a compound of the base of [G4756](G4756) and [G3004](G3004) (in its original sense); to *gather* (or *select*) as a *warrior*, that is, *enlist* in the army: - choose to be a soldier.
o: from a compound of the base of [G4756](G4756) and [G3004](G3004) (in its original sense)

d:
**1.** the commander of a camp and army, a military tribune
**2.** Praetorian prefect, commander of the praetorian cohorts, captain of the Roman emperor’s body guard
s: From [G4760](G4760) and [G757](G757); a *ruler* *of* *an* *army*, that is, (specifically) a Praetorian *praefect:* - captain of the guard.

d:
**1.** a military camp
**2.** soldiers in camp, an army
s: From the base of [G4756](G4756) and the same as [G3977](G3977); a *camping* *ground*, that is, (by implication) a body of *troops:* - army.
o: from the base of [G4756](G4756) and the same as [G3977](G3977)

d:
**1.** to twist, turn awry
**2.** to torture, put to the rack
**3.** metaph. to pervert, of one who wrests or tortures language in a false sense
s: From a derivative of [G4762](G4762); to *wrench*, that is, (specifically) to *torture* (by the rack), but only figuratively to *pervert:* - wrest.

d:
**1.** to turn, turn around
**2.** to turn one’s self (i.e. to turn the back to one
  **a.** of one who no longer cares for another)
  **b.** metaph. to turn one’s self from one’s course of conduct, i.e. to change one’s mind
s: Strengthened from the base of [G5157](G5157); to *twist*, that is, *turn* quite around or *reverse* (literally or figuratively): - convert, turn (again, back again, self, self about).

d: **1.** to be wanton, to live luxuriously
s: From a presumed derivative of [G4764](G4764); to *be* *luxurious:* - live deliciously.

d:
**1.** excessive strength which longs to break forth, over strength
**2.** luxury
**3.** eager desire
s: Akin to [G4731](G4731); a “straining”, “strenuousness” or “strength”, that is, (figuratively) *luxury* (*voluptuousness*): - delicacy.

d: **1.** a little bird, esp. of the sparrow sort, a sparrow
s: Diminutive of στρουθός strouthos (a *sparrow*); a *little* *sparrow:* - sparrow.

d:
**1.** to spread
**2.** furnish
**3.** to spread with couches or divans
s: Or a simpler form στρωννύω strōnnuō *strone’-noo’-o*, prolonged from a still simpler form στρόω stroō *stro’-o* (used only as an alternate in certain tenses; probably akin to [G4731](G4731) through the idea of *positing*); to “strew”, that is, *spread* (as a carpet or couch): - make bed, furnish, spread, strew.
o: prolongation from a still simpler stroo stro’-o (used only as an alternate in certain tenses, probably akin to [G4731](G4731) through the idea of positing)

d: **1.** hated, detestable
s: From a derivative of an obsolete, apparently primary, word στύγω stugō (to *hate*); *hated*, that is, *odious:* - hateful.
o: from a derivative of an obsolete apparently primary stugo (to hate)

d:
**1.** to be sad, sorrowful
**2.** metaph. of the sky covered with clouds
s: From the same as [G4767](G4767); to *render* *gloomy*, that is, (by implication) *glower* (*be* *overcast* with clouds, or *sombreness* of speech): - lower, be sad.

d:
**1.** a pillar
**2.** a column
  **a.** pillars of fire i.e. flames rising like pillars
**3.** a prop or support
s: From στύω stuō (to *stiffen*; properly akin to the base of [G2476](G2476)); a *post* (“style”), that is, (figuratively) *support:* - pillar.
o: from stuo (to stiffen, properly akin to the base of [G2476](G2476))

d:
Stoics = of the portico
**1.** pertaining to the Stoic philosophy, the author of which, Zeno of Citium, taught at Athens
s: From [G4745](G4745); a “stoic” (as occupying a particular porch in Athens), that is, adherent of a certain philosophy: - Stoick.

The personal pronoun of the second person singular; *thou*: - thou. See also [G4571](G4571), [G4671](G4671), [G4675](G4675); and for the plur. [G5209](G5209), [G5210](G5210), [G5213](G5213), [G5216](G5216).
o: the person pronoun of the second person singular

d:
**1.** a kinship, relationship
**2.** kindred, relations collectively, family
s: From [G4773](G4773); *relationship*, that is, (concretely) *relatives:* - kindred.

d:
**1.** of the same kin, akin to, related by blood
**2.** in a wider sense, of the same nation, a fellow countryman
s: From [G4862](G4862) and [G1085](G1085); a *relative* (by blood); by extension a fellow *countryman:* - cousin, kin (-sfolk, -sman).

d: **1.** pardon, indulgence
s: From a compound of [G4862](G4862) and [G1097](G1097); *fellow* *knowledge*, that is, *concession:* - permission.

d: **1.** to sit together, to sit with one another
s: From [G4862](G4862) and [G2521](G2521); to *seat* *oneself* in company *with:* - sit with.

d:
**1.** to cause to sit down together, place together
**2.** to sit down together
s: From [G4862](G4862) and [G2523](G2523); to *give* (or *take*) *a* *seat* in company *with:* - (make) sit (down) together.

d: **1.** to suffer hardship together with one
s: From [G4862](G4862) and [G2553](G2553); to *suffer* *hardship* in company *with:* - be partaker of afflictions.

d:
**1.** to treat ill with another
**2.** to be ill treated in company with, share persecutions or come into a fellowship of ills
s: From [G4862](G4862) and [G2558](G2558); to *maltreat* in company *with*, that is, (passively) *endure* *persecution* *together:* - suffer affliction with.

d:
**1.** to call together, assemble
**2.** to call together to one’s self
s: From [G4862](G4862) and [G2564](G2564); to *convoke:* - call together.

d: **1.** to cover on all sides, to conceal entirely, to cover up completely
s: From [G4862](G4862) and [G2572](G2572); to *conceal* *altogether:* - cover.

d:
**1.** to bend together, to bend completely
**2.** metaph. to subject one to error and hardness of heart, a figure taken from bowing the back by captives compelled to pass under the yoke
s: From [G4862](G4862) and [G2578](G2578); to *bend* *together*, that is, (figuratively) to *afflict:* - bow down.

d:
**1.** to go down with
  **a.** of those who descend from a high place to a lower place as from Jerusalem to Caesarea
s: From [G4862](G4862) and [G2597](G2597); to *descend* in company *with:* - go down with.

d:
**1.** a putting together or joint deposit (of votes)
  **a.** hence approval, assent, agreement
s: From [G4784](G4784); a *deposition* (of sentiment) in company *with*, that is, (figuratively) *accord* with: - agreement.

d:
**1.** to deposit together with another
**2.** to deposit one’s vote in the urn with another
**3.** to consent to, vote for, agree with
s: Middle voice from [G4862](G4862) and [G2698](G2698); to *deposit* (one’s vote or opinion) in company *with*, that is, (figuratively) to *accord* with: - consent.

d:
**1.** be depositing a ballot in the urn (i.e. by voting for) to assign one a place among, to vote one a place among
**2.** to vote against with others, i.e. to condemn with others
s: From [G4862](G4862) and a compound of [G2596](G2596) and [G5585](G5585); to *count* *down* in company *with*, that is, *enroll* *among:* - number with.
o: from [G4862](G4862) and a compound of [G2596](G2596) and [G5585](G5585)

d:
**1.** to mix together, commingle
**2.** to unite
  **a.** caused the several parts to combine into an organic structure, which is the body
  **b.** to unite one thing to another
s: From [G4862](G4862) and [G2767](G2767); to *commingle*, that is, (figuratively) to *combine* or *assimilate:* - mix with, temper together.

d:
**1.** to move together with others
**2.** to throw into commotion, excite, stir up
s: From [G4682](G4682) and [G2795](G2795); to *move* *together*, that is, (specifically) to *excite* as a mass (to sedition): - stir up.

d:
**1.** to shut up together, enclose
  **a.** of a shoal of fishes in a net
**2.** to shut up on all sides, shut up completely
s: From [G4862](G4862) and [G2808](G2808); to *shut* *together*, that is, *include* or (figuratively) *embrace* in a common subjection to: - conclude, inclose, shut up.

d:
**1.** a fellow heir, a joint heir
**2.** one who obtains something assigned to himself with others, a joint participant
s: From [G4862](G4862) and [G2818](G2818); a *co-heir*, that is, (by analogy) *participant* *in* *common:* - fellow (joint) -heir, heir together, heir with.

d: **1.** to become a partaker together with others, or to have fellowship with a thing
s: From [G4862](G4862) and [G2841](G2841); to *share* in company *with*, that is, *co-participate* in: - communicate (have fellowship) with, be partaker of.

d: **1.** participant with others in anything, joint partner
s: From [G4862](G4862) and [G2844](G2844); a *co-participant:* - companion, partake (-r, -r with).

d:
**1.** to carry or bring together, to collect
  **a.** to house crops, gather into granaries
**2.** to carry with others, help in carrying out, the dead to be buried or burned
  **a.** to bury
s: From [G4862](G4862) and [G2865](G2865); to *convey* *together*, that is, *collect* or *bear* away in company *with* others: - carry.

d:
**1.** to joint together fitly, compound, combine
**2.** to interpret
**3.** to compare
s: From [G4862](G4862) and [G2919](G2919); to *judge* of one thing in connection *with* another, that is, *combine* (spiritual ideas with appropriate expressions) or *collate* (one person with another by way of contrast or resemblance): - compare among (with).

d: **1.** to bend completely forwards, to be bowed together
s: From [G4862](G4862) and [G2955](G2955); to *stoop* *altogether*, that is, *be* *completely* *overcome* by: - bow together.

d: **1.** accident, by chance
s: From a compound of [G4862](G4862) and κυρέω kureō (to *light* or *happen*; from the base of [G2962](G2962)); *concurrence*, that is, *accident:* - chance.
o: from a comparative of [G4862](G4862) and kureo (to light or happen

d:
**1.** to rejoice with, take part in another’s joy
**2.** to rejoice together, to congratulate
s: From [G4862](G4862) and [G5463](G5463); to *sympathize* *in* *gladness*, *congratulate:* - rejoice in (with).

d:
**1.** to pour together, commingle
**2.** to disturb the mind of one, to stir up to tumult or outbreak
**3.** to confound or bewilder
s:
Or συγχύνω sugchunō *soong-khoo’-no*
From [G4862](G4862) and χέω “cheō” (to *pour*) or its alternate; to *commingle* promiscuously, that is, (figuratively) to *throw* (an assembly) *into* *disorder*, to *perplex* (the mind): - confound, confuse, stir up, be in an uproar.
o: from [G4862](G4862) and cheo (to pour) or its alternate

d:
**1.** to use with anyone, use jointly
**2.** to associate with, to have dealings with
s: From [G4862](G4862) and [G5530](G5530); to *use* *jointly*, that is, (by implication) to *hold* *intercourse* *in* *common:* - have dealings with.

d:
**1.** confusion, disturbance
  **a.** of riotous persons
s: From [G4797](G4797); *commixture*, that is, (figuratively) riotous *disturbance:* - confusion.

d:
**1.** to live together with one
  **a.** of physical life on earth
  **b.** to live a new life in union with christ, i.e. dedicated to God
s: From [G4862](G4862) and [G2198](G2198); to continue to *live* in common *with*, that is, *co-survive* (literally or figuratively): - live with.

d:
**1.** to fasten to one yoke, yoke together
**2.** to join together unite
  **a.** of the marriage tie
s: From [G4862](G4862) and the base of [G2201](G2201); to *yoke* *together*, that is, (figuratively) *conjoin* (in marriage): - join together.

d:
**1.** to seek or examine together
**2.** in the NT to discuss, dispute, question
s: From [G4862](G4862) and [G2212](G2212); to investigate *jointly*, that is, *discuss*, *controvert*, *cavil:* - dispute (with), enquire, question (with), reason (together).

d: **1.** mutual questioning, disputation, discussion
s: From [G4802](G4802); *mutual* *questioning*, that is, *discussion:* - disputation (-ting), reasoning.

d: **1.** a disputer, i.e. a learned disputant, sophist
s: From [G4802](G4802); a *disputant*, that is, *sophist:* - disputer.

d:
**1.** yoked together
  **a.** of those united by the bond of marriage, relationship, office, labour, study, business, or the like
  **b.** of a yoke fellow, consort, comrade, colleague, partner
s: From [G4801](G4801); *co-yoked*, that is, (figuratively) as noun, a *colleague*; probably rather as proper name; *Syzygus*, a Christian: - yokefellow.

d:
**1.** to make one alive together
  **a.** of Christians, with christ
s: From [G4862](G4862) and [G2227](G2227); to *reanimate* *conjointly* with (figuratively): - quicken together with.

d: **1.** sycamine tree, having the form and foliage of the mulberry, but fruit resembling the fig
s: Of Hebrew origin \[[H8256](H8256)\] in imitation of [G4809](G4809); a *sycamore* or fig tree: - sycamine tree.
o: of hebrew origin [H8256](H8256) in imitation of [G4809](G4809)

d: **1.** a fig tree
s: From [G4810](G4810); a *fig* *tree:* - fig tree.

d: **1.** a sycomore tree
s: From [G4810](G4810) and μόρον moron (the *mulberry*); the “sycamore” or fig tree: - sycamore tree. Compare [G4807](G4807).

d: **1.** a fig, the ripe fruit of a fig tree
s: Apparently a primary word; a *fig:* - fig.

d:
**1.** to accuse wrongfully, to calumniate, to attack by malicious devices
**2.** to exact money wrongfully
  **a.** to extort from, defraud
s: From a compound of [G4810](G4810) and a derivative of [G5316](G5316); to *be* *a* *fig* *informer* (reporter of the law forbidding the exportation of figs from Greece), “sycopant”, that is, (generally and by extension) to *defraud* (*exact* unlawfully, *extort*): - accuse falsely, take by false accusation.
o: from a compound of [G4810](G4810) and a derivative of [G5316](G5316)

d:
**1.** to carry off booty
  **a.** to carry one off as a captive (and slave)
  **b.** to lead away from the truth and subject to one’s sway
s: From the base of [G4813](G4813) and (the reduplicated form of) [G71](G71); to *lead* away as *booty*, that is, (figuratively) *seduce:* - spoil.
o: from the base of [G4813](G4813) and (the reduplicated form of) [G71](G71)

d: **1.** to rob, despoil
s: From a derivative of σύλλω sullō̄ (to *strip*; probably akin to [G138](G138); compare [G4661](G4661)); to *despoil:* - rob.
o: from a derivative of sullo (to strip, probably akin to [G138](G138), cf [G4661](G4661))

d: **1.** to talk with
s: From [G4862](G4862) and [G2980](G2980); to *talk* *together*, that is, *converse:* - commune (confer, talk) with, speak among.

d:
**1.** to seize, take: one as prisoner
**2.** to conceive, of a woman
  **a.** metaph. of lust whose impulses a man indulges
**3.** to seize for one’s self
  **a.** in a hostile sense, to make (one a permanent) prisoner
**4.** to take hold together with one, to assist, help, to succour
s: From [G4862](G4862) and [G2983](G2983); to *clasp*, that is, *seize* (*arrest*, *capture*); specifically to *conceive* (literally or figuratively); by implication to *aid:* - catch, conceive, help, take.

d:
**1.** to gather up
**2.** to collect in order to carry off
s: From [G4862](G4862) and [G3004](G3004) in its original sense; to *collect:* - gather (together, up).
o: from [G4862](G4862) and [G3004](G3004) in its original sense

d:
**1.** to bring together accounts, reckon up, compute
**2.** to reckon with one’s self, to reason
s: From [G4862](G4862) and [G3049](G3049); to *reckon* *together* (with oneself), that is, *deliberate:* - reason with.

d:
**1.** to affect with grief together
**2.** give with one’s self
s: From [G4862](G4862) and [G3076](G3076); to *afflict* *jointly*, that is, (passively) *sorrow* *at* (on account of) some one: - be grieved.

d:
**1.** to walk with the feet near together
**2.** to come together, meet with one
**3.** of things which fall out at the same time, to happen, turn out, come to pass
s: From [G4862](G4862) and the base of [G939](G939); to *walk* (figuratively *transpire*) *together*, that is, *concur* (*take* *place*): - be (-fall), happen (unto).

d:
**1.** to throw together, to bring together
  **a.** to converse
  **b.** to bring together in one’s mind, confer with one’s self
  **c.** to come together, meet
    **1.** to encounter in a hostile sense
    **2.** to fight with one
    **3.** to bring together of one’s property, to contribute, aid, help
s: From [G4862](G4862) and [G906](G906); to *combine*, that is, (in speaking) to *converse*, *consult*, *dispute*, (mentally) to *consider*, (by implication) to *aid*, (personally) to *join*, *attack:* - confer, encounter, help, make, meet with, ponder.

d:
**1.** to reign together
**2.** metaph. to possess supreme honour, liberty, blessedness, with one in the kingdom of God
s: From [G4862](G4862) and [G936](G936); to *be* *co-regent* (figuratively): - reign with.

d:
**1.** to cause to coalesce, to join together, put together
  **a.** to unite or knit together: in affection
**2.** to put together in one’s mind
  **a.** to compare
  **b.** to gather, conclude, consider
**3.** to cause a person to unite with one in a conclusion or come to the same opinion, to prove, demonstrate
  **a.** to teach, instruct, one
s: From [G4862](G4862) and βιβάζω bibazō (to *force*; causatively \[by reduplication\] of the base of [G939](G939)); to *drive* *together*, that is, *unite* (in association or affection), (mentally) to *infer*, *show*, *teach:* - compact, assuredly, gather, instruct, knit together, prove.
o: from [G4862](G4862) and bibazo (to force, causative \[by reduplication\] of the base of [G939](G939))

d:
**1.** to give counsel
**2.** to take counsel with others, take counsel together, to consult, deliberate
s: From [G4862](G4862) and [G1011](G1011); to *give* (or *take*) *advice* *jointly*, that is, *recommend*, *deliberate* or *determine:* - consult, (give, take) counsel (together).

d:
**1.** counsel, which is given, taken, entered upon
  **a.** consult, deliberate
**2.** a council
  **a.** an assembly of counsellors or persons in consultation (the governors and procurators of provinces had a board of assessors or advisers with whom they took council before rendering judgment)
s: Neuter of a presumed derivative of [G4825](G4825); *advisement*; specifically a *deliberative* body, that is, the provincial *assessors* or lay court: - consultation, counsel, council.

d: **1.** an adviser, counsellor
s: From [G4862](G4862) and [G1012](G1012); a *consultor*, that is, *adviser:* - counsellor.

d:
Simon = harkening
**1.** the second son of Jacob by Leah
**2.** one of Abraham’s descendants
**3.** the one who took the infant Jesus in his arms in the temple
**4.** a teacher at the church of Antioch
**5.** the original name of Peter the apostle
s: From the same as [G4613](G4613); *Symeon* (that is, *Shimon*), the name of five Israelites: - Simeon, Simon.

d: **1.** a fellow disciple
s: From a compound of [G4862](G4862) and [G3129](G3129); a *co-learner* (of Christianity): - fellowdisciple.

d: **1.** to bear witness with, bear joint witness
s: From [G4862](G4862) and [G3140](G3140); to *testify* *jointly*, that is, *corroborate* by (concurrent) evidence: - testify unto, (also) bear witness (with).

d:
**1.** to divide at the same time, divide together
**2.** to assign a portion
**3.** to divide together with one (so that a part comes to me, a part to him)
s: Middle voice from [G4862](G4862) and [G3307](G3307); to *share* *jointly*, that is, *participate* in: - be partaker with.

d:
**1.** partaking together with one, a joint partaker
  **a.** of something
s: From [G4862](G4862) and [G3353](G3353); a *co-participant:* - partaker.

d: **1.** an imitator of others
s: From a presumed compound of [G4862](G4862) and [G3401](G3401); a *co-imitator*, that is, *fellow* *votary:* - follower together.
o: from a presumed compound of [G4862](G4862) and [G3401](G3401)

d: **1.** having the same form as another, similar, conformed to
s: From [G4862](G4862) and [G3444](G3444); *jointly* *formed*, that is, (figuratively) *similar:* - conformed to, fashioned like unto.

d: **1.** to be conformed to, receive the same form as
s: From [G4832](G4832); to *render* *like*, that is, (figuratively) to *assimilate:* - make conformable unto.

d:
**1.** to be affected with the same feeling as another, to sympathise with
**2.** to feel for, have compassion on
s: From [G4835](G4835); to *feel* “sympathy” with, that is, (by implication) to *commiserate:* - have compassion, be touched with a feeling of.

d: **1.** suffering or feeling the like with another, sympathetic
s: From [G4841](G4841); *having* *a* *fellow* *feeling* (“sympathetic”), that is, (by implication) *mutually* *commiserative:* - having compassion one of another.

d:
**1.** to come together
**2.** to come to one’s help
s: From [G4862](G4862) and [G3854](G3854); to *be* *present* *together*, that is, to *convene*; by implication to *appear* *in* *aid:* - come together, stand with.

d:
**1.** to call upon or invite or exhort at the same time or together
**2.** to strengthen (comfort) with others
s: From [G4862](G4862) and [G3870](G3870); to *console* *jointly:* - comfort together.

d:
**1.** to take along together with
**2.** in the NT to take with one as a companion
s: From [G4862](G4862) and [G3880](G3880); to *take* *along* *in* *company:* - take with.

d:
**1.** to abide together with
**2.** to continue to live together
s: From [G4862](G4862) and [G3887](G3887); to *remain* *in* *company*, that is, *still* *live:* - continue with.

d: **1.** to be present together
s: From [G4862](G4862) and [G3918](G3918); to *be* *at* *hand* *together*, that is, *now* *present:* - be here present with.

d:
**1.** to suffer or feel pain together
**2.** to suffer evils (troubles, persecutions) in the like manner with another
s: From [G4862](G4862) and [G3958](G3958) (including its alternate); to *experience* *pain* *jointly* or of the *same* *kind* (specifically *persecution*; to “sympathize”): - suffer with.

d: **1.** to send together with
s: From [G4862](G4862) and [G3992](G3992); to *despatch* *in* *company:* - send with.

d:
**1.** to comprehend at once
**2.** to embrace completely
s: From [G4862](G4862) and a compound of [G4012](G4012) and [G2983](G2983); to *take* *by* *inclosing* *altogether*, that is, *earnestly* *throw* *the* *arms* *about* *one:* - embrace.
o: from [G4862](G4862) and a compound of [G4012](G4012) and [G2983](G2983)

d: **1.** to drink with
s: From [G4862](G4862) and [G4095](G4095); to *partake* *a* *beverage* *in* *company:* - drink with.

d:
**1.** to fill completely
  **a.** of the hold of a ship
**2.** to complete entirely, be fulfilled: of time
s: From [G4862](G4862) and [G4137](G4137); to *implenish* *completely*, that is, (of space) to *swamp* (a boat), or (of time) to *accomplish* (passively be *complete*): - (fully) come, fill up.

d:
**1.** to choke utterly
  **a.** metaph. the seed of the divine word sown in the mind
  **b.** to press round or throng one so as almost to suffocate him
s: From [G4862](G4862) and [G4155](G4155); to *strangle* *completely*, that is, (literally) to *drown*, or (figuratively) to *crowd:* - choke, throng.

d:
**1.** possessing the same citizenship with others, a fellow citizen
  **a.** of Gentiles as received into communion of the saints
  **b.** of the people consecrated to God
s: From [G4862](G4862) and [G4177](G4177); a *native* *of* *the* *same* *town*, that is, (figuratively) *co-religionist* (*fellow* *Christian*): - fellow-citizen.

d:
**1.** to go or journey together
**2.** to come together, to assemble
s: From [G4862](G4862) and [G4198](G4198); to *journey* *together*; by implication to *assemble:* - go with, resort.

d:
**1.** a drinking party, entertainment
  **a.** of the party itself, the guests
  **b.** rows of guests
s: Neuter of a derivative of the alternate of [G4844](G4844); a *drinking* party (“symposium”), that is, (by extension) a *room* of guests: - company.
o: from a derivative of the alternate of [G4844](G4844)

d: **1.** a fellow elder
s: From [G4862](G4862) and [G4245](G4245); a *co-presbyter:* - presbyter, also an elder.

d:
**1.** to bear or bring together
**2.** to bear together or at the same time
  **a.** to carry with others
  **b.** to collect or contribute in order to help
  **c.** to help, be profitable, be expedient
s: From [G4862](G4862) and [G5342](G5342) (including its alternate); to *bear* *together* (*contribute*), that is, (literally) to *collect*, or (figuratively) to *conduce*; especially (neuter participle as noun) *advantage:* - be better for, bring together, be expedient (for), be good, (be) profit (-able for).

d: **1.** to consent, confess
s: From [G4862](G4862) and [G5346](G5346); to *say* *jointly*, that is, *assent* *to:* - consent unto.

d: **1.** one who is of the same people, a fellow countryman
s: From [G4862](G4862) and a derivative of [G5443](G5443); a *co-tribesman*, that is, *native* *of* *the* *same* *country:* - countryman.

d:
**1.** born together with, of joint origin
  **a.** connate, congenital, innate, implanted by birth or nature
**2.** grown together, united with
**3.** kindred
s: From [G4862](G4862) and a derivative of [G5453](G5453); *grown* along *with* (*connate*), that is, (figuratively) closely *united* to: - planted together.

d:
**1.** to cause to grow together
**2.** to grow together, grow with
s: From [G4862](G4862) and [G5453](G5453); passively to *grow* *jointly:* - spring up with.

d:
**1.** to agree together
**2.** to agree with one in making a bargain, to make an agreement, to bargain
s: From [G4859](G4859); to be *harmonious*, that is, (figuratively) to *accord* (*be* *suitable*, *concur*) or *stipulate* (by compact): - agree (together, with).

d: **1.** concord, agreement
s: From [G4856](G4856); *accordance:* - concord.

d: **1.** music
s: From [G4859](G4859); *unison* of sound (“symphony”), that is, a *concert* of instruments (harmonious *note*): - music.

d:
**1.** harmonious, accordant, agreeing
**2.** thing agreed upon, compact
s: From [G4862](G4862) and [G5456](G5456); *sounding* *together* (*alike*), that is, (figuratively) *accordant* (neuter as noun, *agreement*): - consent.

d:
**1.** to compute, count up
**2.** to vote with one
s: From [G4862](G4862) and [G5585](G5585); to *compute* *jointly:* - reckon.

d: **1.** of one mind, of one accord This word is made up of two words sun (together with) and psuchos(soul, self, inner life, or the seat of the feelings, desires,affections). So the word refers to being united in spirit orharmonious (A&G). Paul desired the Philippians to be united intheir affections - one in christ in all desires! Used only herein the NT. - Wayne Steury
s: From [G4862](G4862) and [G5590](G5590); *co-spirited*, that is, *similar* *in* *sentiment:* - like-minded.

d: **1.** with
s: A primary preposition denoting *union*; *with* or *together* (but much closer than [G3326](G3326) or [G3844](G3844)), that is, by association, companionship, process, resemblance, possession, instrumentality, addition, etc.*:* - beside, with. In compounds it has similar applications, including *completeness*.

d:
**1.** to gather together, to gather
  **a.** to draw together, collect
    **1.** of fishes
    **2.** of a net in which they are caught
**2.** to bring together, assemble, collect
  **a.** to join together, join in one (those previously separated)
  **b.** to gather together by convoking
  **c.** to be gathered i.e. come together, gather, meet
**3.** to lead with one’s self
  **a.** into one’s home, i.e. to receive hospitably, to entertain
s: From [G4862](G4862) and [G71](G71); to *lead* *together*, that is, *collect* or *convene*; specifically to *entertain* (hospitably): - + accompany, assemble (selves, together), bestow, come together, gather (selves together, up, together), lead into, resort, take in.

d:
**1.** a bringing together, gathering (as of fruits), a contracting
**2.** in the NT, an assembling together of men, an assembly of men
**3.** a synagogue
  **a.** an assembly of Jews formally gathered together to offer prayers and listen to the reading and expositions of the scriptures; assemblies of that sort were held every sabbath and feast day, afterwards also on the second and fifth days of every week; name transferred to an assembly of Christians formally gathered together for religious purposes
  **b.** the buildings where those solemn Jewish assemblies are held. Synagogues seem to date their origin from the Babylonian exile. In the times of Jesus and the apostles every town, not only in Palestine, but also among the Gentiles if it contained a considerable number of Jewish inhabitants, had at least one synagogue, the larger towns several or even many. These were also used for trials and inflicting punishment.
s: From (the reduplicated form of) [G4863](G4863); an *assemblage* of persons; specifically a Jewish “synagogue” (the meeting or the place); by analogy a Christian *church:* - assembly, congregation, synagogue.

d: **1.** to strive together with one, to help one in striving
s: From [G4862](G4862) and [G75](G75); to *struggle* in company *with*, that is, (figuratively) to *be* *a* *partner* (*assistant*): - strive together with.

d: **1.** to strive at the same time with another
s: From [G4862](G4862) and [G118](G118); to *wrestle* in company *with*, that is, (figuratively) to *seek* *jointly:* - labour with, strive together for.

d:
**1.** to gather together with others
**2.** to assemble
**3.** to be gathered together i.e. to come together
s: From [G4862](G4862) and ἀθροίζω athroizō (to *hoard*); to *convene:* - call (gather) together.

d:
**1.** to take up together with another or others
**2.** to bring together with others
  **a.** to cast up or settle accounts
  **b.** to make a reckoning with
s: From [G4862](G4862) and [G142](G142); to *make* *up* *together*, that is, (figuratively) to *compute* (an account): - reckon, take.

d: **1.** a fellow prisoner
s: From [G4862](G4862) and [G164](G164); a *co-captive:* - fellowprisoner.

d: **1.** to follow together with others, to accompany
s: From [G4862](G4862) and [G190](G190); to *accompany:* - follow.

d:
**1.** to gather together, assemble
**2.** to be assembled, meet with
s: From [G4862](G4862) and ἁλίζω halizō (to *throng*); to *accumulate*, that is, *convene:* - assemble together.

d:
**1.** to ascend at the same time, come up together with to a higher place
  **a.** with one
s: From [G4862](G4862) and [G305](G305); to *ascend* in company *with:* - come up with.

d:
**1.** to recline together, feast together
  **a.** of guests
s: From [G4862](G4862) and [G345](G345); to *recline* in company *with* (at a meal): - sit (down, at the table, together) with (at meat).

d:
**1.** to mix up together
**2.** to keep company with, be intimate with one
s: From [G4862](G4862) and a compound of [G303](G303) and [G3396](G3396); to *mix* *up* *together*, that is, (figuratively) *associate* *with:* - (have, keep) company (with).
o: from [G4862](G4862) and a compound of [G303](G303) and [G3396](G3396)

d:
**1.** to take rest together with
**2.** to sleep together with, to lie with
  **a.** of a husband and wife
  **b.** metaph. to rest or refresh one’s spirits with one (i.e. to give and get refreshment by mutual intercourse)
s: Middle voice from [G4862](G4862) and [G373](G373); to *recruit* *oneself* in company *with:* - refresh with.

d:
**1.** to meet with
  **a.** of events: to happen or befall
s: From [G4862](G4862) and a derivative of [G473](G473); to *meet* *with*; figuratively to *occur:* - befall, meet.

d: **1.** a meeting with
s: From [G4876](G4876); a *meeting* *with:* - meet.

d:
**1.** to lay hold along with, to strive to obtain with others, help in obtaining
**2.** to take hold with another
s: From [G4862](G4862) and [G482](G482); to *take* hold of *opposite* *together*, that is, *co-operate* (*assist*): - help.

d:
**1.** to lead away with or together
**2.** metaph. to be carried away with
  **a.** of a thing, i.e. by a thing, so as to experience with others the force of that which carries away
  **b.** to yield or submit one’s self to lowly things, conditions, employments: not to evade their power
s: From [G4862](G4862) and [G520](G520); to *take* *off* *together*, that is, *transport* *with* (*seduce*, passively *yield*): - carry (lead) away with, condescend.

d:
**1.** to die together
**2.** to die with one
s: From [G4862](G4862) and [G599](G599); to *decease* (literally) in company *with*, or (figuratively) similarly *to:* - be dead (die) with.

d:
**1.** to destroy together
**2.** to perish together (to be slain along with)
s: From [G4862](G4862) and [G622](G622); to *destroy* (middle voice or passive voice, *be* *slain*) in company *with:* - perish with.

d: **1.** to send with
s: From [G4862](G4862) and [G649](G649); to *despatch* (on an errand) in company *with:* - send you.

d:
**1.** to join closely together
**2.** to frame together
  **a.** parts of a building
  **b.** the members of the body
s: From [G4862](G4862) and a derivative of a compound of [G719](G719) and [G3004](G3004) (in its original sense of *laying*); to *render* *close* *jointed* *together*, that is, *organize* *compactly:* - be fitly framed (joined) together.
o: from [G4862](G4862) and a derivative of a compound of [G719](G719) and [G3004](G3004) (in its original sense of laying)

d:
**1.** to seize by force
**2.** to catch or lay hold of (one so that he is no longer his own master)
**3.** to seize by force and carry away
s: From [G4862](G4862) and [G726](G726); to *snatch* *together*, that is, *seize:* - catch.

d:
**1.** to cause to grow together
**2.** to grow together
s: From [G4862](G4862) and [G837](G837); to *increase* (*grow* *up*) *together:* - grow together.

d:
**1.** that which binds together, a band, bond
  **a.** of ligaments by which the members of the human body are united together
**2.** that which is bound together, a bundle
s: From [G4862](G4862) and [G1199](G1199); a *joint* *tie*, that is, *ligament*, (figuratively) *uniting* *principle*, *control:* - band, bond.

d:
**1.** to tie together, to bind together
**2.** to bind or fasten on all sides
**3.** to bind just as (i.e. jointly with) another
s: From [G4862](G4862) and [G1210](G1210); to *bind* *with*, that is, (passively) *be* *a* *fellow* *prisoner* (figuratively): - be bound with.

d:
**1.** to approve together, to join in approving
**2.** to glorify together
s: From [G4862](G4862) and [G1392](G1392); to *exalt* to dignity in company (that is, *similarly*) *with:* - glorify together.

d:
**1.** a fellow servant, one who serves the same master with another
  **a.** the associate of a servant (or slave)
  **b.** one who with others serves (ministers to) a king
  **c.** a colleague of one who is christ’s servant in publishing the gospel
  **d.** one who with others acknowledges the same Lord, Jesus, and obeys his commands
  **e.** one who with others is subject to the same divine authority in the messianic economy
    **1.** of angels as the fellow servants of Christians
s: From [G4862](G4862) and [G1401](G1401); a *co-slave*, that is, *servitor* or *ministrant* *of* *the* *same* *master* (human or divine): - fellowservant.

d: **1.** a running together, concourse, esp. hostile or riotous
s: From (the alternate of) [G4936](G4936); a *running* *together*, that is, (riotous) *concourse:* - run together.

d:
**1.** to raise together, to cause to raise together
**2.** to raise up together from mortal death to a new and blessed life dedicated to God
s: From [G4862](G4862) and [G1453](G1453); to *rouse* (from death) in company *with*, that is, (figuratively) to *revivify* (spiritually) in resemblance to: - raise up together, rise with.

d:
**1.** any assembly (esp. of magistrates, judges, ambassadors), whether convened to deliberate or pass judgment
**2.** any session or assembly or people deliberating or adjudicating
  **a.** the Sanhedrin, the great council at Jerusalem, consisting of the seventy one members, viz. scribes, elders, prominent members of the high priestly families and the high priest, the president of the assembly. The most important causes were brought before this tribunal, inasmuch as the Roman rulers of Judaea had left to it the power of trying such cases, and also of pronouncing sentence of death, with the limitation that a capital sentence pronounced by the Sanhedrin was not valid unless it was confirmed by the Roman procurator.
  **b.** a smaller tribunal or council which every Jewish town had for the decision of less important cases.
s: Neuter of a presumed derivative of a compound of [G4862](G4862) and the base of [G1476](G1476); a *joint* *session*, that is, (specifically) the Jewish *Sanhedrim*; by analogy a subordinate *tribunal:* - council.
o: from a presumed derivative of a compound of [G4862](G4862) and the base of [G1476](G1476)

d:
**1.** the consciousness of anything
**2.** the soul as distinguishing between what is morally good and bad, prompting to do the former and shun the latter, commending one, condemning the other
  **a.** the conscience
s: From a prolonged form of [G4894](G4894); *co-perception*, that is, moral *consciousness:* - conscience.

d:
**1.** to see (have seen) together with others
**2.** to see (have seen) in one’s mind with one’s self
  **a.** to understand, perceive, comprehend,
**3.** to know with another
**4.** to know in one’s mind or with one’s self, to be conscience of
s: From [G4862](G4862) and [G1492](G1492); to *see* *completely*; used (like its primary) only in two past tenses, respectively meaning to *understand* or *become* *aware*, and to *be* *conscious* or (clandestinely) *informed* *of:* - consider, know, be privy, be ware of.

d: **1.** to be with
s: From [G4862](G4862) and [G1510](G1510) (including its various inflections); to *be* in company *with*, that is, *present* at the time: - be with.

d: **1.** to come together
s: From [G4862](G4862) and εῖμι eimi (to *go*); to *assemble:* - gather together.

d: **1.** to enter together
s: From [G4862](G4862) and [G1525](G1525); to *enter* in company *with:* - go in with, go with into.

d: **1.** a fellow traveller, companion in travel
s: From [G4862](G4862) and the base of [G1553](G1553); a *co-absentee* from home, that is, *fellow* *traveller:* - companion in travel, travel with.

d: **1.** elected or chosen (by God to eternal life) together with
s: From a compound of [G4862](G4862) and [G1586](G1586); *chosen* in company *with*, that is, *co-elect* (*fellow* *Christian*): - elected together with.

d:
**1.** to drive together, compel
**2.** to constrain by extortion, urge
s: From [G4862](G4862) and [G1643](G1643); to *drive* *together*, that is, (figuratively) *exhort* (to reconciliation): - + set at one again.

d:
**1.** at attest together with
**2.** to join in bearing witness, to unite in adding testimony
s: From [G4862](G4862) and [G1957](G1957); to *testify* *further* *jointly*, that is, *unite* *in* *adding* *evidence:* - also bear witness.

d: **1.** to follow with, to accompany
s: Middle voice from [G4862](G4862) and a primary word ἕπω hepō (to *follow*); to *attend* (*travel*) in company *with:* - accompany.
o: middle voice from [G4862](G4862) and a primary hepo (to follow)

d:
**1.** to work together, help in work, be partner in labour
**2.** to put forth power together with and thereby to assist
s: From [G4904](G4904); to *be* *a* *fellow* *worker*, that is, *co-operate:* - help (work) with, work (-er) together.

d: **1.** a companion in work, fellow worker
s: From a presumed compound of [G4862](G4862) and the base of [G2041](G2041); a *co-laborer*, that is, *coadjutor:* - companion in labour, (fellow-) helper (-labourer, -worker), labourer together with, workfellow.
o: from a presumed compound of [G4862](G4862) and the base of [G2041](G2041)

d:
**1.** to come together
  **a.** to assemble
  **b.** of conjugal cohabitation
**2.** to go (depart) or come with one, to accompany one
s: From [G4862](G4862) and [G2064](G2064); to *convene*, *depart* in company *with*, *associate* with, or (specifically) *cohabit* (conjugally): - accompany, assemble (with), come (together), come (company, go) with, resort.

d: **1.** to eat with, take food together with
s: From [G4862](G4862) and [G2068](G2068) (including its alternate); to *take* *food* in company *with:* - eat with.

d:
**1.** a running together, a flowing together with
**2.** knowledge
  **a.** understanding
  **b.** the understanding, i.e the mind so far forth as it understands
s: From [G4920](G4920); a mental *putting* *together*, that is, *intelligence* or (concretely) the *intellect:* - knowledge, understanding.

d: **1.** intelligent, having understanding, wise, learned
s: From [G4920](G4920); mentally *put* (or *putting*) *together*, that is, *sagacious:* - prudent. Compare [G5429](G5429).

d:
**1.** to be pleased together with, to approve together (with others)
**2.** to be pleased at the same time with, consent, agree to
  **a.** to applaud
s: From [G4862](G4862) and [G2106](G2106); to *think* *well* *of* *in* *common*, that is, *assent* to, *feel* *gratified* *with:* - allow, assent, be pleased, have pleasure.

d:
**1.** to entertain together
**2.** to feast sumptuously with
s: From [G4862](G4862) and a derivative of a presumed compound of [G2095](G2095) and a derivative of [G2192](G2192) (meaning to *be* *in* *good* *condition*, that is, \[by implication\] to *fare* *well*, or *feast*); to *entertain* sumptuously in company *with*, that is, (middle or passive voice) to *revel* *together:* - feast with.
o: from [G4862](G4862) and a derivative of a presumed compound of [G2095](G2095) and a derivative of [G2192](G2192) (meaning to be in good condition, i.e. \[by implication\] to fare well, or feast)

d:
**1.** to place over or appoint together
**2.** to rise up together
  **a.** against one
s: From [G4862](G4862) and [G2186](G2186); to *stand* *up* *together*, that is, to *resist* (or *assault*) *jointly:* - rise up together.

d:
**1.** to hold together
  **a.** any whole, lest it fall to pieces or something fall away from it
**2.** to hold together with constraint, to compress
  **a.** to press together with the hand
  **b.** to hold one’s ears, to shut the heavens that it may not rain
  **c.** to press on every side
    **1.** of a besieged city
    **2.** of a strait, that forces a ship into a narrow channel
    **3.** of a cattle squeeze, that pushing in on each side, forcing the beast into a position where it cannot move so the farmer can administer medication
**3.** to hold completely
  **a.** to hold fast
    **1.** of a prisoner
  **b.** metaph.
    **1.** to be held by, closely occupied with any business
    **2.** in teaching the word
    **3.** to constrain, oppress, of ills laying hold of one and distressing him
    **4.** to be held with, afflicted with, suffering from
    **5.** to urge, impel
**4.** of the soul
s: From [G4862](G4862) and [G2192](G2192); to *hold* *together*, that is, to *compress* (the ears, with a crowd or siege) or *arrest* (a prisoner); figuratively to *compel*, *perplex*, *afflict*, *preoccupy:* - constrain, hold, keep in, press, lie sick of, stop, be in a strait, straiten, be taken with, throng.

d:
**1.** to rejoice together with (another or others)
**2.** in the NT once to rejoice or delight with one’s self or inwardly
s: Middle voice from [G4862](G4862) and the base of [G2237](G2237); to *rejoice* in *with* oneself, that is, *feel* *satisfaction* concerning: - delight.
o: middle voice from [G4862](G4862) and the base of [G2237](G2237)

d:
**1.** intercourse (with one), intimacy
**2.** custom
**3.** a being used to, accustomed
s: From a compound of [G4862](G4862) and [G2239](G2239); *mutual* *habituation*, that is, *usage:* - custom.

d: **1.** one of the same age, an equal in age
s: From [G4862](G4862) and a derivative of [G2244](G2244); a *co-aged* person, that is, *alike* in years: - equal.

d: **1.** to bury together with
s: From [G4862](G4862) and [G2290](G2290); to *inter* in company *with*, that is, (figuratively) to *assimilate* spiritually (to Christ by a sepulture as to sin): - bury with.

d: **1.** to break to pieces, shatter
s: From [G4862](G4862) and θλάω thlaō (to *crush*); to *dash* *together*, that is, *shatter:* - break.

d: **1.** to press together, press on all sides
s: From [G4862](G4862) and [G2346](G2346); to *compress*, that is, *crowd* on all sides: - throng.

d:
**1.** break in pieces, to crush
**2.** metaph.
  **a.** to break one’s heart
  **b.** to deprive of strength and courage, dispirit, incapacitate for enduring trials
s: From [G4862](G4862) and θρύπτω thruptō (to *crumble*); to *crush* *together*, that is, (figuratively) to *dispirit:* - break.

d:
**1.** to set or bring together
  **a.** in a hostile sense, of combatants
**2.** to put (as it were) the perception with the thing perceived
  **a.** to set or join together in the mind
    **1.** i.e. to understand: the man of understanding
    **2.** idiom for: a good and upright man (having the knowledge of those things which pertain to salvation)
s: From [G4862](G4862) and ἵημι hiēmi (to *send*); to *put* *together*, that is, (mentally) to *comprehend*; by implication to *act* *piously:* - consider, understand, be wise.

d:
**1.** to place together, to set in the same place,to bring or band together
  **a.** to stand with (or near)
**2.** to set one with another
  **a.** by way of presenting or introducing him
  **b.** to comprehend
**3.** to put together by way of composition or combination, to teach by combining and comparing
  **a.** to show, prove, establish, exhibit
**4.** to put together, unite parts into one whole
  **a.** to be composed of, consist
s: From [G4862](G4862) and [G2476](G2476) (including its collateral forms); to *set* *together*, that is, (by implication) to *introduce* (favorably), or (figuratively) to *exhibit*; intransitively to *stand* *near*, or (figuratively) to *constitute:* - approve, commend, consist, make, stand (with).

d: **1.** to journey with, travel in company with
s: From [G4862](G4862) and [G3593](G3593); to *travel* in company *with:* - journey with.

d:
**1.** a journey in company
  **a.** of a company of travellers, associates on a journey, a caravan
s: From a compound of [G4862](G4862) and [G3598](G3598) (“synod”); *companionship* on a journey, that is, (by implication) a *caravan:* - company.

d:
**1.** to dwell together
  **a.** of the domestic association
  **b.** of intercourse of a husband and wife
s: From [G4862](G4862) and [G3611](G3611); to *reside* *together* (as a family): - dwell together.

d:
**1.** to build together
  **a.** to build together or with others
  **b.** to put together or construct by building, out of several things to build up one whole
    **1.** of the human body
s: From [G4862](G4862) and [G3618](G3618); to *construct*, that is, (passively) to *compose* (in company with other Christians, figuratively): - build together.

d: **1.** to talk with
s: From [G4862](G4862) and [G3656](G3656); to *converse* mutually: - talk with.

d:
**1.** to border on, be contiguous to
  **a.** of a thing
s: From [G4862](G4862) and a derivative of a compound of the base of [G3674](G3674) and the base of [G3725](G3725); to *border* *together*, that is, *adjoin:* - join hard.
o: from [G4862](G4862) and a derivative of a compound of the base of [G3674](G3674) and the base of [G3725](G3725)

d:
**1.** a holding together, a narrowing
**2.** the contracting part of a way
**3.** metaph. straits, distress, anguish
s: From [G4912](G4912); *restraint*, that is, (figuratively) *anxiety:* - anguish, distress.

d:
**1.** to put in order with or together, to arrange
**2.** to (put together), constitute
  **a.** to prescribe, appoint
s: From [G4862](G4862) and [G5021](G5021); to *arrange* *jointly*, that is, (figuratively) to *direct:* - appoint.

d: **1.** completion, consummation, end
s: From [G4931](G4931); *entire* *completion*, that is, *consummation* (of a dispensation): - end.

d:
**1.** to end together or at the same time
**2.** to end completely
  **a.** bring to an end, finish, complete
**3.** to accomplish, bring to fulfilment
  **a.** to come to pass
**4.** to effect, make, (conclude)
**5.** to finish
  **a.** to make an end of
  **b.** to bring to an end
  **c.** destroy
s: From [G4862](G4862) and [G5055](G5055); to *complete* *entirely*; generally to *execute* (literally or figuratively): - end, finish, fulfil, make.

d:
**1.** to cut in pieces
**2.** to cut short
**3.** metaph.
  **a.** to dispatch briefly, execute or finish quickly
  **b.** to hasten
  **c.** a short word i.e. an expedited prophecy or decree
s: From [G4862](G4862) and the base of [G5114](G5114); to *contract* by cutting, that is, (figuratively) *do* *concisely* (*speedily*): - (cut) short.

d:
**1.** to preserve (a thing from perishing or being lost)
**2.** to keep within one’s self, keep in mind (a thing, lest it be forgotten)
s: From [G4862](G4862) and [G5083](G5083); to *keep* closely *together*, that is, (by implication) to *conserve* (from ruin); mentally to *remember* (and *obey*): - keep, observe, preserve.

d:
**1.** to put together with, to place together, to join together
  **a.** to place in one’s mind
    **1.** to resolve, determine
    **2.** to make an arrangement, to engage
  **b.** to assent to, to agree to
s: Middle voice from [G4862](G4862) and [G5087](G5087); to *place* *jointly*, that is, (figuratively) to *consent* (*bargain*, *stipulate*), *concur:* - agree assent, covenant.

d: **1.** concisely, briefly, in a few words
s: Adverb from a derivative of [G4932](G4932); *concisely* (*briefly*): - a few words.

d:
**1.** to run together
  **a.** of the gathering of a multitude
**2.** to run along with others
**3.** metaph.
  **a.** to rush with, to cast one’s self, plunge
s: From [G4862](G4862) and [G5143](G5143) (including its alternate); to *rush* *together* (hastily *assemble*) or *headlong* (figuratively): - run (together, with).

d:
**1.** break, to break in pieces, shiver
**2.** to tread down
  **a.** to put Satan under foot and (as a conqueror) trample on him
  **b.** to break down, crush
    **1.** to tear one’s body and shatter one’s strength
s: From [G4862](G4862) and the base of [G5147](G5147); to *crush* *completely*, that is, to *shatter* (literally or figuratively): - break (in pieces), broken to shivers (+ -hearted), bruise.

d:
**1.** that which is broken or shattered, a fracture
**2.** calamity, ruin, destruction
s: From [G4937](G4937); *concussion* or utter *fracture* (properly concretely), that is, complete *ruin:* - destruction.

d:
**1.** nourished with one
**2.** brought up with one
**3.** companion of one’s childhood and youth
s: From [G4862](G4862) and [G5162](G5162) (in a passive sense); a *fellow* *nursling*, that is, *comrade:* - brought up with.

d: **1.** to meet with, come
s: From [G4862](G4862) and [G5177](G5177); to *chance* *together*, that is, *meet* with (*reach*): - come at.

d:
Syntyche = with fate
**1.** a female member of the church of Philippi
s: From [G4940](G4940); an *accident*; *Syntyche*, a Christian female: - Syntyche.

d:
**1.** to dissemble with
**2.** to act hypocritically with
s: From [G4862](G4862) and [G5271](G5271); to *act* *hypocritically* in concert *with:* - dissemble with.

d: **1.** to help together
s: From [G4862](G4862) and a derivative of a compound of [G5259](G5259) and the base of [G2041](G2041); to *be* *a* *co-auxiliary*, that is, *assist:* - help together.
o: from [G4862](G4862) and a derivative of a compound of [G5259](G5259) and the base of [G2041](G2041)

d:
**1.** to feel the pains of travail with, be in travail together
**2.** metaph. to undergo agony (like a woman in childbirth) along with
s: From [G4862](G4862) and [G5605](G5605); to *have* (parturition) *pangs* in company (concert, simultaneously) *with*, that is, (figuratively) to *sympathize* (in expectation of relief from suffering): - travail in pain together.

d:
**1.** a swearing together
**2.** a conspiracy
s: From a compound of [G4862](G4862) and [G3660](G3660); a *swearing* *together*, that is, (by implication) a *plot:* - conspiracy.

d:
Syracuse = a Syrian hearing
**1.** a large maritime city of Sicily, having an excellent harbour and surrounded by a 14 mile (23 km) wall
s: Plural of uncertain derivation; *Syracusae*, the capital of Sicily: - Syracuse.

d:
Syria = exalted
**1.** a region of Asia bounded on the north by Taurus and amanus ranges, on the east by the Euphrates and Arabia, on the south by Palestine, and the west by Phoenicia and the mediterranean
s: Probably of Hebrew origin \[[H6865](H6865)\]; *Syria* (that is, *Tsyria* or *Tyre*), a region of Asia: - Syria.

d: **1.** an inhabitant of Syria
s: From the same as [G4947](G4947); a *Syran* (that is, probably *Tyrian*), a native of Syria: - Syrian.

d:
Syrophenician = exalted palm
**1.** the name of a mixed nation, half Phoenicians and half Syrians
s: Feminine of a compound of [G4948](G4948) and the same as [G5403](G5403); a *Syro-Phaenician* woman, that is, a female native of Phaenicia in Syria: - Syrophenician.
o: from a compound of [G4948](G4948) and the same as [G5403](G5403)

d: **1.** Syrtis, the name of two places in the African or Libyan Sea between Carthage and Cyrenaicia, full of shallows and sandbanks, and therefore destructive to ships; the western Syrtis, between the islands Cercina and meninx (or the promontories of Zeitha and Brachodes), was called Syris minor, the eastern (extending from the promontories of Cephalae on the west to that of Boreum on the east) was called Syris major; this latter must be the one referred to in Act 27:17, for upon this the ship in which Paul was sailing might easily be cast after leaving Crete
s: From [G4951](G4951); a *shoal* (from the sand *drawn* thither by the waves), that is, the *Syrtis* Major or great bay on the North coast of Africa: - quicksands.

d:
**1.** to draw, drag
  **a.** of one before the judge, to prison, to punishment
s: Probably akin to [G138](G138); to *trail:* - drag, draw, hale.

d: **1.** to convulse completely
s: From [G4862](G4862) and [G4682](G4682); to *rend* *completely*, that is, (by analogy) to *convulse* violently: - throw down.

d:
**1.** a common sign or concerted signal
**2.** a sign given according to agreement
s: Neuter of a compound of [G4862](G4862) and the base of [G4591](G4591); a *sign* *in* *common*, that is, preconcerted *signal:* - token.
o: from a compound of [G4862](G4862) and the base of [G4591](G4591)

d:
**1.** belonging to the same body
**2.** metaph. to the same church
