s: From [G4862](G4862) and [G4983](G4983); *of* a *joint* *body*, that is, (figuratively) a *fellow* *member* of the Christian community: - of the same body.

d: **1.** a companion in insurrection, a fellow rioter
s: From a compound of [G4862](G4862) and a derivative of [G4714](G4714); a *fellow* *insurgent:* - make insurrection with.
o: from a compound of [G4862](G4862) and a derivative of [G4714](G4714)

d: **1.** commendatory, introductory
s: From a derivative of [G4921](G4921); *introductory*, that is, *recommendatory:* - of commendation.

d: **1.** to crucify alone with
s: From [G4862](G4862) and [G4717](G4717); to *impale* in company *with* (literally or figuratively): - crucify with.

d:
**1.** to place together
  **a.** to draw together, contact
    **1.** to diminish
    **2.** to shorten, abridge
    **3.** the time has been drawn together into a brief compass, is shortened
  **b.** to roll together, wrap up, wrap around with bandages, etc., to enshroud
s: From [G4862](G4862) and [G4724](G4724); to *send* (*draw*) *together*, that is, *enwrap* (*enshroud* a corpse for burial), *contract* (an interval): - short, wind up.

d: **1.** to groan together
s: From [G4862](G4862) and [G4727](G4727); to *moan* *jointly*, that is, (figuratively) *experience* *a* *common* *calamity:* - groan together.

d:
**1.** to stand or march in the same row (file) with
  **a.** of soldiers
  **b.** to stand over against, be parallel with
  **c.** to answer to, resemble
    **1.** so once of a type in the OT which answers to the antitype in the NT
s: From [G4862](G4862) and [G4748](G4748); to *file* *together* (as soldiers in ranks), that is, (figuratively) to *correspond* to: - answer to.

d:
**1.** a fellow soldier
**2.** an associate in labours and conflicts for the cause of christ
s: From [G4862](G4862) and [G4757](G4757); a *co-campaigner*, that is, (figuratively) an *associate* in Christian toil: - fellowsoldier.

d:
**1.** to twist together, roll together
**2.** to collect, combine, unite
  **a.** of men, to (gather themselves together) assemble
s: From [G4862](G4862) and [G4762](G4762); to *twist* *together*, that is, *collect* (a bundle, a crowd): - gather.

d:
**1.** a twisting up together, a binding together
**2.** a secret combination, a coalition, conspiracy
**3.** a concourse of disorderly persons, a riot
s: From [G4962](G4962); a *twisting* *together*, that is, (figuratively) a secret *coalition*, riotous *crowd:* - + band together, concourse.

d: **1.** to conform one’s self (i.e. one’s mind and character) to another’s pattern, (fashion one’s self according to)
s: From [G4862](G4862) and a derivative of [G4976](G4976); to *fashion* *alike*, that is, *conform* to the same pattern (figuratively): - conform to, fashion self according to.

d:
Sychar = drunken
**1.** probably another name for the town of Shechem, a town in Samaria, near the well of Jacob
s: Of Hebrew origin \[[H7941](H7941)\]; *Sychar* (that is, *Shekar*), a place in Palestine: - Sychar.

d:
Shechem = shoulder (literal early rising): diligence
**1.** a city in Ephraim
**2.** the son of Emmor
s: Of Hebrew origin \[[H7927](H7927)\]; *Sychem* (that is, *Shekem*), the name of a Canaanite and of a place in Palestine: - Sychem.

d:
**1.** slaughter
  **a.** of sheep destined for slaughter
  **b.** of day of destruction
s: From [G4969](G4969); *butchery* (of animals for food or sacrifice, or \[figuratively\] of men \[*destruction*\]): - slaughter.

d: **1.** that which is destined for slaughter, a victim
s: Neuter of a derivative of [G4967](G4967); a *victim* (in sacrifice): - slain beast.

d:
**1.** to slay, slaughter, butcher
**2.** to put to death by violence
**3.** mortally wounded
s: A primary verb; to *butcher* (especially an animal for food or in sacrifice) or (generally) to *slaughter*, or (specifically) to *maim* (violently): - kill, slay, wound.

d: **1.** exceedingly, greatly
s: Neuter plural of σφοδρός sphodros (*violent*; of uncertain derivation) as adverb; *vehemently*, that is, in *a* *high* *degree*, *much:* - exceeding (-ly), greatly, sore, very.
o: neuter plural of sphodros (violent, of uncertain derivation) as adverb

d: **1.** exceedingly
s: Adverbially from the same as [G4970](G4970); *very* *much:* - exceedingly.

d:
**1.** to set a seal upon, mark with a seal, to seal
  **a.** for security: from Satan
  **b.** since things sealed up are concealed (as the contents of a letter), to hide, keep in silence, keep secret
  **c.** in order to mark a person or a thing
    **1.** to set a mark upon by the impress of a seal or a stamp
    **2.** angels are said to be sealed by God
  **d.** in order to prove, confirm, or attest a thing
    **1.** to confirm authenticate, place beyond doubt
  **e.** of a written document
  **f.** to prove one’s testimony to a person that he is what he professes to be
s: From [G4973](G4973); to *stamp* (with a signet or private mark) for security or preservation (literally or figuratively); by implication to *keep* *secret*, to *attest:* - (set a, set to) seal up, stop.

d:
**1.** a seal
  **a.** the seal placed upon books
  **b.** a signet ring
  **c.** the inscription or impression made by a seal
    **1.** of the name of God and christ stamped upon their foreheads
  **d.** that by which anything is confirmed, proved, authenticated, as by a seal (a token or proof)
s: Probably strengthened from [G5420](G5420); a *signet* (as *fencing* in or protecting from misappropriation); by implication the *stamp* impressed (as a mark of privacy, or genuineness), literally or figuratively: - seal.

d: **1.** the ankle
s: Neuter of a presumed derivative probably of the same as σφαῖρα sphaira (a *ball*, “sphere”; compare the feminine σφῦρα sphura , a *hammer*); the ankle (as globular): - ancle bone.
o: from a presumed derivative probably of the same as sphaira (a ball, sphere, cf the feminine sphura, a hammer)

d:
**1.** near, hard by
**2.** well nigh, nearly, almost
s: Neuter of a presumed derivative of the alternate of [G2192](G2192) as an adverb; *nigh*, that is, *nearly:* - almost.
o: neuter of a presumed derivative of the alternate of [G2192](G2192) as adverb

d: **1.** the habitus, as comprising everything in a person which strikes the senses, the figure, bearing, discourse, actions, manner of life etc.
s: From the alternate of [G2192](G2192); a *figure* (as a *mode* or *circumstance*), that is, (by implication) external *condition:* - fashion.

d:
**1.** to cleave, cleave asunder, rend
**2.** to divide by rending
**3.** to split into factions, be divided
s: Apparently a primary verb; to *split* or *sever* (literally or figuratively): - break, divide, open, rend, make a rent.

d:
**1.** a rent
**2.** metaph. a division, dissension
s: From [G4977](G4977); a *split* or *gap* (“schism”), literally or figuratively: - division, rent, schism.

d:
**1.** a cord or rope made of rushes
**2.** a rope
s: Diminutive of σχοῖνος schoinos (a *rush* or *flag* plant; of uncertain derivation); a *rushlet*, that is, *grass* *withe* or *tie* (genitive case): - small cord, rope.
o: diminutive of schoinos (a rush or flag-plant, of uncertain derivation)

d:
**1.** to cease from labour, to loiter
**2.** to be free from labour, to be at leisure, to be idle
  **a.** to have leisure for a thing
  **b.** to give one’s self to a thing
**3.** of things
  **a.** of places, to be unoccupied, empty
  **b.** of a centurion’s vacant office
  **c.** of vacant ecclesiastical offices
  **d.** of officers without charge
s: From [G4981](G4981); to *take* *a* *holiday*, that is, *be* *at* *leisure* for (by implication *devote* *oneself* wholly to); figuratively to *be* *vacant* (of a house): - empty, give self.

d:
**1.** freedom from labour
**2.** a place where there is leisure for anything, a school
s: Probably feminine of a presumed derivative of the alternate of [G2192](G2192); properly *loitering* (as a *withholding* of oneself from work) or *leisure*, that is, (by implication) a “school” (as *vacation* from physical employment): - school.
o: probably feminine of a presumed derivative of the alternate of [G2192](G2192)

d:
**1.** to save, keep safe and sound, to rescue from danger or destruction
  **a.** one (from injury or peril)
    **1.** to save a suffering one (from perishing), i.e. one suffering from disease, to make well, heal, restore to health
    **2.** to preserve one who is in danger of destruction, to save or rescue
  **b.** to save in the technical biblical sense
    **1.** negatively
  **c.** to deliver from the penalties of the messianic judgment
  **d.** to save from the evils which obstruct the reception of the messianic deliverance
s: From a primary word σῶς sōs̄ (contraction for the obsolete σάος saos, “safe”); to *save*, that is, *deliver* or *protect* (literally or figuratively): - heal, preserve, save (self), do well, be (make) whole.
o: from a primary sos (contraction for obsolete saoz, safe)

d:
**1.** the body both of men or animals
  **a.** a dead body or corpse
  **b.** the living body
    **1.** of animals
**2.** the bodies of planets and of stars (heavenly bodies)
**3.** is used of a (large or small) number of men closely united into one society, or family as it were; a social, ethical, mystical body
  **a.** so in the NT of the church
**4.** that which casts a shadow as distinguished from the shadow itself
s: From [G4982](G4982); the *body* (as a *sound* whole), used in a very wide application, literally or figuratively: - bodily, body, slave.

d:
**1.** corporeal, bodily
  **a.** having a bodily form or nature
  **b.** pertaining to the body
s: From [G4983](G4983); *corporeal* or *physical:* - bodily.

d:
**1.** bodily, corporally
  **a.** of the exalted spiritual body, visible only to the inhabitants of heaven
s: Adverb from [G4984](G4984); *corporeally* or *physically:* - bodily.

d:

d:
Tarsus = a flat basket
**1.** a major city in Cilicia and the birthplace and early home of Paul. Act 9:11; Act 21:39; Act 22:3. Even in the flourishing period of Greek history it was an important city. In the Roman civil wars, it sided with Caesar and on the occasion of a visit from him its name changed to Juliopolis. Augustus made it a free city. Its was renowned as a place of education under the early Roman emperors. Strabo compares it in this respect to Athens and Alexandria. Tarsus also was a place of much commerce. It was situated in a wild and fertile plain on the banks of the Cydnus. No ruins of any importance remain.
s: Perhaps the same as ταρσός tarsos (a *flat* basket); *Tarsus*, a place in Asia Minor: - Tarsus.
o: perhaps the same as tarsos (a flat basket)
