d: **1.** the fourteenth
s: From [G5064](G5064) and [G2532](G2532) and [G1182](G1182); *fourteenth:* - fourteenth.

d: **1.** on the fourth day
s: From [G5064](G5064); pertaining to the *fourth* day: - four days.

d: **1.** the fourth
s: From [G5064](G5064); *fourth:* - four (-th).

d: **1.** quadrangular, square
s: From [G5064](G5064) and [G1137](G1137); *four* *cornered*, that is, *square:* - foursquare.

d: **1.** a quaternion
s: Neuter of a presumed derivative of τέτρας tetras (a *tetrad*; from [G5064](G5064)); a *quaternion* or squad (picket) of four Roman soldiers: - quaternion.
o: from a presumed derivative of tetras (a tetrad, from [G5064](G5064))

d: **1.** four thousand
s: From the multiplicative adverb of [G5064](G5064) and [G5507](G5507); *four* *times* *a* *thousand:* - four thousand.
o: from the multiplicative adverb of [G5064](G5064) and [G5507](G5507)

d: **1.** four hundred
s: Neuter and plural from [G5064](G5064) and [G1540](G1540); *four* *hundred:* - four hundred.

d: **1.** of four months, lasting four months
s: Neuter of a compound of [G5064](G5064) and [G3376](G3376); a *four* *months’* space: - four months.
o: neuter of a compound of [G5064](G5064) and [G3376](G3376)

d: **1.** quadruple, fourfold
s: From [G5064](G5064) and a derivative of the base of [G4118](G4118); *quadruple:* - fourfold.
o: from [G5064](G5064) and a derivative of the base of [G4118](G4118)

d: **1.** a fourfooted animal
s: From [G5064](G5064) and [G4228](G4228); a *quadruped:* - fourfooted beast.

d: **1.** to be a governor of a tetrarchy, be tetrarch of a region
s: From [G5076](G5076); to *be* *a* *tetrarch:* - (be) tetrarch.

d:
**1.** a tetrarch
  **a.** a governor of the fourth part of a region. Thus Strabo states that Galactia was formerly divided into three parts, each one of which was distributed into four smaller subdivisions each of which was governed by a tetrarch. Strabo relates that thessaly, before the time of Philip of Macedon, had been divided into four tetrarchies, each having its own tetrarch.
  **b.** the governor of a third part or half a country, or even a ruler of an entire country or district provided it were of comparatively narrow limits; a petty prince. Thus Antony made herod (afterwards king) and Phasael, sons of Antipater, tetrarchs of Palestine. After the death of herod the great, his sons, Achelaus styled an ethnarch but Antipas and Philip with the title of tetrarchs, divided and governed the kingdom left by their father.
s: From [G5064](G5064) and [G757](G757); the *ruler* *of* *a* *fourth* part of a country (“tetrarch”): - tetrarch.

d: **1.** reduce to ashes
s: From τέφρα tephra (*ashes*); to *incinerate*, that is, *consume:* - turn to ashes.

d:
**1.** of the plastic art
**2.** of a trade
s: From the base of [G5088](G5088); *art* (as *productive*), that is, (specifically) a *trade*, or (generally) *skill:* - art, craft, occupation.

d: **1.** an artificer, craftsman
s: From [G5078](G5078); an *artisan*; figuratively a *founder* (*Creator*): - builder, craftsman.

d:
**1.** to make liquid
**2.** to become liquid, to melt
**3.** to perish or become destroyed by melting
s: Apparently a primary verb; to *liquefy:* - melt.

d: **1.** at a distance and clearly
s: Adverb from a compound of a derivative of [G5056](G5056) and [G827](G827); in a *far* *shining* manner, that is, *plainly:* - clearly.
o: from a compound of a derivative of [G5056](G5056) and [G827](G827)

d:
**1.** of age
  **a.** of such an age
  **b.** of so great an age, so old
  **c.** so young
**2.** of so great a size, in bulk
**3.** such and so great
s: Masculine and feminine; from a compound of [G3588](G3588) with [G2245](G2245) and [G3778](G3778); *such* *as* *this*, that is, (in \[figuratively\] magnitude) *so* *vast:* - so great, so mighty.
o: from a compound of [G3588](G3588) with [G2245](G2245) and [G3778](G3778)

d:
**1.** to attend to carefully, take care of
  **a.** to guard
  **b.** metaph. to keep, one in the state in which he is
  **c.** to observe
  **d.** to reserve: to undergo something
s: From τηρός teros (a *watch*; perhaps akin to [G2334](G2334)); to *guard* (from *loss* or *injury*, properly by keeping *the* *eye* upon; and thus differing from [G5442](G5442), which is properly to *prevent* escaping; and from [G2892](G2892), which implies a *fortress* or full military lines of apparatus), that is, to *note* (a prophecy; figuratively to *fulfil* a command); by implication to *detain* (in custody; figuratively to *maintain*); by extension to *withhold* (for personal ends; figuratively to *keep* *unmarried*): - hold fast, keep (-er), (ob-, pre-, re) serve, watch.
o: from teros (a watch, perhaps akin to [G2334](G2334))

d:
**1.** a watching
  **a.** of prisoners
  **b.** a place where prisoners are kept, a prison
**2.** a keeping
  **a.** complying with, obeying
s: From [G5083](G5083); a *watching*, that is, (figuratively) *observance*, or (concretely) a *prison:* - hold.

d:
Tiberias = from the Tiber (as river-god)
**1.** a city of Galilee near the Lake of Gennesaret, which herod Antipas, tetrarch of Galilee, greatly enlarged and beautified, and named Tiberias in honour of Tiberias Caesar
s: From [G5086](G5086); *Tiberias*, the name of a town and a lake in Palestine: - Tiberias.

d:
Tiberius = from the Tiber (as God-river)
**1.** the second Roman emperor
s: Of Latin origin; probably *pertaining* *to* *the* river *Tiberis* or *Tiber*; *Tiberius*, a Roman emperor: - Tiberius.

d:
**1.** to set, put, place
  **a.** to place or lay
  **b.** to put down, lay down
    **1.** to bend down
    **2.** to lay off or aside, to wear or carry no longer
    **3.** to lay by, lay aside money
  **c.** to set on (serve) something to eat or drink
  **d.** to set forth, something to be explained by discourse
**2.** to make
  **a.** to make (or set) for one’s self or for one’s use
**3.** to set, fix establish
  **a.** to set forth
  **b.** to establish, ordain
s: A prolonged form of a primary word θέω theō (which is used only as an alternate in certain tenses); to *place* (in the widest application, literally and figuratively; properly in a passive or horizontal posture, and thus different from [G2476](G2476), which properly denotes an upright and active position, while [G2749](G2749) is properly reflexive and utterly prostrate): - + advise, appoint, bow, commit, conceive, give, X kneel down, lay (aside, down, up), make, ordain, purpose, put, set (forth), settle, sink down.
o: a prolonged form of a primary theo theh’-o (which is used only as alternate in certain tenses)

d:
**1.** to bring forth, bear, produce (fruit from the seed)
  **a.** of a woman giving birth
  **b.** of the earth bringing forth its fruits
  **c.** metaph. to bear, bring forth
s: A strengthened from of a primary word τέκω tekō (which is used only as an alternate in certain tenses); to *produce* (from seed, as a mother, a plant, the earth, etc.), literal or figurative: - bear, be born, bring forth, be delivered, be in travail.
o: a strengthened form of a primary teko tek’-o (which is used only as alternate in certain tenses)

d: **1.** to pluck, pluck off
s: Perhaps akin to the alternate of [G138](G138), and thus to [G4951](G4951); to *pull* off: - pluck.
o: perhaps akin to the alternate of [G138](G138), and thus to [G4951](G4951)

d:
Timaeus = highly prized
**1.** the father of the blind man, Bartimaeus
s: Probably of Chaldee origin (compare \[[H2931](H2931)\]); *Timoeus* (that is, *Timay*), an Israelite: - Timaeus.

d:
**1.** to estimate, fix the value
  **a.** for the value of something belonging to one’s self
**2.** to honour, to have in honour, to revere, venerate
s: From [G5093](G5093); to *prize*, that is, *fix* a *valuation* upon; by implication to *revere:* - honour, value.

d:
**1.** a valuing by which the price is fixed
  **a.** of the price itself
  **b.** of the price paid or received for a person or thing bought or sold
**2.** honour which belongs or is shown to one
  **a.** of the honour which one has by reason of rank and state of office which he holds
  **b.** deference, reverence
s: From [G5099](G5099); a *value*, that is, *money* paid, or (concretely and collectively) *valuables*; by analogy *esteem* (especially of the highest degree), or the *dignity* itself: - honour, precious, price, some.

d:
**1.** as of great price, precious
**2.** held in honour, esteemed, especially dear
s: Including the comparative τίμιώτερος timiōteros and the superlative τίμιώτατος timiōtatos; from [G5092](G5092); *valuable*, that is, (objectively) *costly*, or (subjectively) *honored*, *esteemed*, or (figuratively) *beloved:* - dear, honourable, (more, most) precious, had in reputation.

d:
**1.** preciousness, costliness
  **a.** an abundance of costly things
**2.** metaph. worth, excellence
s: From [G5093](G5093); *expensiveness*, that is, (by implication) *magnificence:* - costliness.

d:
Timothy = honouring God
**1.** a resident of Lystra, apparently, whose father was a Greek and mother a Jewess; he was Paul’s travelling companion and fellow labourer
s: From [G5092](G5092) and [G2316](G2316); *dear* *to* *God*; *Timotheus*, a Christian: - Timotheus, Timothy.

d:
Timon = honourable
**1.** one of the seven deacons of the church at Jerusalem
s: From [G5092](G5092); *valuable*; *Timon*, a Christian: - Timon.

d:
**1.** to be a guardian or avenger of honour
  **a.** to succour, come to the help of
**2.** to avenge
**3.** in the NT, to take vengeance on one, to punish
s: From a compound of [G5092](G5092) and οὖρος ouros (a *guard*); properly to *protect* one’s *honor*, that is, to *avenge* (*inflict* *a* *penalty*): - punish.
o: from a comparative of [G5092](G5092) and ouros (a guard)

d:
**1.** a rendering help
**2.** assistance
**3.** vengeance, punishment, penalty
s: From [G5097](G5097); *vindication*, that is, (by implication) a *penalty:* - punishment.

d:
**1.** to pay, to recompense
**2.** to pay penalty, suffer punishment
s: Strengthened for a primary word τίω tiō (which is only used as an alternate in certain tenses); to *pay* a price, that is, as a *penalty:* - be punished with.
o: strengthened for a primary tio tee’-o (which is only used as an alternate in certain tenses)

d:
**1.** a certain, a certain one
**2.** some, some time, a while
s: An enclitic indefinite pronoun; *some* or *any* person or object: - a (kind of), any (man, thing, thing at all), certain (thing), divers, he (every) man, one (X thing), ought, + partly, some (man, -body, -thing, -what), (+ that no-) thing, what (-soever), X wherewith, whom \[-soever\], whose (\[-soever\]).

d: **1.** who, which, what
s: Probably emphatic of [G5100](G5100); an interrogitive pronoun, *who*, *which* or *what* (in direct or indirect questions): - every man, how (much), + no (-ne, thing), what (manner, thing), where (\[-by, -fore, -of, -unto, -with, -withal\]), whether, which, who (-m, -se), why.

d:
**1.** a title
**2.** an inscription, giving the accusation or crime for which a criminal suffered
s: Of Latin origin; a *titulus* or “title” (*placard*): - title.

d:
Titus = nurse
**1.** a Gentile Christian an Paul’s companion in some of his journeys
s: Of Latin origin but uncertain significance; *Titus*, a Christian: - Titus.
o: of Latin origin but uncertain signification

d: **1.** certainly, truly
s: Probably for the dative case of [G3588](G3588); an enclitic particle of *asseveration* by way of contrast; *in* *sooth*: - \[used only with other particles in compounds, as [G2544](G2544), [G3305](G3305), [G5105](G5105), [G5106](G5106), etc.\]
o: probably for the dative case of [G3588](G3588)

d: **1.** wherefore then, for which reason, therefore, consequently
s: From [G5104](G5104) and [G1063](G1063) and [G3767](G3767); *truly* *for* *then*, that is, *consequently:* - there- (where-) fore.

d: **1.** therefore, then, accordingly
s: From [G5104](G5104) and [G3568](G3568); *truly* *now*, that is, *accordingly:* - then, therefore.

d: **1.** such
s: (Including the other inflections); from a derivative of [G5104](G5104) and [G1161](G1161); *such* *like* *then*, that is, *so* *great:* - such.

d: **1.** such as this, of this kind or sort
s: (Including the other inflections); from [G5104](G5104) and [G3778](G3778); *truly* *this*, that is, *of* *this* *sort* (to denote character or individuality): - like, such (an one).

d: **1.** a wall (of a house)
s: Another form of [G5038](G5038); a *wall:* - wall.

d:
**1.** birth
  **a.** the act of bringing forth
  **b.** that which has been brought forth, offspring
**2.** interest of money, usury (because it multiplies money, and as it were breeds)
s: From the base of [G5088](G5088); *interest* on money loaned (as a *produce*): - usury.

d:
**1.** not to dread or shun through fear
**2.** to bear, endure
**3.** to bring one’s self to
**4.** to be bold
**5.** bear one’s self boldly, deal boldly
s: From τόλμα tolma (*boldness*; probably itself from the base of [G5056](G5056) through the idea of *extreme* conduct); to *venture* (objectively or in *act*; while [G2292](G2292) is rather subjective or in *feeling*); by implication to be *courageous:* - be bold, boldly, dare, durst.
o: from tolma (boldness, probably itself from the base of [G5056](G5056) through the idea of extreme conduct)

d: **1.** more boldly
s: Neuter of the compound of a derivative of the bse of [G5111](G5111) (as adverb); *more* *daringly*, that is, *with* *greater* *confidence* than otherwise: - the more boldly.
o: neuter of the compound of a derivative of the base of [G5111](G5111) (as adverb)

d: **1.** a daring man
s: From [G5111](G5111); a *daring* (*audacious*) man: - presumptuous.

d: **1.** sharper
s: Compound of a derivative of the primary word τέμνω temnō (to *cut*; more comprehensive or decisive than [G2875](G2875), as if by a *single* stroke; whereas that implies repeated blows, like *hacking*); *more* *keen:* - sharper.
o: comparative of a derivative of the primary temno (to cut, more comprehensive or decisive than [G2875](G2875), as if by a single stroke, whereas that implies repeated blows, like hacking)

d: **1.** a bow
s: From the base of [G5088](G5088); a *bow* (apparently as the simplest fabric): - bow.

d: **1.** topaz, a greenish yellow precious stone (our chrysolite)
s: Neuter of a presumed derivative (alternate) of τόπάζος topazos (a “topaz”; of uncertain origin); a gem, probably the *chrysolite:* - topaz.
o: from a presumed derivative (alternately) of topazos (a topaz, of uncertain origin)

d:
**1.** place, any portion or space marked off, as it were from surrounding space
  **a.** an inhabited place, as a city, village, district
  **b.** a place (passage) in a book
**2.** metaph.
  **a.** the condition or station held by one in any company or assembly
  **b.** opportunity, power, occasion for acting
s: Apparently a primary word; a *spot* (generally in *space*, but limited by occupancy; whereas [G5561](G5561) is a larger but particular *locality*), that is, *location* (as a position, home, tract, etc.); figuratively *condition*, *opportunity*; specifically a *scabbard:* - coast, licence, place, X plain, quarter, + rock, room, where.

d:
**1.** of quantity: so great, so many
**2.** of time: so long
s: From τόσος tosos (*so* *much*; apparently from [G3588](G3588) and [G3739](G3739)) and [G3778](G3778) (including its variations); so *vast* *as* *this*, that is, *such* (in quantity, amount, number or space): - as large, so great (long, many, much), these many.
o: from tosos (so much, apparently from [G3588](G3588) and [G3739](G3739)) and [G3778](G3778) (including its variations)

d:
**1.** then
**2.** at that time
s: From (the neuter of) [G3588](G3588) and [G3753](G3753); *the* *when*, that is, *at* *the* *time* that (of the past or future, also in consecution): - that time, then.
Properly the genitive case of [G3588](G3588); sometimes used for [G5127](G5127); *of* *this* *person:* - his.

d: **1.** on the contrary, contrariwise
s: Contraction for the neuter of [G3588](G3588) and [G1726](G1726); *on* *the* *contrary:* - contrariwise.
o: contraction for the neuter of [G3588](G3588) and [G1726](G1726)

d: **1.** by name
s: Contraction for the neuter of [G3588](G3588) and [G3686](G3686); *the* *name* (is): - named.
o: contraction for the neuter of [G3588](G3588) and [G3686](G3686)

d: **1.** that is
s: Contraction for [G5124](G5124) and [G2076](G2076); *that* *is:* - that is (to say).

d: **1.** that (thing), this (thing)
s: Neuter, singular, nomitive or accusative of [G3778](G3778); *that* thing: - here \[-unto\], it, partly, self \[-same\], so, that (intent), the same, there \[-fore, -unto\], this, thus, where \[-fore\].
o: neuter singular nominative or accusative case of [G3778](G3778)

d: **1.** these
s: Dative, plural, masculine or neuter of [G3778](G3778); *to* (*for*, *in*, *with* or *by*) *these* (persons or things): - such, them, there \[-in, -with\], these, this, those.
o: dative case plural masculine or neuter of [G3778](G3778)

d: **1.** this
s: Accusative, singular, masculine of [G3778](G3778); *this* (person, as object of verb or preposition): - him, the same, that, this.

d: **1.** of this one
s: Genitive singular masculine or neuter of [G3778](G3778); *of* (*from* or *concerning*) *this* (person or thing): - here \[-by\], him, it, + such manner of, that, thence \[-forth\], thereabout, this, thus.
o: genitive case singular masculine or neuter of [G3778](G3778)

d: **1.** these
s: Accusative plural masculine of [G3778](G3778); *these* (persons, as object of verb or preposition): - such, them, these, this.

d: **1.** to this one
s: Dative singular masculine or neuter of [G3778](G3778); *to* (*in*, *with* or *by*) *this* (person or thing): - here \[-by, -in\], him, one, the same, there \[-in\], this.
o: dative case singular masculine or neuter of [G3778](G3778)

d: **1.** of these
s: Genitive plural masculine or neuter of [G3778](G3778); *of* (*from* or *concerning*) *these* (persons or things): - such, their, these (things), they, this sort, those.
o: genitive case plural masculine or neuter of [G3778](G3778)

d: **1.** male goat
s: From the base of [G5176](G5176); a *he* *goat* (as a *gnawer*): - goat.

d:
**1.** a table
  **a.** a table on which food is placed, an eating place
    **1.** the table in the temple at Jerusalem on which the consecrated loaves were placed
  **b.** equiv. to the food placed upon the table
    **1.** to set a table
    **2.** put food before one
  **c.** a banquet, feast
**2.** the table or stand of a money changer, where he sits, exchanging different kinds of money for a fee (agio), and paying back with interest loans or deposits
s: Probably contracted from [G5064](G5064) and [G3979](G3979); a *table* or *stool* (as being *four* *legged*), usually for food (figuratively a *meal*); also a *counter* for money (figuratively a broker’s *office* for loans at interest): - bank, meat, table.

d:
**1.** a money changer, broker, banker
**2.** one who exchanges money for a fee, and pays interest on deposits
s: From [G5132](G5132); a money *broker* or *banker:* - exchanger.

d: **1.** a wound
s: From the base of τιτρώσκω titrōskō (to *wound*; akin to the base of [G2352](G2352), [G5147](G5147), [G5149](G5149), etc.); a *wound:* - wound.
o: from the base of titrosko (to wound

d: **1.** to wound
s: From [G5134](G5134); to *inflict* *a* *wound:* - wound.

d:
**1.** to seize and twist the neck or throat
  **a.** of combatants who handle thus their antagonist
**2.** to bend back the neck of a victim to be slain, to lay bare or expose by bending back
**3.** to lay bare, uncover, expose
**4.** laid bare, laid open, made manifest to one
s: From [G5137](G5137); to *seize* by *the* *throat* or *neck*, that is, to *expose* the *gullet* of a victim for killing (generally to *lay* *bare*): - opened.

d: **1.** to be ready to incur the most imminent peril to life
s: Probably from [G5143](G5143) (through the idea of *mobility*); the *throat* (*neck*), that is, (figuratively) *life:* - neck.
o: probably from [G5143](G5143) (through the idea of mobility)

d:
**1.** rough, rocky
  **a.** of places of the sea
s: Perhaps strengthened from the base of [G4486](G4486) (as if *jagged* by rents); *uneven*, *rocky* (*reefy*): - rock, rough.
o: perhaps strengthened from the base of [G4486](G4486) (as if jagged by rents)

d:
Trachonitis = a rugged region
**1.** a rough region, inhabited by robbers, situated between Antilibanus on the west and on the east by the mountains of Batanaea and on the north by the territory of Damascus
s: From a derivative of [G5138](G5138); *rough* district; *Trachonitis*, a region of Syria: - Trachonitis.

d: **1.** three
s: A primary (plural) number; “three”: - three.

d:
**1.** tremble
**2.** to fear, be afraid
s: Strengthened from a primary word τρέω treō (to “dread”, “terrify”); to “tremble” or *fear:* - be afraid, trembling.
o: strengthened from a primary treo (to dread, terrify)

d:
**1.** to nourish, support
**2.** feed
**3.** to give suck, to fatten
**4.** to bring up, nurture
s: A primary verb (properly θρέφω threphō; but perhaps strengthened from the base of [G5157](G5157) through the idea of *convolution*); properly to *stiffen*, that is, *fatten* (by implication to *cherish* \[with food, etc.\], *pamper*, *rear*): - bring up, feed, nourish.

d:
**1.** to run
  **a.** of persons in haste
  **b.** of those who run in a race course
**2.** metaph.
  **a.** of doctrine rapidly propagated
  **b.** by a metaphor taken from runners in a race, to exert one’s self, strive hard
  **c.** to spend one’s strength in performing or attaining something
  **d.** word occurs in Greek writings denoting to incur extreme peril, which it requires the exertion of all one’s effort to overcome
s: Apparently a primary verb (properly θρέχω threchō; compare [G2359](G2359)); which uses δρέμω dremō, *drem’-o* (the base of [G1408](G1408)) as an alternate in certain tenses; to *run* or *walk* *hastily* (literally or figuratively): - have course, run.
o: apparently a primary verb (properly, threcho, cf [G2359](G2359)), which uses dremo drem’-o (the base of [G1408](G1408)) as alternate in certain tenses

d: **1.** thirty
s: The decade of [G5140](G5140); *thirty:* - thirty.

d: **1.** three hundred
s: Plural from [G5140](G5140) and [G1540](G1540); *three* *hundred:* - three hundred.

d: **1.** a thistle, a prickly wild plant, hurtful to other plants
s: From [G5140](G5140) and [G956](G956); properly a *crow* *foot* (*three* *pronged* obstruction in war), that is, (by analogy) a *thorny* plant (*caltrop*): - brier, thistle.

d: **1.** a worn way, a path
s: From τρίβω tribō (to “rub”; akin to τείρω teirō, τρύω truō, and the base of [G5131](G5131), [G5134](G5134)); a *rut* or worn *track:* - path.
o: from tribo (to rub, akin to teiro, truo, and the base of [G5131](G5131), [G5134](G5134))

d: **1.** a space of three years
s: From a compound of [G5140](G5140) and [G2094](G2094); a *three* *years’* *period* (*triennium*): - space of three years.

d:
**1.** to squeak, make a shrill cry
**2.** to gnash or grind one’s teeth
s: Apparently a primary verb; to *creak* (*squeak*), that is, (by analogy) to *grate* the teeth (in frenzy): - gnash.

d:
**1.** of three months
**2.** a space of three months
s: Neuter of a compound of [G5140](G5140) and [G3376](G3376) as noun; a *three* *months’* space: - three months.
o: neuter of a compound of [G5140](G5140) and [G3376](G3376) as noun

d: **1.** thrice
s: Adverb from [G5140](G5140); *three* *times:* - three times, thrice.

d: **1.** having three roofs or stories, the third story
s: Neuter of a compound of [G5140](G5140) and [G4721](G4721) as noun; a *third* *roof* (*story*): - third loft.
o: neuter of a compound of [G5140](G5140) and [G4721](G4721) as noun

d: **1.** three thousand
s: From [G5151](G5151) and [G5507](G5507); *three* *times* *a* *thousand:* - three thousand.

d: **1.** the third
s: From [G5140](G5140); *third*; neuter (as noun) a *third* *part*, or (as adverb) a (or the) *third* time, *thirdly:* - third (-ly).

d: **1.** made of hair
s: From [G2359](G2359); *hairy*, that is, made *of* *hair* (*mohair*): - of hair.

d:
**1.** a trembling or quaking with fear
**2.** with fear and trembling, used to describe the anxiety of one who distrusts his ability completely to meet all requirements, but religiously does his utmost to fulfil his duty
s: From [G5141](G5141); a “trembling”, that is, quaking with *fear:* - + tremble (-ing).

d:
**1.** a turning
  **a.** of the heavenly bodies
s: From an apparently primary word τρέπω trepō (to *turn*); a *turn* (“trope”), that is, *revolution* (figuratively *variation*): - turning.
o: from an apparently primary trepo to turn

d:
**1.** a manner, way, fashion
  **a.** as, even as, like as
**2.** manner of life, character, deportment
s: From the same as [G5157](G5157); a *turn*, that is, (by implication) *mode* or *style* (especially with preposition or relatively prefixed as adverb *like*); figuratively *deportment* or *character:* - (even) as, conversation, \[+ like\] manner (+ by any) means, way.

d: **1.** to bear one’s manner, endure one’s character
s: From [G5158](G5158) and [G5409](G5409); to *endure* one’s *habits:* - suffer the manners.

d: **1.** food, nourishment
s: From [G5142](G5142); *nourishment* (literally or figuratively); by implication *rations* (*wages*): - food, meat.

d:
Trophimus = nutritious
**1.** an Ephesian Christian, and friend of the apostle Paul
s: From [G5160](G5160); *nutritive*; *Trophimus*, a Christian: - Trophimus.

d: **1.** a nurse
s: From [G5142](G5142); a *nourisher*, that is, *nurse:* - nurse.

d:
**1.** a track of a wheel, a rut
**2.** a track, a path
s: From [G5164](G5164); a *track* (as a wheel *rut*), that is, (figuratively) a *course* of conduct: - path.

d: **1.** a wheel
s: From [G5143](G5143); a *wheel* (as a *runner*), that is, (figuratively) a *circuit* of physical effects: - course.

d: **1.** a dish, a deep dish
s: Neuter of a presumed derivation of uncertain affinity; a *bowl:* - dish.
o: from a presumed derivative of uncertain affinity

d:
**1.** to gather in ripe fruits
**2.** to gather the harvest or vintage
  **a.** of fruit gathered
s: From a derivative of τρύγω trugō (to *dry*) meaning ripe *fruit* (as if *dry*); to *collect* the vintage: - gather.
o: from a derivative of trugo (to dry) meaning ripe fruit (as if dry)

d: **1.** turtledove
s: From τρύζω truzō (to *murmur*; akin to [G5149](G5149), but denoting a *duller* sound); a *turtle* *dove* (as *cooing*): - turtle-dove.
o: from truzo (to murmur; akin to [G5149](G5149), but denoting a duller sound)

d: **1.** a hole, (eye of the needle)
s: From a derivative of τρύώ truō (to *wear* away; akin to the base of [G5134](G5134), [G5147](G5147) and [G5176](G5176)); an *orifice*, that is, a needle’s *eye*: - eye. Compare [G5169](G5169).
o: from a derivative of truo (to wear away, akin to the base of [G5134](G5134), [G5147](G5147) and [G5176](G5176))

d: **1.** a hole, (eye of the needle)
s: From a derivative of the base of [G5168](G5168); an *aperture*, that is, a needle’s *eye:* - eye.
o: from a derivative of the base of [G5168](G5168)

d:
Tryphena = luxurious
**1.** a Christian woman
s: From [G5172](G5172); *luxurious*; *Tryphaena*, a Christian woman: - Tryphena.

d: **1.** to live delicately, live luxuriously, be given to soft and luxurious life
s: From [G5172](G5172); to *indulge* *in* *luxury:* - live in pleasure.

d: **1.** softness, effeminate, luxurious living
s: From θρύπτω thruptō̄ (to *break* up or \[figuratively\] *enfeeble*, especially the mind and body by indulgence); *effeminacy*, that is, *luxury* or *debauchery:* - delicately, riot.
o: from thrupto (to break up or \[figuratively\] enfeeble, especially the mind and body by indulgence)

d:
Tryphosa = luxuriating
**1.** a Christian woman
s: From [G5172](G5172); *luxuriating*; *Tryphosa*, a Christian female: - Tryphosa.

d:
Troas = a Trojan
**1.** a city near hellespont
s: From Τρός Tros (a *Trojan*); the *Troad* (or plain of Troy), that is, *Troas*, a place in Asia Minor: - Troas.

d:
Trogyllium = a cache
**1.** the name of a town and a promontory of Ionia, not far from the island of Samos, at the foot of Mt. Mycale between Ephesus and the mouth of the river Maeander
s: Of uncertain derivation; *Trogyllium*, a place in Asia Minor: - Trogyllium.

d:
**1.** to gnaw, crunch, chew raw vegetables or fruits (as nuts, almonds)
  **a.** of animals feeding
  **b.** of men
**2.** to eat
s: Probably strengthened from a collateral form of the base of [G5134](G5134) and [G5147](G5147) through the idea of *corrosion* or *wear*; or perhaps rather of a base of [G5167](G5167) and [G5149](G5149) through the idea of a *craunching* sound; to *gnaw* or *chew*, that is, (genitive case) to *eat:* - eat.
o: probably strengthened from a collateral form of the base of [G5134](G5134) and [G5147](G5147) through the idea of corrosion or wear, or perhaps rather of a base of [G5167](G5167) and [G5149](G5149) through the idea of a crunching sound

d:
**1.** to hit the mark
  **a.** of one discharging a javelin or arrow
**2.** to reach, attain, obtain, get, become master of
**3.** to happen, chance, fall out
  **a.** to specify, to take a case, as for example
**4.** to meet one
**5.** of he who meets one or presents himself unsought, any chance, ordinary, common person
**6.** to chance to be
s: Probably for an obsolete τύχω tuchō (for which the middle voice of another alternate τεύχω teuchō \[to *make* *ready* or *bring* *to* *pass*\] is used in certain tenses; akin to the base of [G5088](G5088) through the idea of *effecting*; properly to *affect*; or (specifically) to *hit* or *light* *upon* (as a mark to be reached), that is, (transitively) to *attain* or *secure* an object or end, or (intransitively) to *happen* (as if *meeting* with); but in the latter application only impersonally (with [G1487](G1487)), that is, *perchance*; or (present participle) as adjective *usual* (as if commonly *met* *with*, with [G3756](G3756), *extraordinary*), neuter (as adverb) *perhaps*; or (with another verb) as adverb by *accident* (*as* *it* *were*): - be, chance, enjoy, little, obtain, X refresh . . . self, + special. Compare [G5180](G5180).
o: probably for an obsolete tucho (for which the middle voice of another alternate teucho \[to make ready or bring to pass\] is used in certain tenses, akin to the base of [G5088](G5088) through the idea of effecting

d:
**1.** to beat the drum or timbrel
**2.** to torture with the tympanum, an instrument of punishment
s: From a derivative of [G5180](G5180) (meaning a *drum*, “tympanum”); to stretch on an instrument of *torture* resembling a drum, and thus *beat* to death: - torture.
o: from a derivative of [G5180](G5180) (meaning a drum, tympanum)

d:
**1.** the mark of a stroke or blow, print
**2.** a figure formed by a blow or impression
  **a.** of a figure or image
  **b.** of the image of the Gods
**3.** form
  **a.** the teaching which embodies the sum and substance of religion and represents it to the mind, manner of writing, the contents and form of a letter
**4.** an example
  **a.** in the technical sense, the pattern in conformity to which a thing must be made
  **b.** in an ethical sense, a dissuasive example, a pattern of warning
    **1.** of ruinous events which serve as admonitions or warnings to others
  **c.** an example to be imitated
    **1.** of men worthy of imitation
  **d.** in a doctrinal sense
    **1.** of a type i.e. a person or thing prefiguring a future (Messianic) person or thing
s: From [G5180](G5180); a *die* (as *struck*), that is, (by implication) a *stamp* or *scar*; by analogy a *shape*, that is, a *statue*, (figuratively) *style* or *resemblance*; specifically a *sampler* (“type”), that is, a *model* (for imitation) or *instance* (for warning): - en- (ex-) ample, fashion, figure, form, manner, pattern, print.

d:
**1.** to strike, beat, smite
  **a.** with a staff, a whip, the fist, the hand
  **b.** of mourners, to smite their breast
**2.** to smite one on whom he inflicts punitive evil
**3.** to smite
  **a.** metaph. i.e. to wound, disquiet one’s conscience
s: A primary verb (in a strengthened form); to “thump”, that is, *cudgel* or *pummel* (properly with a stick or *bastinado*), but in any case by *repeated* blows; thus differing from [G3817](G3817) and [G3960](G3960), which denote a \[usually single\] blow with the hand or any instrument, or [G4141](G4141) with the *fist* \[or a *hammer*\], or [G4474](G4474) with the *palm*; as well as from [G5177](G5177), an *accidental* collision); by implication to *punish*; figuratively to *offend* (the conscience): - beat, smite, strike, wound.
o: a primary verb (in a strengthened form)

d:
Tyrannus = sovereign
**1.** an Ephesian in whose school Paul taught the gospel
s: A provincial form of the derivative of the base of [G2962](G2962); a “tyrant”; *Tyrannus*, an Ephesian: - Tyrannus.
o: a provincial form of the derivative of the base of [G2962](G2962)

d:
**1.** disturb, trouble
**2.** to be troubled in mind, disquieted
s: From τύρβη turbē̄ (Latin *turba*, a *crowd*; akin to [G2351](G2351)); to *make* “turbid”, that is, *disturb:* - trouble.
o: from turbe (Latin turba, a crowd, akin to [G2351](G2351))

d: **1.** a resident of Tyre
s: From [G5184](G5184); a *Tyrian*, that is, inhabitant of Tyrus: - of Tyre.

d:
Tyre = a rock
**1.** a Phoenician city on the mediterranean, very ancient, large, splendid, flourishing in commerce, and powerful by land and sea
s: Of Hebrew origin \[[H6865](H6865)\]; *Tyrus* (that is, *Tsor*), a place in Palestine: - Tyre.

d:
**1.** blind
**2.** mentally blind
s: From [G5187](G5187); *opaque* (as if *smoky*), that is, (by analogy) *blind* (physically or mentally): - blind.

d:
**1.** to blind, make blind
**2.** in the NT metaph. to blunt the mental discernment, darken the mind
s: From [G5185](G5185); to *make* *blind*, that is, (figuratively) to *obscure:* - blind.

d:
**1.** to raise a smoke, to wrap in a mist
  **a.** metaph.
    **1.** to make proud, puff up with pride, render insolent
    **2.** to be puffed up with haughtiness or pride
**2.** to blind with pride or conceit, to render foolish or stupid
  **a.** beclouded, besotted
s: From a derivative of [G5188](G5188); to envelop with *smoke*, that is, (figuratively) to *inflate* with self conceit: - high-minded, be lifted up with pride, be proud.

d:
**1.** to cause or emit smoke, raise a smoke
**2.** to smoke
s: Apparently a primary verb; to make a *smoke*, that is, slowly *consume* without flame: - smoke.

d: **1.** like a whirlwind, tempestuous
s: From a derivative of [G5188](G5188); *stormy* (as if *smoky*): - tempestuous.

d:
Tychicus = fateful
**1.** an Asiatic Christian, friend and companion of the apostle Paul
s: From a derivative of [G5177](G5177); *fortuitous*, that is, *fortunate*; *Tychicus*, a Christian: - Tychicus.

d:
**1.** hyacinth, of the colour of hyacinth
  **a.** of a red colour bordering on black
s: From [G5192](G5192); “hyacinthine” or “jacinthine”, that is, deep *blue:* - jacinth.

d: **1.** hyacinth, the name of a flower, also of a precious stone of the same colour, a dark blue verging on black
s: Of uncertain derivation; the “hyacinth” or “jacinth”, that is, some gem of a deep *blue* color, probably the *zirkon:* - jacinth.

d: **1.** of glass or transparent like glass, glassy
s: From [G5194](G5194); *glassy*, that is, *transparent:* - of glass.

d:
**1.** any stone transparent like glass
**2.** glass
s: Perhaps from the same as [G5205](G5205) (as being transparent like *rain*); *glass:* - glass.
o: perhaps from the same as [G5205](G5205) (as being transparent like rain)

d:
**1.** to be insolent, to behave insolently, wantonly, outrageously
**2.** to act insolently and shamefully towards one, to treat shamefully
**3.** of one who injures another by speaking evil of him
s: From [G5196](G5196); to *exercise* *violence*, that is, *abuse:* - use despitefully, reproach, entreat shamefully (spitefully).

d:
**1.** insolence
  **a.** impudence, pride, haughtiness
**2.** a wrong springing from insolence, an injury, affront, insult
**3.** mental injury and wantonness of its infliction being prominent
**4.** injury inflicted by the violence of a tempest
s: From [G5228](G5228); *insolence* (as *over* bearing), that is, *insult*, *injury:* - harm, hurt, reproach.

d:
**1.** an insolent man
**2.** one who, uplifted with pride, either heaps insulting language upon others or does them some shameful act of wrong
s: From [G5195](G5195); an *insulter*, that is, *maltreater:* - de-spiteful, injurious.

d:
**1.** to be sound, to be well, to be in good health
**2.** metaph.
  **a.** of Christians whose opinions are free from any mixture of error
  **b.** of one who keeps the graces and is strong
s: From [G5199](G5199); to *have* sound *health*, that is, *be* *well* (in body); figuratively to be *uncorrupt* (*true* in doctrine): - be in health, (be safe and) sound, (be) whole (-some).

d:
**1.** sound
  **a.** of a man who is sound in body
**2.** to make one whole i.e. restore him to health
**3.** metaph. teaching which does not deviate from the truth
s: From the base of [G837](G837); *healthy*, that is, *well* (in body); figuratively *true* (in doctrine): - sound, whole.

d:
**1.** damp, moist, wet
**2.** full of sap, green
s: From the base of [G5205](G5205); *wet* (as if with *rain*), that is, (by implication) *sappy* (*fresh*): - green.

d:
**1.** a vessel for holding water
**2.** a water jar, a water pot
s: From [G5204](G5204); a *water* *jar*, that is, *receptacle* for family supply: - waterpot.

d: **1.** to drink water, be a drinker of water
s: From a compound of [G5204](G5204) and a derivative of [G4095](G4095); to *be* a *water* *drinker*, that is, to *abstain* *from* *vinous* *beverages:* - drink water.
o: from a compound of [G5204](G5204) and a derivative of [G4095](G4095)

d: **1.** dropsical, suffering from dropsy
s: From a compound of [G5204](G5204) and a derivative of [G3700](G3700) (as if *looking* *watery*); to *be* “dropsical”: - have the dropsy.
o: from a compound of [G5204](G5204) and a derivative of [G3700](G3700) (as if looking watery)

d:
**1.** water
  **a.** of water in rivers, in fountains, in pools
  **b.** of the water of the deluge
  **c.** of water in any of the earth’s repositories
  **d.** of water as the primary element, out of and through which the world that was before the deluge, arose and was compacted
  **e.** of the waves of the sea
  **f.** fig. used of many peoples
s: From the base of [G5205](G5205); *water* (as if *rainy*) literally or figuratively: - water.
o: genitive case, hudatos hoo’-dat-os, etc., from the base of [G5205](G5205)

d: **1.** rain
s: From a primary word ὕω huō (to *rain*); *rain*, especially a *shower:* - rain.

d:
**1.** adoption, adoption as sons
  **a.** that relationship which God was pleased to establish between himself and the Israelites in preference to all other nations
  **b.** the nature and condition of the true disciples in christ, who by receiving the spirit of God into their souls become sons of God
  **c.** the blessed state looked for in the future life after the visible return of christ from heaven
s: From a presumed compound of [G5207](G5207) and a derivative of [G5087](G5087); the *placing* as a *son*, that is, *adoption* (figuratively Christian *sonship* in respect to God): - adoption (of children, of sons).
o: from a presumed compound of [G5207](G5207) and a derivative of [G5087](G5087)

d:
**1.** a son
  **a.** rarely used for the young of animals
  **b.** generally used of the offspring of men
  **c.** in a restricted sense, the male offspring (one born by a father and of a mother)
  **d.** in a wider sense, a descendant, one of the posterity of any one,
    **1.** the children of Israel
    **2.** sons of Abraham
  **e.** used to describe one who depends on another or is his follower
    **1.** a pupil
**2.** son of man
  **a.** term describing man, carrying the connotation of weakness and mortality
  **b.** son of man, symbolically denotes the fifth kingdom in Dan 7:13 and by this term its humanity is indicated in contrast with the barbarity and ferocity of the four preceding kingdoms (the Babylonian, the median and the Persian, the Macedonian, and the Roman) typified by the four beasts. In the book of Enoch (2nd Century) it is used of christ.
  **c.** used by christ himself, doubtless in order that he might intimate his messiahship and also that he might designate himself as the head of the human family, the man, the one who both furnished the pattern of the perfect man and acted on behalf of all mankind. christ seems to have preferred this to the other messianic titles, because by its lowliness it was least suited to foster the expectation of an earthly messiah in royal splendour.
**3.** son of God
  **a.** used to describe Adam (Luk 3:38)
  **b.** used to describe those who are born again (Luk 20:36)
  **c.** and of angels and of Jesus christ
**4.** of those whom God esteems as sons, whom he loves, protects and benefits above others
  **a.** in the OT used of the Jews
  **b.** in the NT of Christians
  **c.** those whose character God, as a loving father, shapes by chastisements (Heb 12:5-13)
  **d.** those who revere God as their father, the pious worshippers of God, those who in character and life resemble God, those who are governed by the spirit of God, repose the same calm and joyful trust in God which children do in their parents (Rom 8:14, Gal 3:26 ), and hereafter in the blessedness and glory of the life eternal will openly wear this dignity of the sons of God. Term used preeminently of Jesus christ, as enjoying the supreme love of God, united to him in affectionate intimacy, privy to his saving councils, obedient to the father’s will in all his acts
s: Apparently a primary word; a “son” (sometimes of animals), used very widely of immediate, remote or figurative kinship: - child, foal, son.

d:
**1.** a forest, a wood
**2.** felled wood, fuel
s: Perhaps akin to [G3586](G3586); a *forest*, that is, (by implication) *fuel:* - matter.
Accusative of [G5210](G5210); *you* (as the object of a verb or preposition): - ye, you, (+ -ward), your (+ own).
Irregular plural of [G4771](G4771); *you* (as subject of verb): - ye (yourselves), you.

d:
Hymenaeus = belonging to marriage
**1.** a heretic, one of the opponents of the apostle Paul
s: From Ὑμήν Humēn (the god of *weddings*); “hymenaeal”; *Hymenaeus*, an opponent of Christianity: - Hymenus.

d:
**1.** you, yours
  **a.** to be possessed by you
  **b.** to be allocated by you
  **c.** proceeding from you
s: From [G5210](G5210); *yours*, that is, *pertaining* *to* *you:* - your (own).
Irregular dative case of [G5210](G5210); *to* (*with* or *by*) *you:* - ye, you, your (-selves).

d:
**1.** to sing the praise of, sing hymns to
**2.** to sing a hymn, to sing
  **a.** singing of paschal hymns these were Psalms 113 - 118 and 136, which the Jews called the great Hallel
s: From [G5215](G5215); to *hymn*, that is, sing a religious ode; by implication to *celebrate* (God) in song: - sing an hymn (praise unto).

d:
**1.** a song in tithe praise of Gods, heroes, conquerors
**2.** a sacred song, hymn
s: Apparently from a simpler (obsolete) form of ὕδέω hudeō (to *celebrate*; probably akin to [G103](G103); compare [G5567](G5567)); a “hymn” or religious ode (one of the Psalms): - hymn.
o: apparently from a simpler (obsolete) form of hudeo (to celebrate, probably akin to [G103](G103), cf [G5667](G5667))

d: **1.** of yours
s: Genitive case of [G5210](G5210); *of* (*from* or *concerning*) *you:* - ye, you, your (own, -selves).

d:
**1.** to lead under, bring under
**2.** to withdraw one’s self, to go away, depart
s: From [G5259](G5259) and [G71](G71); to *lead* (oneself) *under*, that is, *withdraw* or *retire* (as if *sinking* out of sight), literally or figuratively: - depart, get hence, go (a-) way.

d:
**1.** obedience, compliance, submission
**2.** obedience rendered to anyone’s counsels, an obedience shown in observing the requirements of Christianity
s: From [G5219](G5219); *attentive* *hearkening*, that is, (by implication) *compliance* or *submission:* - obedience, (make) obedient, obey (-ing).

d:
**1.** to listen, to harken
  **a.** of one who on the knock at the door comes to listen who it is, (the duty of a porter)
**2.** to harken to a command
  **a.** to obey, be obedient to, submit to
s: From [G5259](G5259) and [G191](G191); to *hear* *under* (as a *subordinate*), that is, to *listen* *attentively*; by implication to *heed* or *conform* to a command or authority: - hearken, be obedient to, obey.

d: **1.** under i.e. subject to a man: married
s: From [G5259](G5259) and [G435](G435); in subjection *under* *a* *man*, that is, a *married* woman: - which hath an husband.

d:
**1.** to go to meet, to meet
**2.** in military reference
  **a.** of a hostile meeting
s: From [G5259](G5259) and a derivative of [G473](G473); to *go* *opposite* (*meet*) *under* (*quietly*), that is, to *encounter*, *fall* *in* *with:* - (go to) meet.

d: **1.** to go to meet
s: From [G5221](G5221); an *encounter* or *concurrence* (with [G1519](G1519) for infinitive, in order to *fall* *in* *with*): - meeting.

d: **1.** possessions, goods, wealth, property
s: From [G5225](G5225); *existency* or *proprietorship*, that is, (concretely) *property*, *wealth:* - goods, substance.

d: **1.** possessions, goods, wealth, property
s: Neuter plural of present participle active of [G5225](G5225) as noun; things *extant* or *in* *hand*, that is, *property* or *possessions:* - goods, that which one has, things which (one) possesseth, substance, that hast.
o: neuter plural of present participle active of [G5225](G5225) as noun

d:
**1.** to begin below, to make a beginning
  **a.** to begin
**2.** to come forth, hence to be there, be ready, be at hand
**3.** to be
s: From [G5259](G5259) and [G756](G756); to *begin* *under* (*quietly*), that is, *come* *into* *existence* (*be* *present* or *at* *hand*); expletively, to *exist* (as copula or subordinate to an adjective, participle, adverb or preposition, or as auxilliary to principal verb): - after behave, live.

d:
**1.** to resist no longer, but to give way, yield (of combatants)
**2.** metaph. to yield to authority and admonition, to submit
s: From [G5259](G5259) and εἴκω eikō (to *yield*, be “weak”); to *surrender:* - submit self.
o: from [G5259](G5259) and eiko (to yield, be weak)

d:
**1.** opposite to
  **a.** set over against: meeting one another
**2.** opposed to, contrary to, an adversary
s: From [G5259](G5259) and [G1727](G1727); *under* (*covertly*) *contrary* to, that is, *opposed* or (as noun) an *opponent:* - adversary, against.

d:
**1.** in behalf of, for the sake of
**2.** over, beyond, more than
**3.** more, beyond, over
s: A primary preposition; “over”, that is, (with the genitive case) of place, *above*, *beyond*, *across*, or causal, *for* the sake of, *instead*, *regarding*; with the accusative case *superior* *to*, more *than*. In compounds it retains many of the listed applications: - (+ exceeding abundantly) above, in (on) behalf of, beyond, by, + very chiefest, concerning, exceeding (above, -ly), for, + very highly, more (than), of, over, on the part of, for sake of, in stead, than, to (-ward), very. In compounds it retains many of the above applications.

d:
**1.** to lift or raise up over some thing
**2.** to lift one’s self up, be exalted, be haughty
**3.** to carry one’s self haughtily to, behave insolently towards one
s: Middle voice from [G5228](G5228) and [G142](G142); to *raise* oneself *over*, that is, (figuratively) to *become* *haughty:* - exalt self, be exalted above measure.

d:
**1.** beyond the bloom or prime of life
**2.** overripe, plump and ripe, (and so in a greater danger of defilement)
  **a.** of a virgin
s: From [G5228](G5228) and the base of [G188](G188); *beyond* the “acme”, that is, figuratively (of a daughter) *past* the *bloom* (*prime*) of youth: - + pass the flower of (her) age.

d:
**1.** above
  **a.** above a thing
  **b.** of a place
  **c.** of rank or power
s: From [G5228](G5228) and [G507](G507); *above* *upward*, that is, *greatly* *higher* (in place or rank): - far above, over.

d:
**1.** to increase beyond measure
**2.** to grow exceedingly
s: From [G5228](G5228) and [G837](G837); to *increase* *above* ordinary degree: - grow exceedingly.

d:
**1.** to step over, beyond
**2.** metaph.
  **a.** to transgress
  **b.** to overstep the proper limits
  **c.** trespass, do wrong, sin
    **1.** of one who defrauds another in business
  **d.** overreaches
s: From [G5228](G5228) and the base of [G939](G939); to *transcend*; that is, (figuratively) to *overreach:* - go beyond.

d: **1.** above measure
s: Adverb from present participle active of [G5235](G5235); *excessively:* - beyond measure.

d:
**1.** to surpass in throwing, to throw over or beyond any thing
**2.** to transcend, surpass, exceed, excel
**3.** excelling, exceeding
s: From [G5228](G5228) and [G906](G906); to *throw* *beyond* the usual mark, that is, (figuratively) to *surpass* (only active participle *supereminent*): - exceeding, excel, pass.

d:
**1.** a throwing beyond
**2.** metaph.
  **a.** superiority, excellence, pre-eminence
  **b.** beyond measure, exceedingly, preeminently
  **c.** beyond all measure
s: From [G5235](G5235); a *throwing* *beyond* others, that is, (figuratively) *supereminence*; adverbially (with [G1519](G1519) or [G2596](G2596)) *pre-eminently:* - abundance, (far more) exceeding, excellency, more excellent, beyond (out of) measure.

d: **1.** to overlook, take no notice of, not attend to
s: From [G5228](G5228) and [G1492](G1492); to *overlook*, that is, *not* *punish:* - wink at.

d: **1.** beyond: the regions lying beyond the country of one’s residence
s: From [G5228](G5228) and the neuter plural of [G1565](G1565); *above* *those* parts, that is, *still* *farther:* - beyond.
o: from [G5228](G5228) and the neuter plural of [G1565](G1565)

d: **1.** to extend beyond the prescribed bounds, stretch out beyond measure, stretch out overmuch
s: From [G5228](G5228) and [G1614](G1614); to *extend* *inordinately:* - stretch beyond.

d:
**1.** to pour out beyond measure
**2.** to overflow, run over
s: From [G5228](G5228) and the alternate form of [G1632](G1632); to *pour* *out* *over*, that is, (passively) to *overflow:* - run over.
o: from [G5228](G5228) and the alternate form of [G1632](G1632)

d: **1.** to intercede for one
s: From [G5228](G5228) and [G1793](G1793); to *intercede* *in* *behalf* *of:* - make intercession for.

d:
**1.** to have or hold over one
**2.** to stand out, rise above, overtop
  **a.** to be above, be superior in rank, authority, power
    **1.** the prominent men, rulers
  **b.** to excel, to be superior, better than, to surpass
s: From [G5228](G5228) and [G2192](G2192); to *hold* oneself *above*, that is, (figuratively) to *excel*; participle (as adjective, or neuter as noun) *superior*, *superiority:* - better, excellency, higher, pass, supreme.

d:
**1.** pride, haughtiness, arrogance
**2.** the character of one who, with a swollen estimate of his own powers or merits, looks down on others and even treats them with insolence and contempt
s: From [G5244](G5244); *haughtiness:* - pride.

d:
**1.** showing one’s self above others, overtopping, conspicuous above others, pre-eminent
**2.** with an overweening estimate of one’s means or merits, despising others or even treating them with contempt, haughty
s: From [G5228](G5228) and [G5316](G5316); *appearing* *above* others (*conspicuous*), that is, (figuratively) *haughty:* - proud.

d: **1.** to be more than a conqueror, to gain a surpassing victory
s: From [G5228](G5228) and [G3528](G3528); to *vanquish* *beyond*, that is, *gain* a decisive *victory:* - more than conquer.

d:
**1.** overswollen
**2.** metaph. immoderate, extravagant
s: From [G5228](G5228) and [G3591](G3591); *bulging* *over*, that is, (figuratively) *insolent:* - great swelling.

d:
**1.** elevation, pre-eminence, superiority
**2.** metaph. excellence
s: From [G5242](G5242); *prominence*, that is, (figuratively) *superiority* (in rank or character): - authority, excellency.

d:
**1.** to abound beyond measure, abound exceedingly
**2.** to overflow, to enjoy abundantly
s: From [G5228](G5228) and [G4052](G4052); to *super* *abound:* - abound much more, exceeding.

d: **1.** beyond measure, exceedingly
s: From [G5228](G5228) and [G4057](G4057); *superabundantly*, that is, *exceedingly:* - beyond measure.

d:
**1.** to be exceedingly abundant
**2.** to overflow
**3.** to possess in excess
s: From [G5228](G5228) and [G4121](G4121); to *super* *abound:* - be exceeding abundant.

d:
**1.** metaph. to exalt to the highest rank and power, raise to supreme majesty
**2.** to extol most highly
**3.** to be lifted up with pride, exalted beyond measure
**4.** to carry one’s self loftily
s: From [G5228](G5228) and [G5312](G5312); to *elevate* *above* others, that is, *raise* to the *highest* position: - highly exalt.

d: **1.** to think more highly of one’s self than is proper
s: From [G5228](G5228) and [G5426](G5426); to *esteem* oneself *overmuch*, that is, *be* *vain* or *arrogant:* - think more highly.

d:
**1.** the highest part of the house, the upper rooms or story where the women resided
**2.** a room in the upper part of a house, sometimes built upon the flat roof of the house, whither Orientals were wont to retire in order to sup, meditate, pray
s: Neuter of a derivative of [G5228](G5228); a *higher* part of the house, that is, apartment in the *third* *story:* - upper chamber (room).

d:
**1.** to hold under, to put under, place underneath
**2.** metaph. to sustain, undergo
  **a.** suffer punishment
s: From [G5259](G5259) and [G2192](G2192); to *hold* oneself *under*, that is, *endure* with patience: - suffer.

d: **1.** giving ear, obedient
s: From [G5219](G5219); *attentively* *listening*, that is, (by implication) *submissive:* - obedient.

d:
**1.** to act as a rower, to row
**2.** to minister, render services
s: From [G5257](G5257); to *be* *a* *subordinate*, that is, (by implication) *subserve:* - minister (unto), serve.

d:
**1.** servant
  **a.** an underrower, subordinate rower
  **b.** any one who serves with hands: a servant
    **1.** in the NT of the officers and attendants of magistrates as -- of the officer who executes penalties
    **2.** of the attendants of a king, servants, retinue, the soldiers of a king, of the attendant of a synagogue
    **3.** of any one ministering or rendering service
  **c.** any one who aids another in any work
    **1.** an assistant
    **2.** of the preacher of the gospel
s: From [G5259](G5259) and a derivative of ἐρέσσω eressō (to *row*); an *under* *oarsman*, that is, (genitive case) *subordinate* (*assistant*, *sexton*, *constable*): - minister, officer, servant.
o: from [G5259](G5259) and a derivative of eresso (to row)

d: **1.** sleep
s: From an obsolete primary (perhaps akin to [G5259](G5259) through the idea of *subsilience*); *sleep*, that is, (figuratively) spiritual *torpor:* - sleep.
o: from an obsolete primary (perhaps akin to [G5259](G5259) through the idea of subsilience)

d: **1.** by, under
s: A primary preposition; *under*, that is, (with the genitive) of place (*beneath*), or with verbs (the agency or means, *through*); (with the accusative) of place (whither \[*underneath*\] or where \[*below*\]) or time (when \[*at*\])*:* - among, by, from, in, of, under, with. In compounds it retains the same genitive applications, especially of *inferior* position or condition, and specifically *covertly* or *moderately*.

d:
**1.** to throw or put under
**2.** to suggest to the mind
**3.** to instruct privately, instigate, to bribe or induce (someone) unlawfully or secretly to perform some misdeed or commit a crime
**4.** to induce (a person esp. a witness) to give false testimony
s: From [G5259](G5259) and [G906](G906); to *throw* in *stealthily*, that is, *introduce* by collusion: - suborn.

d:
**1.** a writing copy, including all the letters of the alphabet, given to beginners as an aid in learning to draw them
**2.** an example set before one
s: From a compound of [G5259](G5259) and [G1125](G1125); an *underwriting*, that is, *copy* for imitation (figuratively): - example.

d:
**1.** a sign suggestive of anything, delineation of a thing, representation, figure, copy
**2.** an example: for imitation
  **a.** of the thing to be imitated
  **b.** for a warning, of a thing to be shunned
s: From [G5263](G5263); an *exhibit* for imitation or warning (figuratively *specimen*, *adumbration*): - en- (ex-) ample, pattern.

d:
**1.** to show by placing under (i.e. before) the eyes
**2.** to show by words and arguments, i.e. to teach
**3.** to show by make known future things
s: From [G5259](G5259) and [G1166](G1166); to *exhibit* *under* the eyes, (figuratively) to *exemplify* (*instruct*, *admonish*): - show, (fore-) warn.

d: **1.** to receive as a guest
s: From [G5259](G5259) and [G1209](G1209); to *admit* *under* one’s roof, that is, *entertain* hospitably: - receive.

d:
**1.** to underbind
**2.** to bind under one’s self, bind on
s: From [G5259](G5259) and [G1210](G1210); to *bind* *under* one’s feet, that is, *put* *on* shoes or sandals: - bind on, (be) shod.

d: **1.** what is bound under, a sandal, a sole fastened to the foot with thongs
s: From [G5265](G5265); something *bound* *under* the feet, that is, a *shoe* or *sandal:* - shoe.

d:
**1.** under judgment, one who lost his suit
**2.** debtor to one, owing satisfaction to
  **a.** of liable to punishment from God
s: From [G5259](G5259) and [G1349](G1349); *under* *sentence*, that is, (by implication) *condemned:* - guilty.

d:
**1.** under the yoke
**2.** a beast of burden, an ass
  **a.** the ass was the common animal used by the Orientals on journey and for carrying burdens
s: Neuter of a compound of [G5259](G5259) and [G2218](G2218); an animal *under* the *yoke* (*draught* *beast*), that is, (specifically) a *donkey:* - ass.
o: neuter of a compound of [G5259](G5259) and [G2218](G2218)

d:
**1.** to undergird
  **a.** to bind a ship together laterally: i.e. with girths or cables, to enable it to survive the force of waves and tempest
s: From [G5259](G5259) and [G2224](G2224); to *gird* *under*, that is, *frap* (a vessel with cables across the keel, sides and deck): - undergirt.

d: **1.** under, underneath
s: From [G5259](G5259) and [G2736](G2736); *down* *under*, that is, *beneath:* - under.

d:
**1.** to take up another’s statements in reference to what one has decided for one’s self
  **a.** to reply, answer
**2.** to make answer (speak) on the stage
  **a.** to impersonate anyone, play a part
**3.** to simulate, feign, pretend
s: Middle voice from [G5259](G5259) and [G2919](G2919); to *decide* (*speak* or *act*) *under* a false part, that is, (figuratively) *dissemble* (*pretend*): - feign.

d:
**1.** an answering
**2.** an answer
**3.** the acting of a stage player
**4.** dissimulation, hypocrisy
s: From [G5271](G5271); *acting* *under* a feigned part; that is, (figuratively) *deceit* (“hypocrisy”): - condemnation, dissimulation, hypocrisy.

d:
**1.** one who answers, an interpreter
**2.** an actor, stage player
**3.** a dissembler, pretender, hypocrite
s: From [G5271](G5271); an *actor* *under* an assumed character (*stage* *player*), that is, (figuratively) a *dissembler* (“hypocrite”): - hypocrite.

d:
**1.** to take up in order to raise, to bear on high
  **a.** to take up and carry away
**2.** to receive hospitably, welcome
**3.** to take up
  **a.** follow in speech, in order either to reply to or controvert or supplement what another has said
**4.** to take up in the mind
  **a.** to assume, suppose
s: From [G5259](G5259) and [G2983](G2983); to *take* from *below*, that is, *carry* *upward*; figuratively to *take* *up*, that is, *continue* a discourse or topic; mentally to *assume* (*presume*): - answer, receive, suppose.

d:
**1.** to leave behind
**2.** to be left behind, left remaining
  **a.** of a survivor
s: From [G5295](G5295) and [G3007](G3007); to *leave* *under* (*behind*), that is, (passively) to *remain* (*survive*): - be left.

d: **1.** a vessel placed under a press (and in the Orient usually sunk in the earth) to receive the expressed juice of the grapes, a pit
s: Neuter of a presumed compound of [G5259](G5259) and [G3025](G3025); vessel or receptacle *under* the *press*, that is, lower *winevat:* - winefat.
o: from a presumed compound of [G5259](G5259) and [G3025](G3025)

d: **1.** to leave, leave behind
s: A prolonged form for [G5275](G5275); to *leave* *behind*, that is, *bequeath:* - leave.

d:
**1.** to remain
  **a.** to tarry behind
**2.** to remain i.e. abide, not recede or flee
  **a.** to preserve: under misfortunes and trials to hold fast to one’s faith in christ
  **b.** to endure, bear bravely and calmly: ill treatments
s: From [G5259](G5259) and [G3306](G3306); to *stay* *under* (*behind*), that is, *remain*; figuratively to *undergo*, that is, *bear* (trials), *have* *fortitude*, *persevere:* - abide, endure, (take) patient (-ly), suffer, tarry behind.

d:
**1.** to cause one to remember, bring to remembrance, recall to mind: to another
**2.** to put one in remembrance, admonish, of something
**3.** to be reminded, to remember
s: From [G5259](G5259) and [G3403](G3403); to *remind* *quietly*, that is, *suggest* to the (middle voice, one’s own) memory: - put in mind, remember, bring to (put in) remembrance.

d:
**1.** a reminding
**2.** remembrance
s: From [G5279](G5279); a *reminding* or (reflexively) *recollection:* - remembrance.

d:
**1.** steadfastness, constancy, endurance
  **a.** in the NT the characteristic of a man who is not swerved from his deliberate purpose and his loyalty to faith and piety by even the greatest trials and sufferings
  **b.** patiently, and steadfastly
**2.** a patient, steadfast waiting for
**3.** a patient enduring, sustaining, perseverance
s: From [G5278](G5278); cheerful (or hopeful) *endurance*, *constancy:* - enduring, patience, patient continuance (waiting).

d: **1.** to suppose, surmise
s: From [G5259](G5259) and [G3539](G3539); to *think* *under* (*privately*), that is, to *surmise* or *conjecture:* - think, suppose, deem.

d: **1.** a surmising
s: From [G5282](G5282); *suspicion:* - surmising.

d:
**1.** to sail under, that is, to sail close by
**2.** to the leeward of
s: From [G5259](G5259) and [G4126](G4126); to *sail* *under* the lee of: - sail under.

d:
**1.** to blow underneath
**2.** to blow softly
s: From [G5259](G5259) and [G4154](G4154); to *breathe* *gently*, that is, *breeze:* - blow softly.

d:
**1.** a footstool
  **a.** to make one a footstool of one’s feet, i.e. to subject, to reduce under one’s power
  **b.** metaph. taken from the practice of conquerors who placed their feet on the necks of their conquered enemies
s: Neuter of a compound of [G5259](G5259) and [G4228](G4228); something *under* the *feet*, that is, a *footrest* (figuratively): - footstool.

d:
**1.** a setting or placing under
  **a.** thing put under, substructure, foundation
**2.** that which has foundation, is firm
  **a.** that which has actual existence
    **1.** a substance, real being
  **b.** the substantial quality, nature, of a person or thing
  **c.** the steadfastness of mind, firmness, courage, resolution
    **1.** confidence, firm trust, assurance
s: From a compound of [G5259](G5259) and [G2476](G2476); a *setting* *under* (*support*), that is, (figuratively) concretely *essence*, or abstractly *assurance* (objectively or subjectively): - confidence, confident, person, substance.

d:
**1.** to draw back, let down, lower
  **a.** to withdraw: of a timid person
**2.** to withdraw one’s self, i.e. to be timid, to cover, shrink
  **a.** of those who from timidity hesitate to avow what they believe
  **b.** to be unwilling to utter from fear
  **c.** to shrink from declaring, to conceal, dissemble
s: From [G5259](G5259) and [G4724](G4724); to *withhold* *under* (*out* *of* *sight*), that is, (reflexively) to *cower* or *shrink*, (figuratively) to *conceal* (*reserve*): - draw (keep) back, shun, withdraw.

d: **1.** the timidity of one stealthily retreating
s: From [G5288](G5288); *shrinkage* (*timidity*), that is, (by implication) *apostasy:* - draw back.

d:
**1.** to turn back
  **a.** to turn about
**2.** to return
s: From [G5259](G5259) and [G4762](G4762); to *turn* *under* (*behind*), that is, to *return* (literally or figuratively): - come again, return (again, back again), turn back (again).

d: **1.** to strew, spread under
s: From [G5259](G5259) and [G4766](G4766); to *strew* *underneath* (the feet as a carpet): - spread.

d:
**1.** the act of subjecting
**2.** obedience, subjection
s: From [G5293](G5293); *subordination:* - subjection.

d:
**1.** to arrange under, to subordinate
**2.** to subject, put in subjection
**3.** to subject one’s self, obey
**4.** to submit to one’s control
**5.** to yield to one’s admonition or advice
**6.** to obey, be subject A Greek military term meaning to arrange \[troop divisions\] in amilitary fashion under the command of a leader. In non-military use,it was a voluntary attitude of giving in, cooperating, assumingresponsibility, and carrying a burden.
s: From [G5259](G5259) and [G5021](G5021); to *subordinate*; reflexively to *obey:* - be under obedience (obedient), put under, subdue unto, (be, make) subject (to, unto), be (put) in subjection (to, under), submit self unto.

d:
**1.** to place under
**2.** metaph. to supply, suggest (supply from one’s own resources)
s: From [G5259](G5259) and [G5087](G5087); to *place* *underneath*, that is, (figuratively) to *hazard*, (reflexively) to *suggest:* - lay down, put in remembrance.

d:
**1.** to run under
  **a.** of navigators
    **1.** to run past a place on the shore, and therefore in a higher position
    **2.** running under the lee of
s: From [G5259](G5259) and [G5143](G5143) (including its alternate); to *run* *under*, that is, (specifically) to *sail* *past:* - run under.

d:
**1.** an outline, sketch, brief and summary exposition
**2.** an example, pattern
  **a.** for an example of those who should hereafter believe
  **b.** to show by the example of my conversation that the same grace which I had obtained would not be wanting also to those who should hereafter believe
s: From a compound of [G5259](G5259) and a derivative of [G5179](G5179); *typification* *under* (*after*), that is, (concretely) a *sketch* (figuratively) for imitation: - form, pattern.
o: from a compound of [G5259](G5259) and a derivative of [G5179](G5179)

d:
**1.** to bear by being under, bear up (a thing placed on one’s shoulders)
**2.** to bear patiently, to endure
s: From [G5259](G5259) and [G5342](G5342); to *bear* from *underneath*, that is, (figuratively) to *undergo* hardship: - bear, endure.

d:
**1.** to go back
**2.** withdraw
s: From [G5259](G5259) and [G5562](G5562); to *vacate* *down*, that is, *retire* quietly: - go aside, withdraw self.

d:
**1.** to beat black and blue, to smite so as to cause bruises and livid spots
  **a.** like a boxer one buffets his body, handle it roughly, discipline by hardships
**2.** metaph.
  **a.** to give one intolerable annoyance
    **1.** beat one out, wear one out
  **b.** by entreaties
**3.** that part of the face that is under the eyes
s: From a compound of [G5259](G5259) and a derivative of [G3700](G3700); to hit *under* the *eye* (*buffet* or *disable* an antagonist as a pugilist), that is, (figuratively) to *tease* or *annoy* (into compliance), *subdue* (one’s passions): - keep under, weary.
o: from a compound of [G5259](G5259) and a derivative of [G3700](G3700)

d: **1.** swine
s: Apparently a primary word; a *hog* (“swine”): - sow.

d:
**1.** hyssop
**2.** a plant used by the hebrews in their ritual sprinklings
s: Of foreign origin \[[H231](H231)\]; “hyssop”: - hyssop.

d:
**1.** behind
  **a.** to come late or too tardily
    **1.** to be left behind in the race and so fail to reach the goal, to fall short of the end
    **2.** metaph. fail to become a partaker, fall back from
  **b.** to be inferior in power, influence and rank
    **1.** of the person: to be inferior to
  **c.** to fail, be wanting
  **d.** to be in want of, lack
**2.** to suffer want, to be devoid of, to lack (be inferior) in excellence, worth
s: From [G5306](G5306); to *be* *later*, that is, (by implication) to *be* *inferior*; genitively to *fall* *short* (*be* *deficient*): - come behind (short), be destitute, fall, lack, suffer need, (be in) want, be the worse.

d:
**1.** deficiency, that which is lacking
**2.** in reference to property and resources, poverty, want, destitution
s: From [G5302](G5302); a *deficit*; specifically *poverty:* - that which is behind, (that which was) lack (-ing), penury, want.

d: **1.** want, poverty
s: From [G5302](G5302); a *falling* *short*, that is, (specifically) *penury:* - want.

d:
**1.** latter, later, coming after, the second
**2.** afterward, after this, later, lastly
s: Neuter of [G5306](G5306) as adverb; *more* *lately*, that is, *eventually:* - afterward, (at the) last (of all).

d:
**1.** latter, later, coming after, the second
**2.** afterward, after this, later, lastly
s: Comparatively from [G5259](G5259) (in the sense of *behind*); *later:* - latter.
o: comparative from [G5259](G5259) (in the sense of behind)

d: **1.** woven
s: From ὑφαίνω huphainō (to *weave*); *woven*, that is, (perhaps) *knitted:* - woven.

d:
**1.** high, lofty
  **a.** exalted on high
  **b.** with an uplifted arm, i.e. with signal power
**2.** metaph. eminent, exalted
  **a.** in influence and honour
  **b.** to set the mind on, to seek, high things (as honours and riches), to be aspiring
s: From [G5311](G5311); *lofty* (in place or character): - high (-er, -ly) (esteemed).

d: **1.** to be high minded, proud

d: **1.** A sect that seems to have started after the Jewish exile. In addition to OT books the Pharisees recognised in oral tradition a standard of belief and life. They sought for distinction and praise by outward observance of external rites and by outward forms of piety, and such as ceremonial washings, fastings, prayers, and alms giving; and, comparatively negligent of genuine piety, they prided themselves on their fancied good works. They held strenuously to a belief in the existence of good and evil angels, and to the expectation of a messiah; and they cherished the hope that the dead, after a preliminary experience either of reward or of penalty in Hades, would be recalled to life by him, and be requited each according to his individual deeds. In opposition to the usurped dominion of the herods and the rule of the Romans, they stoutly upheld the theocracy and their country’s cause, and possessed great influence with the common people. According to Josephus they numbered more than 6000. They were bitter enemies of Jesus and his cause; and were in turn severely rebuked by him for their avarice, ambition, hollow reliance on outward works, and affection of piety in order to gain popularity.
s: Of Hebrew origin (compare \[[H6567](H6567)\]); a *separatist*, that is, exclusively *religious*; a *Pharisaean*, that is, Jewish sectary: - Pharisee.

d:
Felix = happy
**1.** a Roman procurator of Judea appointed by the emperor Claudius in A.D. 53. He ruled the province in a mean, cruel, and profligate manner. His period of office was full of troubles and seditions. Paul was brought before Felix at Caesarea. He was remanded in prison, and kept there two years in hopes of extorting money from him. Act 24:26, Act 24:27. At the end of that time Porcius Festus was appointed to supersede Felix, who, on his return to Rome, was accused by the Jews in Caesarea, and would have suffered the penalty due to his atrocities had not his brother Pallas prevailed with the emperor Nero to spare him. The wife of Felix was Drusilla, daughter of herod Agrippa I., who was his third wife and whom he persuaded to leave her husband and marry him.
s: Of Latin origin; *happy*; *Phelix* (that is, *Felix*), a Roman: - Felix.
